pick_six_2026.outlook:
Oregon is #2 in Game Grader over the past three-year average. Last year they finished #5 in Game Grader and #1 in opponent-adjusted yardage margin – and did so with a younger lineup. They are the only program to stack three straight top five recruiting classes and two top five transfer hauls.

Well, it’s 2026 and I am sticking to my call from back in July 2025. Oregon is my 2026 National Champion pick.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
In last year’s 2025 preview, I wrote that “Oregon is my pick to win the national championship … next year in 2026.”

Dan Lanning elevated the program’s recruiting profile to compete with the Dynasty Tier super-recruiters. And then he did it three years in a row. Oregon, Alabama, and Ohio State are the only programs to stack Top 5 recruiting classes in each of the past three years. Oregon took it a step further and signed two Top 5 transfer classes too.

On paper, it was an embarrassment of riches, but the 2025 two-deep was packed with first-time starters, true freshmen and sophomores. I still picked Oregon to finish third in the Big Ten and earn a Playoff at-large bid, but noted the real national title shot would come in 2026.

Five games in, Oregon looked ahead of schedule. They dealt Oklahoma State their worst loss in a century (69-3, +420 yardage), dominated the last scheduled Civil War with Oregon State (41-7, +440 yardage), and spoiled Penn State’s dream season and White Out crowd in double-overtime.

Then their nation-best home win streak was snapped at 18 games by the eventual Heisman winner and eventual national champion Indiana.

Oregon got right back on track with a +550 yardage win over Rutgers, quarterback Dante Moore led a game-winning drive in the final minute to hold off Iowa’s upset bid, and Oregon proceeded to win the rest of their games by double-digits.

That includes the first home playoff game in school history, a 51-34 win over James Madison, and then a Peach Bowl 23-0 shutout over #4 Texas Tech.

The semifinal rematch with Indiana was doomed from the start, as the Hoosiers took back the opening pass for a Pick Six and raced to a 35-7 halftime lead and eventual 56-22 win. Nothing was stopping Indiana in 2025. But Oregon’s 13-2 campaign with a young roster will pay dividends in 2026 and beyond.
pick_six_2026.offense:
It helps getting back a first-round NFL quarterback. Dante Moore surprised by returning to Oregon for a final year after passing for 3,565 yards, 30 touchdowns (10 picks), and the #5 QB Rating in Power 4. Moore is a polished passer, accurate with ball placement and a top five completion percentage (72%), and led the only offense to place in the top five of all three of my opponent- adjusted metrics: #5 overall, #4 passing, #4 rushing.

Moore returns as a Heisman favorite. Before he announced his return, former five-star and two- year Nebraska starter Dylan Raiola shocked Husker Nation and transferred to Eugene. Even after Moore’s announcement, Raiola decided to stay at Oregon and will get a developmental year before gunning for the 2027 job.

Noah Whittington graduated after leading with 829 yards. The running back room was complicated by a run of injuries, and a pair of Top200 true freshmen aced their auditions. Jordon Davison cashed in 15 touchdowns, Dierre Hill gained a nation-best 8.8 yards/carry, and these two are the lead pair for 2026. The phenom freshmen sent three other backs to the portal, so the third back will be incoming Top100 Tradarian Ball.

Injuries hit the receiver room too, with original WR1 Evan Stewart getting knocked out in fall camp, and starters Gary Bryant and Dakorien Moore both missing games. Both Stewart and Moore were five-stars and the #1 rated receiver in their classes, and both returned fully healthy this offseason to form an elite one-two punch. Top100 freshman Jeremiah McClellan stepped up last year and despite neither of the three being slot receivers, the staff said they will go “position-less” to get their playmakers on the field together. Add in two more five-stars – Jalen Lott and Gatlin Bair – plus a 900-yard receiver last year in Iverson Hooks (UAB) and this is a top unit.

Kenyon Sadiq earned first-team All-Big Ten and was the first tight end off the board in April’s NFL Draft. Oregon feels confident they’ll make it two-in-a-row with Jamari Johnson who surged over

the back half of the season and was matching Sadiq’s performance. A pair of Top50 prospects will battle for the second spot: Andrew Olesh (Penn State) and Kendre Harrison.

All five linemen earned All-Big Ten honors, and if it sounds repetitive, it is -- 12 offensive players were all-conference. The starting tackles Isaiah World and Alex Harkey and guard Emmanuel Pregnon are all gone but the other two return in center Iapani Laloulu and third-year starting guard Dave Iuli. The staff declined the transfer portal this cycle and doubled down on their recent blue- chip recruiting and development. At left tackle, four-star Fox Crader battles Top100 Ziyare Addison. At the other two spots, veterans Kawika Rogers and Michael Bennett will be challenged by four Top100 linemen.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Oregon was the only team with a Top 5 offense and a Top 5 defense per my opponent-adjusted metrics. Nine defenders earned All-Big Ten honors and eight starters are back.

The entire starting defensive line returned intact with Bear Alexander and A’Mauri Washington on the interior, and Matayo Uiagalelei and Teitum Tuioti off the ends. Uiagalelei led the Big Ten in sacks in the 2024 regular season, Tuioti has a high motor, and both are third-year starters. The front four is so strong, all four of their backups transferred out to other Power 4 schools with four- star grades. UNC starter D’Antre Robinson helped bolster the new two-deep, along with two five- stars Elijah Rushing and Anthony Jones, and two more Top200 guys in Nasir Wyatt and Aydin Breland.

Their leader in the middle Bryce Boettcher is gone after posting 136 tackles, an Oregon high since 1979. Jerry Mixon is a returning starter, and former Top100 Devon Jackson has sprinter speed and is poised to finally break out. The staff ignored the portal here, instead going with three four-star freshmen reserves.

As if this roster wasn’t stacked enough, the secondary is simply unbelievable. I don’t think I’ve seen this amount of raw firepower in any defensive backfield in Pick Six Previews’ history – at least in recruiting ranking terms. Four five-stars, four more Top50’s, and four more Top100s.

That softens the blow of losing All-American safety Dillon Thieneman. Brandon Finney and Ify Obidegwu both surged to starting roles as freshmen last year, Finney earned Freshman All-America honors, and they are joined by two more five-stars Na’eem Offord and Aaron Scott (Ohio State). Aaron Flowers is a returning starter at safety, they signed the #1 transfer safety, All-Big Ten Koi Perich (Minnesota), and have a pair of five-stars packing the two-deep in Trey McNutt and Jett Washington.

Good luck throwing the ball against Oregon the next few seasons.

pick_six_projections.notes: Ciancia's 2026 CFP projection: Big Ten champion (automatic bid to 12-team Playoff).

pick_six_2026.outlook:
11 more draft picks gone? No problem. The Ohio State machine rolls on into 2026 with a top five offense, multiple Heisman contenders, a veteran offensive line, and another round of five-stars moving up into starting roles.

This time around they added six Power 4 starting defenders from the transfer portal for extra firepower for Patricia’s second season calling the defense.

Ohio State will return to the Big Ten title game and then gear up for another Playoff run. If Sayin takes the next step
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
After winning the national title, Ohio State had 14 players drafted – four first- rounders – for the second-biggest draft class in modern history.

But here on the Dynasty Tier there are no “rebuilding” seasons, only reloads.

With five straight Top 5 recruiting classes, 2025 was simply just the next round of young five-stars stepping up into the starting lineup.

The defense clicked right away, with new coordinator Matt Patricia replacing Jim Knowles, and they suffocated preseason #1 Texas and their Heisman favorite Arch Manning to just seven points, stopping them twice inside the ten-yard line. Ohio State snapped Washington’s nation-best 22-game home win streak holding them to 1/11 on third downs and just 234 yards.

It took until the eighth game for Ohio State to allow a first-half touchdown, and they eventually finished with the #1 scoring defense in America.

Ryan Day kept the offensive scheme safe and conservative for first-time starter Julian Sayin but then took off the training wheels after the first month. Sayin was flawless. He ended up setting an NCAA regular season record with a 78.4% completion rate and earned a seat at the Heisman ceremony.

Day was able to get that final team goal off the checklist by finally beating Michigan, snapping their four-game series streak, and they did so with a 27-9 physical beatdown. “Nobody wants to win this game more than me,” said a relieved Day.

A perfect 12-0 regular season started to show some imperfections in the postseason. In the Big Ten title game and Playoff quarterfinal, Indiana and Miami combined for 10 sacks and held Ohio State to just 2.1 yards/carry. Sayin threw critical first-half interceptions, and was unable to create when the pocket broke down. Indiana won by 3, Miami won by 10, and Ohio State was bounced from the bracket on New Year’s Eve.

In April, the NFL’s 33rd Team sent another 11 players to the draft. They became the first school to have 7+ drafted in the first two rounds in consecutive drafts, and became the first since 1967 with four of the top 11 picks.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Most of the talent drain was on defense, and Ohio State returns their Heisman candidate quarterback, 1,000 yard running back, four offensive line starters, and superstar receiver Jeremiah Smith who many believe is the best overall player in college football.

Sayin finished his first season with 3,610 yards, 32 touchdowns and eight picks to win the Shaun Alexander Freshman of the Year award. His passing accuracy and ball placement are as good as anyone, but to unlock the final tier of his game, Sayin needs to create plays with his legs in crunch time – whether it be pocket elusiveness to extend the play, or tucking the ball on a critical third-and-medium. Basically the Craig Krenzel type plays that don’t show up on the stat sheet, but eventually win national titles.

Bo Jackson is back after his surprise 1,000-yard freshman season, and the offense looks to add more explosiveness to the run game (#73). They may have found lightning in a bottle with incoming Top100 athlete Legend Bey who Day has already compared to Tyreek Hill and Buckeye great Curtis Samuel. Bey will be the do-it-all from the slot, H-back, etc.

Since 2019, Ohio State has featured at least two future first-round picks in their receiver room. Brian Hartline built a conveyor belt of five-stars and 2025 was no different with Smith earning unanimous All- America honors with 1,243 yards and 12 touchdowns. Carnell Tate was selected fourth overall. Smith is back for a final season and is on pace to break all school receiving records, and five-star Brandon Inniss also returns to the starting trio. A pair of five-stars Mylan Graham and Quincy Porter both transferred out to Notre Dame, likely due to the breakout of five-star Chris Henry who surged all the way to the #2 role in spring and will be the beneficiary of Smith’s double-teams. Devin McCuin (UTSA) earned All-AAC last year with 65 catches and 726 yards, and another freshman Brock Boyd drew big spring reviews.

Both All-Big Ten tight ends Max Klare and Will Kacmarek are gone, but the staff signed another all- leaguer in Hunter Welcing (Northwestern). Mason Williams (Ohio) was All-MAC, but the spring hero was Top200 Nate Roberts.

The offensive line was strong in the regular season, had its pinnacle performance against Michigan, but then struggled against the elite lines of Indiana and Miami. Four starters are back, all four earned All- Big Ten honors, and their 91 combined starts make this one of the most veteran lines in America: tackles Austin Siereveld and Phillip Daniels, guard Luke Montgomery, and center Carson Hinzman. Siereveld did not allow a single sack all year and is their best shot at an All-America season. Tegra Tshabola transferred out to Kentucky after losing his starting job. A trio of former Top200 prospects will battle to be the fifth starter – Joshua Padilla, Gabe VanSickle, and spring hero Ian Moore.
pick_six_2026.defense:
The “mad scientist” Patricia built the best defense of the entire College Football Playoff era. Ohio State allowed just 9.3 points/game, 219 yards/game, which were both Playoff era bests (2014-2025). 12 defenders earned All-Big Ten, three were unanimous All-Americans, and three were drafted in the first 11 picks.

Kayden McDonald was a force in the middle, posting a productive stat line for a defensive tackle (65 tackles, 9 for loss, 3 sacks), Caden Curry led with 11 sacks and 16.5 tackles-for-loss, and Tywone Malone earned the other starting tackle spot. All three are gone, and end Kenyatta Jackson is the only returning starter on the line. Ohio State added two starters off the Alabama line – tackle James Smith and end Qua Russaw – and both were former five-star recruits who earned four-star transfer grades. They signed another former Top100 starter John Walker (UCF), and still have five-star Eddrick Houston ready for a breakout season at tackle.

Even the greatest reloading programs would struggle here. Ohio State has to replace two All-American, first-round linebackers in Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles. Payton Pierce was their third backer and he steps into the top role, the staff signed Wisconsin starter Christian Alliegro who was ranked the #3 linebacker transfer this cycle, and then a trio of blue-chippers add to the position battle. Riley Pettijohn and TJ Alford were both Top100’s from the 2025 class, five-star Cincere Johnson was the #1 linebacker of 2026, and spring reports mention that Alford was the early standout.

Ohio State has as strong a claim as anyone to the “Defensive Back U” title, and Caleb Downs leaves as one of their best safeties of all-time along with Mike Doss and Jack Tatum. Jaylen McClain returns at the other safety spot with star potential, and the staff signed a pair of All-ACC safeties in Earl Little (Florida State) and Terry Moore (Duke). They added more firepower with five-star Jay Timmons and Top100 Blaine Bradford. Davison Igbinosun heads to the pros but Jermaine Mathews returns at one corner, and five-star Devin Sanchez is poised to be yet another Buckeye great.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
The U came alive in the Playoff spotlight and accelerated Cristobal’s program build. I projected Playoff bids in 2024 and 2025 – the ’24 team was one of the last teams out, ’25 was the final team in – and a college football giant is awakening.

It seems odd, since they still haven’t won the conference title game, but Miami is the new ACC dynasty program. The talent that Cristobal has stockpiled is head and shoulders above the rest of the league and they are my pick to win the ACC, and make another Playoff run in January.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Behind their nation-best lines of scrimmage, and one of the most improved defenses, Miami closed out another 10-2 regular season. They swept their in-state rivals again, and then closed with four wins by an average of 28 points/game.

Their most important win actually came way back in the opener. Miami’s pass rush finished off a physical 27-24 win over Notre Dame and they snapped their eight-year drought against Top 10 opponents.

In 2024, Miami’s 10-2 record landed them just outside the Playoff field. This time 10- 2 was enough, due to their critical head-to-head win over the other final 10-2 team in question: Notre Dame.

It was the correct decision. “Let us never, ever devalue the importance of head-to- head competition, please,” said head coach Mario Cristobal.

Miami found another gear in the postseason. They went into Kyle Field and beat Texas A&M 10-3 behind a breakout performance by running back Mark Fletcher and a game- sealing pick in the endzone by Bryce Fitzgerald.

Another interception flipped the Cotton Bowl, as Keionte Scott jumped a screen pass and took back a Pick Six 72 yards as Miami knocked out the defending champs Ohio State – 2002 payback.

Miami got more late-game heroics from the offense in the semifinal as freshman phenom Malachi Toney zig-zagged through the Ole Miss defense for a score. Then veteran Carson Beck scrambled in for the game-winner in the final seconds.

Miami returned to the national title stage for the first time in a generation, and like the old days, they got to play for it on their home turf. Ultimately, Indiana made two critical fourth-down plays – the back shoulder fade to Charlie Becker, and a Heisman-tier scramble by Fernando Mendoza – and Miami fell six points short of their sixth ring.

As Cristobal put it: we say, ‘The U is Here,’ we are here right now.

Despite falling a few plays short, the postseason run accelerated Cristobal’s program build, and all the elite talent acquisition is paying dividends.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Beck went pro, so the staff went back for a third-straight transfer quarterback. They hit home runs with Cam Ward and Beck, and this round should be no different.

Darian Mensah led Duke to a rare ACC title with his 3,973 passing yards, 35 touchdowns, and high 67% completion rate. He was graded a Top 5 transfer quarterback this cycle and all season long he showed off both touch and arm strength, and a gunslinger attitude.

Mensah had the most downfield pass attempts in Power 4 last year. Their quarterback selection addresses one of the only weaknesses of the offense last year: a lack of downfield, vertical shots in the pass game.

Miami was one of five Power 4 offenses to feature a 3,000-yard passer, 1,000-yard rusher, and 1,000-yard receiver. Duke was one of the others, and Mensah brought his receiver Cooper Barkate with him to join Miami’s workhorse back Fletcher, and highlight-reel Toney.

Fletcher found an extra gear in the Playoffs, averaging 126 rushing yards/game which was nearly double his regular season average. Marty Brown also returns, plus another round of Top200 blue-chippers in Jordan Lyle and Girard Pringle.

The receiver room could be the nation’s best. Toney is a no-brainer All-America pick after breaking Miami’s school records for receptions (109) and yards (1,211) as a true freshman. Barkate put up 1,106 yards for Duke last year, earned All-ACC, and was ranked a Top 10 transfer receiver this cycle. Toney is the best screen pass receiver, while Barkate actually led the nation in the 10-19 yard intermediate range last year. The staff signed four-star transfers Vandrevius Jacobs (South Carolina) and Cam Vaughn (West Virginia) who were Power 4 starters and combined for 1,089 yards last year.

The spring surprise was sophomore Joshua Moore’s surge up the depth chart to a starting role. The 6’4, 220-pound former Top100 moved ahead of the veteran transfers. Plus, another round of Top100’s are incoming from the 2026 class: Milan Parris and Somourian Wingo.

The tight end room had one of its lowest outputs in decades last year. Elija Lofton is a returning starter and more top recruits join the rotation with four-star Luka Gilbert and Top100 Gavin Mueller.

Cristobal’s program was built intentionally from the inside out, with attention on the lines of scrimmage. He and ace line coach Alex Mirabal built one of the nation’s best last year. Four linemen earned All-ACC honors, all four are gone, and anchor Francis Mauigoa was drafted in the first round.

Miami signed the #1 offensive lineman this cycle Jackson Cantwell and he is projected to start at left tackle right away. Cristobal has started true freshmen successfully in the past like Penei Sewell and Mauigoa. Another five-star Samson Okunlola is next to him at left guard, oft-injured Ryan Rodriguez takes over at center, and veteran Matthew McCoy shifted out to right tackle. The final guard spot is a battle between four-star Max Buchanan and Top100 SJ Alofaituli who are both second-years.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Cristobal made one of the best coordinator hires of the entire 2025 cycle with Corey Hetherman here on defense. Hetherman inherited a below-average unit and with a more aggressive scheme, and an elite pass rush, vaulted Miami up to #4 in my opponent-adjusted number.

Six starters are gone, including two first-round draft picks off the edges. Rueben Bain and Akheem Mesidor were game-wreckers and combined for an insane 150 quarterback pressures, 33 tackles for loss, and 22 sacks. Normally that loss of star power would be enough to sink the defense, but Miami is absolutely stacked in the trenches. Of the eight linemen in the two-deep, four are five-stars, three more are Top200’s, and the other is All-ACC tackle Ahmad Moten.

Former five-star tackle Justin Scott (Saint Ignatius) is poised for an All-ACC season, Keona Davis (Nebraska) was a full-year starter, and Jarquez Carter (Ohio State) was Top200 in the 2025 class. At end, five-stars Armondo Blount and Marquise Lightfoot are joined by the nation’s #2 transfer edge Damon Wilson (Missouri) who posted 10 sacks last year.

Wesley Bissainthe is gone but All-ACC Mo Toure was granted an eighth college season and is the leader in the middle. Chase Smith enters his sixth season and

moved up into a starting role in spring.

The secondary loses nickelback Scott and safety Jakobe Thomas, but the room is overflowing with talent. All four of the starting corners are back: Xavier Lucas, OJ Frederique, Damari Brown, and Ethan O’Connor. The staff signed four- star transfer Omar Thornton who started for Boston College last year and showed off excellent open-field tackling and got ACC honorable mention. Zechariah Poyser is back at safety, then three more Top100s pack the room with playoff hero Fitzgerald and incoming freshmen JJ Dunnigan and Camdin Portis.

pick_six_projections.notes: Ciancia's 2026 CFP projection: ACC champion (automatic bid to 12-team Playoff).

pick_six_2026.outlook:
After missing the bracket by one spot, Notre Dame has a chance for redemption in 2026. They get virtually the same team back – minus their first-round running backs – and even get a rematch shot at Miami.

This is definitely a top five defense in America, the offensive line is elite again, and Freeman continues to upgrade the program’s talent level. Oh, and they have a legit Heisman contender under center in CJ Carr.

The schedule is favorable as they draw only three of my Top 25 teams (Miami, SMU, and @ BYU), plus the bottom four ACC teams, and two of the bottom three from the Big Ten. Notre Dame will return to the Playoff as serious National Title contenders.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Fresh off a national title appearance, Notre Dame lost a physical battle at Miami, then lost again in a wild shootout against Texas A&M thanks in part to a botched extra point hold. 0-2 by a combined four points.

The defense rounded into form, new starting quarterback CJ Carr was extremely efficient, and they leaned on their best feature: a running back pair of eventual first-round picks.

Jeremiyah Love was a weekly highlight reel, like his 94-yarder to seal the Boston College game, or his video-game spin move against Pittsburgh, and he ran all the way to the Heisman ceremony. His co-star Jadarian Price took back a kickoff 100 yards for a touchdown to help seal the USC win.

After the 0-2 start, Notre Dame dominated the remainder of their schedule. They won their final ten games, all by double-digits, with an average margin of 30 points/game and +190 yardage/game.

The College Football Playoff committee placed Notre Dame at #11, but due to their bylaw granting auto-bids to the best five conference winners (two non-AQ champs due to five-loss Duke), the Irish missed the bracket by one spot.

Athletic director Pete Bevacqua went on a 48-hour tirade across multiple channels and shows. “There is no explanation that could possibly be given to explain the outcome.”

Here’s an explanation: Notre Dame played two Playoff teams and lost both times. The final spot came down to 10-2 Miami and 10-2 Notre Dame. Miami won when they played each other.

Notre Dame then opted out of bowl season altogether. Iowa State and Kansas State opted out of bowl seasons due to coach transitions that sent 40+ players into the portal. Not the case here.

Separating “deserving resume” from “power ratings,” there is no doubting that Notre Dame was Playoff-caliber in the latter. My opponent-adjusted Game Grader placed Notre Dame #4.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Love and Price ended up as Notre Dame’s second 2,000-yard pair of backs since the 1960s joining Jerome Bettis and Reggie Brooks (1992). Love earned unanimous All-America honors, Price got honors as a kick returner, and both were drafted in the first round.

They were the engine of one of the nation’s best offenses of 2025. Notre Dame ranked in the top five

in scoring with 42 points/game, yards/carry (5.7), QB Rating, and both explosive rushing and passing.

Carr turned in a stellar first year as the starter, ranked #6 in QB Rating, #3 in yards/attempt, and earned Freshman All-America honors. He’s got a strong deep ball, nice touch on sideline throws, and quickly took control of the offense as the season went on. When needed, he can tuck the ball and fall forward for key yardage.

Love and Price will be missed as program legends. Aneyas Williams is the new lead back, and had a role in the 2024 playoff run with six touches/game and a high 7.6 per/carry career average.

The offensive line was a strength as usual here, ranking #31 in OL Run Push and #12 in pass protection. Billy Schrauth was drafted and Aamil Wagner graduated, but the other three starters are back. The staff is shifting around their roles, but Anthonie Knapp is a legit All-America contender at guard, Ashton Craig is recovering from an injury at center, and 6’7 Guerby Lambert shifted to tackle. They hope to get injured Charles Jagusah back healthy in time for the season, but if not, Sullivan Absher has plenty of experience. The newcomer is redshirt freshman, former five-star Will Black who won the starting job at left tackle. This should be another elite unit for ace offensive line coach Joe Rudolph.

From spring practice reports, it appears to be an athletic, agile line that may run more outside zone than last year.

One of the most dominant streaks in college football survived another year. Every Notre Dame starting tight end since 2005 was eventually drafted and Eli Raridon continued the lineage. Raridon ranked in the Top 15 of Power 4 with 482 receiving yards, but the 2026 pair – Cooper Flanagan and James Flanigan -- are stronger in run blocking. Notre Dame signed the #1 tight end recruit this cycle in five-star Ian Premer (Great Bend, KS).

Notre Dame loses their reliable slot receiver Will Pauling and 6’4 big-frame Malachi Fields but receiving leader Jordan Faison is back. Faison had a breakthrough 2025 and quit lacrosse to focus fully on his final season. The staff needed to pull in some transfers here, and there is no better spot than Brian Hartline’s NFL conveyor belt in Columbus. Notre Dame signed two Ohio State receivers, Mylan Graham and Quincy Porter, and both are former five-star recruits who were stuck in a crowded room. Graham will start in the slot, Porter fills in for Fields’ role, and Jaden Greathouse is finally healthy.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Chris Ash was catching some heat in September after the 0-2 start, and another defensive breakdown against lowly Purdue. But then his defense rounded into form and ended up as one of the most dominant units nationally. Notre Dame finished #6 overall in my opponent-adjusted metric -- #3 passing, #8 rushing – and was elite in every area.

Ash is just getting started, too. 10 starters returned, plus five four-star transfers pack the two-deep.

Notre Dame was stout at the point of attack, and Jason Onye and Elijah Hughes return from their five-man tackle rotation. The staff signed All-ACC Francis Brewu (Pittsburgh) and Tionne Gray (Oregon) who were both ranked as top five transfer defensive tackles. Both starting ends return with future NFL-er Boubacar Traore and former five-star Bryce Young. Another former five-star Keon Keeley (Alabama) transferred in.

The full four-man linebacker core returns and all four placed within the team’s top six in tackles- for-loss. Drayk Bowen was named a team captain, Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa has high NFL grades, while Jaiden Ausberry and Jaylen Sneed are solid traditional inside backers.

Leonard Moore earned unanimous All-America honors and is arguably the best overall player in the nation. He returns as a lockdown corner, his co-starter Christian Gray shifted over to the nickel spot, while a new trio battles of the second corner

spot. All three are former Top200 prospects: Dallas Golden, Mark Zackery, and Jayden Sanders (Michigan).

Last year they had to replace All-American Xavier Watts and the secondary took a few games to step up. Redshirt freshman Tae Johnson took the starting job from Jalen Stroman. Johnson and Adon Shuler (27 career starts) are both back, plus Luke Talich is solid in sub-packages like red zone or two-minute drill.

pick_six_projections.notes: Ciancia's 2026 CFP projection: at-large bid, projected to host USC in first round.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Georgia won the SEC last year with the league’s #1 rank in Game Grader, they return 14 starters, and the two-deep is overflowing with former five-stars. They will be back in Atlanta to defend their crown and benefit from the SEC’s easiest schedule as the only team to face only three of the top eight.

Georgia is my pick to win the SEC title, but the Dynasty-Tier is graded on their performance in January. Kirby Smart has a championship-caliber defense yet again, but to make a deep Playoff run he’ll need some of those five-star receiver recruits to rise up as game-changers.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
In their SEC opener, Georgia trailed Tennessee by eight in the final minutes when Gunner Stockton hit London Humphreys on a 28-yard fade – on a do-or-die fourth down – for a touchdown. Georgia converted the two-pointer and eventually survived in overtime.

Their second-half comeback and last-minute resiliency wound up being the theme of the 2025 season.

Georgia trailed in seven of their eight SEC games, but still went 7-1 in league play. The goal-line fumble forced by CJ Allen saved the Auburn game, the defense suffocated Ole Miss in the fourth quarter, and against Florida it was a Chauncey Bowens 36-yard burst that clinched another one.

In total, four were fourth-quarter comeback wins.

“I don’t write the scripts,” joked head coach Kirby Smart.

Their lone loss was to Alabama, when the Crimson Tide came into Athens and snapped their nation-best 33-game home win streak. Georgia got another shot at them in the SEC title and dominated the rematch, 28-7, to clinch the program’s fourth SEC title in five years.

Georgia earned a first-round bye, but just like 2024, they were bounced in the quarterfinals. Trinidad Chambliss made countless highlight reel plays for Ole Miss, who seemed to rally internally after the Lane Kiffin drama.

On the Dynasty Tier, it is national title or bust. After consecutive crowns in 2021 and 2022, Georgia now has a three-year title drought – and Playoff win drought – heading into 2026.

They return 14 starters, and the newcomers to the starting lineup and two-deep are most likely five- stars or Top100 blue-chippers. Georgia’s last four recruiting classes: #2, #1, #2, #6. On top of that, they signed seven more four-star transfers to post the #2 transfer class on a per-player average.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Stockton thrived in his first full-year as the starter. He earned third-team All-SEC after passing for 2,894 yards, 24 touchdowns (just 5 picks) with another 462 yards and 10 scores on the ground. He ranked fourth in QB Rating within the SEC and is now a proven, championship-caliber quarterback.

Georgia’s running back pair returns and both Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens took on the lead role at various points in the season. Frazier overcame his fumble issue with zero over the final 11 games. He led with 947 yards (5.5 per carry) and Bowens added 526 (5.1). Short-yardage bowling ball Josh McCray graduated but the staff found an SEC replacement in Dante Dowdell (Kentucky).

Their best offensive weapon Zachariah Branch went to the pros, and three more graduated: Colbie Young, Dillon Bell, and Noah Thomas. That means only one of their top five receivers returns with London Humphreys back on the outside. The staff signed a rising star in 6’3 Isiah Canion (Georgia Tech) who earned a four-star transfer grade after posting 480 yards and a high 14.6 per-catch average last season. Most schools would have added another round of transfers, but Georgia is confident in their elite recruiting here. Six more four-stars pack the rotation with five-star Talyn Taylor and Top100 CJ Wiley as the most likely breakout candidates. Kaiden Prothro is a 6’6 Top50 true freshman who was a spring hero.

Georgia also loses starting tight end Oscar Delp but the room remains packed with talent. Co-starter Lawson Luckie is back as a proven receiving threat, especially in the red zone, and he had a three- touchdown game in the first Ole Miss matchup. Jaden Reddell brings the speed, 6’7 Elyiss Williams is the blocker, and Ethan Barbour is an H-back, fullback type.

Similar to the wide receiver room, the staff avoided the transfer portal and doubled down on their stockpile of blue-chip offensive linemen. Monroe Freeling was a first-round draft pick, guard Micah Morris was also drafted, but the other three starters return. Drew Bobo earned second-team All-SEC at center, Earnest Greene excelled at tackle, and guard Dontrell Glover was named a Freshman All- American.

The open tackle spot will likely be former Top100 Juan Gaston, who earned some starts as a true freshman and will get a second-year bonus this fall. He’ll be challenged in fall camp by incoming five-star Ekene

Ogboko and Smart has shown he’s willing to play true freshmen linemen recently. The open guard spot was a battle between two Top100’s Daniel Calhoun and Michael Uini until true freshman Zykie Helton emerged as a spring hero.

For Georgia to make a deeper Playoff run, the offensive line needs to get a more consistent, Top 25 run push. The past two lines have ranked #65 and #66 in my OL Run Push stat.
pick_six_2026.defense:
After Smart’s transition season in 2016, his next nine defenses were all Top 25 units in my opponent- adjusted rankings. Only Alabama and Notre Dame can match that streak.

The 2025 defense finished #12 and was especially stout against the run holding opponents to just 82 rushing yards/game (#4) and 2.9 per carry (#8).

Eight starters are back, along with the vast majority of the two-deep which holds more weight here because no other defense rotates their players more.

In the trenches, Christen Miller went pro but the other eight linemen in the three-deep are all back. Elijah Griffin and Jordan Hall are at defensive tackle, Xzavier McLeod and Nnamdi Ogboko rotate at nose tackle, while Gabe Harris and Joseph Jonah-Ajonye are at end. Georgia signed the #1 edge recruit of 2025 Isaiah Gibson, meaning this room packs four five-stars and four more former Top100’s.

Brian Hartline had his conveyor belt of five-star receivers at Ohio State, but defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann has the linebacker equivalent here. First-team All-SEC CJ Allen went pro, but the three 2026 starters are all former five-stars. Raylen Wilson is back after a dominant 2025, Chris Cole returns at inside backer, and Justin Williams is the third backer.

Quintavius Johnson is a returning starter at the “Jack” position, an outside backer/end hybrid, and the staff signed the #4 ranked transfer edge Amaris Williams (Auburn) but he suffered a spring ACL injury.

Four starters are back in the secondary with cornerback Daylen Everette as the lone departure. Ellis Robinson was ranked the #1 cornerback of the 2024 class and he played like it, earning FWAA Freshman of the Year. Top100 DeMello Jones will battle Gentry Williams (Oklahoma) at the other corner spot.

KJ Bolden returns at safety after earning second-team All-SEC and last year Rasean Dinkins surged up the depth chart as a true freshman. Zion Branch also returns, plus the staff signed two four-star transfers in All-AAC ballhawk Ja’Marley Riddle (East Carolina) and three-year starter Khalil Barnes (Clemson). That’s a ton of firepower to fill out the secondary.

pick_six_projections.notes: Ciancia's 2026 CFP projection: SEC champion (automatic bid to 12-team Playoff).

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Oklahoma has a championship-caliber defense again. The passing attack will be improved thanks to two key transfer additions at receiver, a second-year coordinator bonus, and a healthy Mateer.

Oklahoma will return to the Playoff in 2026, and they are my pick to play Georgia in the SEC title game.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Losing seasons are rare at Oklahoma. Before Brent Venables was hired, they only suffered five losing seasons in the 75 years since WWII.

Then Venables posted two losing seasons in three years.

In 2025 they were dealt arguably the toughest schedule in the nation, and with the pressure rising, Venables delivered.

He built an elite, Top 5 defense that absolutely suffocated opponents. Oklahoma forced a negative play – sack or tackle-for-loss – on 15% of snaps which was by far the #1 mark nationally. They sacked Auburn nine times, posted six straight 10+ TFL games, and the defense led the way in five ranked wins.

Two plays shifted the season from average to Playoff-caliber. Against Tennessee, All-American R Mason Thomas took a fumble back 71 yards for the school-record longest scoop-and-score. The next week, All-SEC Eli Bowen scored an 87-yard Pick Six to flip the Alabama win.

The offense did just enough to complement Venables’ elite defense, like in the final few minutes of the season when John Mateer hit Isaiah Sategna on a 58-yard score to beat LSU 17-13 and secure Oklahoma’s first Playoff

bid since 2019.

Though the first-round rematch with Alabama went the wrong way, the 10-win season with half against ranked teams, was a statement season.

Oklahoma returns 14 starters, seven on each side, and gets a second-year coordinator bonus on offense. Venables landed the breakthrough season, and 2026 presents a shot to prove staying power in the SEC.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Last offseason Venables hired rising-star coordinator Ben Arbuckle to install his Air Raid offense that shattered records at Western Kentucky and Washington State. It was a package deal too, with Arbuckle bringing his quarterback Mateer who led FBS with 44 total touchdowns in 2024.

It simply didn’t click in 2025. Maybe it was the transition year and new scheme installation, or the freshman-filled offensive line, or Mateer’s hand injury. But while the defense ranked #3 in my opponent-adjusted metric, the offense was just #50 of 68 Power 4.

Before Mateer hurt his hand in the Auburn game, Oklahoma’s opponent-adjusted passing was #42, but post-injury it fell slightly to #52 of 68. Mateer placed 13th in the SEC in QB Rating with 14 touchdown passes and 11 picks.

This offseason Mateer focused on fixing his mechanics and footwork – less sidearm, off-balance throws – and appeared improved throughout spring ball. Stats aside, he always has that uncanny playmaking ability and should get an efficiency boost in his second SEC season.

The run game was “pathetic” in Venables’ words. The 3.5 yards/carry was Oklahoma’s worst since 2010 and the 118 yards/game was their worst since 1999. He hired ace running backs coach Deland McCullough who had just coached Heisman finalists in back-to-back years with Ashton Jeanty and Jeremiyah Love. Tory Blaylock led with 480 yards as a true freshman, Xavier Robinson added 421 and both return for 2026.

The offensive line was part of the issue, as the extremely young unit ranked in the national bottom ten of my OL Run Push metric (#124). Three freshmen moved up the depth chart to combine for 24 starts last year. Michael Fasusi started all year as a true freshman five-star, while Top100 Ryan Fodje and Eddy Pierre-Louis started six each. Those young reps and starts should pay dividends with a second-year bonus here in 2026. Starting center Jake Maikkula also returns, and while they do lose an All-SEC draft pick in Febechi Nwaiwu, the staff signed two-year Arkansas starter E’Marion Harris who earned a four-star transfer billing. Six upperclassmen transferred out to other Power 4 rosters, but all were three-star transfers who fell behind the youngsters on the depth chart.

Sategna earned first-team All-SEC after placing in the league’s top three in receiving yards and touchdowns. He returns in the slot, and while their next three departed, the staff landed two highly- touted Power 4 starters through the portal. 6’3 Parker Livingstone (Texas) was in the starting rotation as a freshman and posted an explosive 17.8 per-catch average good for fourth in the SEC. Trell Harris

(Virginia) earned All-ACC with a productive 59 catches for 847 yards last year. It’s already a proven starting trio, but Mackenzie Alleyne (Washington State) emerged as a spring hero and has past experience in Arbuckle’s offense.

The tight end room is a total rebuild after All-SEC Jaren Kanak went pro. The converted linebacker Kanak was solid but now the staff added in a pair of four-star transfers, plus Hall-of-Famer Jason Witten to coach the position. Hayden Hansen (Florida) was a three-year starter and ranked second in the SEC with 44 catches last year. Hansen was ranked the #2 transfer tight end this cycle, and Jack Van Dorselaer was a four-star in the 2025 class. They showed off more 12 personnel (one back, two tight ends) in spring.
pick_six_2026.defense:
When he took over, Oklahoma had posted six straight below-average defenses. Venables’ third defense ranked #10 in my opponent-adjusted number. His fourth defense was a masterpiece.

Oklahoma led the nation in sacks/game and TFL/game, ranked 4th in yards/play, and 7th in scoring defense. Aside from the stat sheet, the defense made the game-winning plays against Tennessee and Alabama to help punch their Playoff ticket.

The elite depth in the trenches stood out -- they rotated eight-deep and never missed a beat.

Half of that defensive line group returns, and in total seven starting defenders are back. That includes four All-SEC stars and two All-Freshmen.

Thomas and Gracen Halton were drafted, but All-SEC Taylor Wein returns after leading with seven sacks, 15 TFL, and 35 QB pressures off the edge. Wein is poised for an All-America campaign and at the other end spot former five-star Adepoju Adebawore and Top200 Danny Okoye are the next duo up. Oklahoma also signed a Top100 prospect in Jake Kreul. At the tackle spots, five-star David Stone has been dominant, and Jayden Jackson earned Freshman All-America in 2024. Another Top200 pair rounds out the two- deep: Nigel Smith and Trent Wilson.

Owen Heinecke got a bonus year of eligibility, so Oklahoma returns its top two tacklers at linebacker. Heinecke and Kip Lewis combined for 22.5 tackles-for-loss, and while their backups transferred out, Oklahoma signed four-star Cole Sullivan (Michigan) who started the final three games last year and was looking like a Michigan rising star.

The elite corner duo returns with All-SEC Eli Bowen paired with SEC All-Freshman Courtland Guillory, plus the third corner is another blue-chipper in Top100 Jacobe Johnson. Peyton Bowen is yet another all-leaguer at safety, Michael Boganowski is a hard hitter in run support, and Reggie Powers is their hybrid “cheetah” role.

It’s also worth noting that Oklahoma returns the league’s top punter Grayson Miller and Lou Groza winner Tate Sandell who hit eight 50+ yarders that helped flip close games.

pick_six_projections.notes: Ciancia's 2026 CFP projection: at-large bid, projected to host Boise State in first round.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Texas went all-in this offseason with a top five transfer haul that packed in 10 Power 4 starters to a roster already overflowing with five-star talent. They are also in the top five in high school recruiting average, and are #4 in projected NFL Draft picks.

Like most quarterbacks, Manning will get a second-year boost – he already showed improvement as the 2025 season
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Fresh off consecutive Playoff runs, Texas entered 2025 as the preseason AP #1 team for the first time in school history. They also had the preseason Heisman favorite at quarterback with five-star super-recruit Arch Manning.

The hype was short-lived as they ran into a brick wall in the opener. #3 Ohio State stuffed Texas twice inside the 10 yard-line and took away Manning’s deep ball. The 14-7 loss didn’t change any team goals, but their SEC opener loss to unranked Florida did. Manning was sacked six times, missed two wide-open touchdown throws, and the running backs were held to 15 yards rushing.

Ryan Niblett saved the season with game-changing punt returns in three straight games, the 23-6 win over Oklahoma, and then overtime-survival wins against Kentucky and Mississippi State. Texas was able to beat three Top 10 teams – Oklahoma, Vanderbilt, Texas A&M – to get back into the Playoff hunt, but a total meltdown in the fourth quarter against Georgia dealt them an eliminating third loss.

With the bowl win, Steve Sarkisian got Texas to 10+ wins in three consecutive seasons for the first time here since 2009. But with such high preseason expectations, and nation-leading roster funding, a Playoff miss makes it a missed opportunity.

After finishing #4 and #3 in Game Grader the previous two seasons, Texas slid down to #22 in 2025 for their lowest rank since Sarkisian’s debut in 2021.

To turn the momentum back around, Sarkisian made a coordinator switch on defense, and then Texas reloaded with the #3 transfer haul this cycle. This class brings an instant boost of talent to offensive skill positions and in total adds an incredible 10 Power 4 starters into the program.

At Texas, the standard is always Playoff or Bust, but that is even more true after a hiatus.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Sometimes the national media locks in on a topic and it drives extreme viewpoints. The preseason hype for Manning was clearly too high, but conversely the negative overreactions in September went too far the other way. Manning’s 2025 season was common: a first-time starting quarterback had some growing pains and then showed clear improvements as the season progressed.

He was booed after 10 straight incompletions against UTEP but then in the season-finale he out- dueled a Heisman contender and ruined A&M’s perfect season.

My opponent-adjusted passing stats show the in-season development. Texas ranked #42 of 68 Power 4 over the first half of the season, but rose to #15 over the final six games. Manning threw for 3,163 yards, 26 touchdowns and just seven picks, and also added 399 rushing yards and 10 scores on the ground – and he even caught one against Arkansas.

Texas bolstered the skill positions around him and they enter 2026 with a top running back duo and arguably the best receiver room.

The top three running backs all transferred out, but Texas signed the #3 and #6 ranked transfers and both were all-conference in 2025. Hollywood Smothers (NC State) led the ACC with 85 yards/game and Raleek Brown (Arizona State) has been described by coaches as a “Tasmanian Devil, a bowling ball, and a pitbull.” Both backs are explosive, with high 6.0 yard/carry averages last year.

The receiver room struggled with dropped passes and lead target Ryan Wingo was often double-teamed. The other two starters DeAndre Moore (Colorado) and Parker Livingstone (Oklahoma) transferred out but Texas signed the nation’s #1 receiver Cam Coleman (Auburn). Wingo and Coleman are both former five-stars, and Coleman is a future first-round draft pick who wins 50/50 balls and adds a red zone boost. Defenses can’t double-team them both. Emmett Mosley returns in the slot and is joined by Wake Forest starter Sterling Berkhalter and former Top100 Daylan McCutcheon. As if that wasn’t enough, another pair of five-star freshmen pack the rotation: Kaliq Lockett and Jermaine Bishop.

Jack Endries went pro, but the staff signed Michigan State starting tight end Michael Masunas, who earned four-star transfer grades, to battle Top100 Nick Townsend.

The limiting factor on offense, and maybe the overall 2026 team, is their offensive line development. Last year they failed to get consistent rushing production, ranking #82 in my OL Run Push for the second straight year. They broke down in pass protection in their losses.

Their best lineman, All-SEC DJ Campbell was drafted but three starters return. Left tackle Trevor Goosby is drawing high draft projections himself and should get All-America hype. Connor Robertson is back at center, and Brandon Baker is shifting from tackle to guard. Two incoming transfers fill out the other two spots with FBS veteran Laurence Seymore (Western Kentucky) at left guard and Wake Forest starter Melvin Siani – who allowed zero sacks on 900 snaps last year – at right tackle.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Texas posted a Top 10 overall defense in my opponent-adjusted metric, but they struggled against the pass and Sarkisian decided to make a change. He fired coordinator Pete Kwiatkowski and hired Will Muschamp, a top defensive mind who has had more success as a coordinator than a head coach. Muschamp aka “Coach Boom” has been with the Georgia program the past five years as an analyst and co-coordinator.

Muschamp led the defense here for three years from 2008-2010 and during that span Texas led the nation in sacks and placed in the top ten of all major stat categories. The 2009 team made it all the way to the national title.

Three starters return along the defensive line with All-SEC Colin Simmons as the headliner. Simmons led the conference with 12 sacks and is a sure-fire All-America pick for 2026. Muschamp mentioned moving Simmons around in various spots and roles to confuse offenses. At the other end Lance Jackson returns after an SEC All-Freshman debut. Muschamp likes huge space-eating nose tackles to control two gaps, and he’s got two giants here with 330-pounder Maraad Watson and Arkansas starter Ian Geffrard who checks in at 6’5 380. Hero Kanu and Alex January are both back at the other tackle spot.

All-American linebacker Anthony Hill went pro, starter Liona Lefau transferred out, but Ty’Anthony Smith is the next rising star. Brad Spence is another returning starter though incoming Top100 Kosi Okpala could earn reps right away. The staff signed two four-star transfers who were Power 4 starters last year: Justin Cryer (Florida State) and Rasheem Biles (Pittsburgh) who is a two-time All-ACC selection with three Pick Sixes the past two years.

The secondary needs the most improvement after falling from elite (#2) in 2024 down to average last year (#42) in opponent QB Rating. Both All-SEC picks are gone with corner Malik Muhammad and captain Michael Taaffe both getting drafted. Texas has a pair of five-stars as projected starters at corner with returning starter Kobe Black and redshirt freshman Kade Phillips – plus they added Bo Mascoe (Rutgers) who has shown strong coverage skills in the Big Ten.

Top100 Graceson Littleton impressed as a true freshman and will start at nickel, Jelani McDonald should get All-SEC hype, and a pair of five-stars – Derek Williams and Xavier Filsaime – battle at the other safety spot.

pick_six_projections.notes: Ciancia's 2026 CFP projection: at-large bid, projected first-round game at Texas Tech.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Texas Tech’s transfer portal dominance translated into on-field dominance with an 11-win regular season – all by 20+ points – and the school’s first outright Big 12 title. They are just getting started.

Over the past two cycles, the average Big 12 team has signed two four-star transfers. Texas Tech signed 20. They are fully reloaded again with the most talented roster no matter how you view it: recruiting rankings, transfer rankings, all- conference players, mock NFL Draft picks, etc.

Tech avoids BYU and Utah, and their four toughest Big 12 opponents all have to come to Lubbock. Texas Tech proved me right by getting to Dallas last year. This year they are my pick to repeat as Big 12 champs, and have the best shot in
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Following the 2024 season, Texas Tech shocked the college football world by signing the #2 ranked transfer class. In total, they signed 13 four-star transfers – more than the other 15 Big 12 schools combined.

Tech routed their three non-conference opponents and then made a statement by beating #14 Utah 34-10 in the Big 12 opener. Utah head coach Kyle Whittingham was stunned: “never would have believed in a million years that we would lose the line of scrimmage.”

That quickly became a pattern as Texas Tech’s defensive front seven dominated all season and all seven guys finished with All-Big 12 honors. Do- it-all Jacob Rodriguez posted the most productive stat-line by a linebacker in decades and earned the top spot on my Heisman ballot.

Texas Tech bulldozed through their schedule and joined some elite company. In the Playoff era (2014-2025) there have been 1,566 FBS teams, but just three won 11 regular season games by 20+ points: 2018 Alabama, 2019 Ohio State, and now 2025 Texas Tech.

They hosted College Gameday for the first time since 2008, clinched their first Big 12 title game appearance, and then suffocated BYU 34-7 to win the school’s first outright conference title in 70 years.

Joey McGuire, Mr. Texas High School Football, delivered the best season in Texas Tech history.

Yes, the Matador Club provided a program-changing budget, but they are not the only program with similar resources. At the Big 12 post-game press conference, McGuire made it a point to mention the roots of his three stars sitting next to him – quarterback Behren Morton was a hometown hero, Rodriguez was a converted quarterback walk-on, and linebacker Ben Roberts’ only offer in 2022 was Texas Tech.

Their Playoff debut was a 23-0 shutout loss to Oregon, but with their roster retention and another elite transfer haul, Texas Tech is just getting started.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Morton went pro, and the staff signed the #2 rated transfer quarterback this cycle, five-star Brendan Sorsby (Cincinnati). With an ongoing legal battle, in June his college career ended and he will prepare for the pros.

Former Top200 Will Hammond was Morton’s backup last year and played well when Morton was injured. Hammond led four scoring drives late in the Utah win, ran for two touchdowns against Kansas, and has thrown for 1,151 yards and nine touchdowns so far. He is also an effective runner on zone reads, scrambles, and quarterback designed runs – he even showed off breakaway speed on a 64-yard run in the opener.

Hammond is still recovering from an ACL injury but with Sorsby gone, the timeline has been moved up to a full return in mid-August, just in time for kickoff. Tech also signed Tulsa’s 2024 starter Kirk Francis and four-star freshman Lloyd Jones got game reps against West Virginia.

Tech’s one-two punch at running back returns with 1,000-yarder Cameron Dickey and explosive J’Koby Williams. Dickey posted a 263-yard game against Kansas State, both backs earned All-Big 12 honors and combined to catch 60 balls for 600+ yards in the pass game. 2025 four-star transfer Quinten Joyner (USC) is back healthy and somehow they retained all three.

Receivers Caleb Douglas, Reggie Virgil, and Coy Eakin all ranked in the league’s Top 16 WR in receiving yardage, but only Eakin returns for 2026. The two outside spots are open and the staff signed a pair of two-year starters Kenny Johnson (Pittsburgh) and former Top200 Malcolm Simmons (Auburn). Micah Hudson was a five-star and Tech’s highest-ranked recruit and he has breakout potential. From the 2026 class they signed Top100 Chase Campbell (Wolfforth, TX) and have three more four-stars in the room. There is plenty of firepower here yet again.

All-Big 12 Terrance Carter returns after placing second in the league in receiving categories among tight ends. Jett Carpenter (Nevada) was All-Mountain West and actually led his team in receptions and yards.

The offensive line was strong enough to win the conference, but on the Playoff tier it appeared to be a limiting factor. Texas Tech ranked slightly above average in both my OL Run Push (#60) and Pass

Protection (#51) though against Oregon, outside of one Williams’ run, Tech was held to 1 yard/carry and sacked four times. This room is upgraded for 2026 with three All-Big 12 starters back – left tackle Howard Sampson, center Sheridan Wilson, and right tackle Jacob Ponton – plus four blue-chip additions. A pair of four-star transfers will fill the guard spots with Jordan Church (Louisville) and Hunter Zambrano (2025 transfer) both earning Top 10 rankings. Five-star Felix Ojo (Mansfield Lake Ridge, TX) and Top100 Bryce Gilmore (Prosper, TX) bolster the tackle spots.
pick_six_2026.defense:
McGuire saw coordinator Shiel Wood build a Top 25 defense at Houston and hired him to do the same here. Texas Tech pumped the defense with four-star transfers, loaded up the best defensive line in school history, and they surged all the way to the #1 spot in my opponent-adjusted defensive rankings.

Nine starters got All-Big 12 honors, five were first-team, and David Bailey and Rodriguez were unanimous All-Americans. Rodriguez swept the defensive awards, finished fifth in the Heisman and posted the most productive linebacker stat-line in a generation: 117 tackles, 11 for loss, 7 forced fumbles, 4 interceptions, 2 fumble recoveries, and even two rushing touchdowns out of the wildcat. Against Oklahoma State, he shot through the line and grabbed the ball right out of the back’s arms and sprinted 70 yards for a touchdown. J-Rod earned my vote.

Rodriguez and four defensive linemen were all drafted. Bailey, Romello Height, Lee Hunter, and Skyler Gill-Howard formed a legendary defensive line and McGuire admits that while there are no exact replacements, Tech added “four future NFL draft picks” through the portal. Top-rated four-star transfer Mateen Ibirogba (Wake Forest) and Bryce Butler (Washington) fill Hunter’s spot at nose tackle. Off the edge they signed a pair of first-team all-leaguers from the non-AQ level in Adam Trick (Miami, OH) and Trey White (San Diego State). AJ Holmes is a returning starter at defensive tackle with All-Big 12 accolades, and Jayden Cofield is back in the two-deep. Tech signed five-star edge rusher LaDamion Guyton (Savannah, GA) for additional firepower.

Roberts was the Big 12 Title MVP with two interceptions and returns as the leader at linebacker. While Rodriguez cannot be replaced, Tech signed the #2 linebacker transfer, two-time All-Big 12 Austin

Romaine (Kansas State). Corey Platt (Houston) has high upside but has missed two seasons with injury.

Four defensive back starters return, led by the corner pair of first-team All-Big 12 Brice Pollock and Amier Boyd. Linebacker/safety hybrid John Curry and safety Brenden Jordan are back, and then Top200 Peyton Morgan was a spring hero and “ballhawk” to earn the open safety spot.

pick_six_projections.notes: Ciancia's 2026 CFP projection: Big 12 champion (automatic bid to 12-team Playoff).

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Cignetti’s national champion Hoosiers head into 2026 with a clear top five defense with an impressive six All- Big Ten stars returning on that side of the ball. The offensive line should contend for the Joe Moore Award and their coordinators are both elite.

It’s splitting hairs at the top of the Big Ten, but the loss of the Heisman winner and two game-changing receivers moves Indiana out of the top spot. They are still a Playoff pick and have a shot at a repeat title.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
It’s a shame their namesake “Hoosiers” was already used in an award-winning sports film, because Curt Cignetti’s turnaround story here was made for Hollywood. ESPN’s Sean McDonough said, “it’s one of the great stories of all time – not just in college football, but in American sports.”

Cignetti took over the losingest program in the sport, boldly claimed “I win, Google me” at the opening press conference, and then proceeded to do just that.

The 11-win transition season was impressive enough, but the 2025 team unlocked another tier: perfection.

The regular season had six 40+ point blowouts, including a 63-10 beatdown of #9 Illinois that boosted Indiana up into the Top 10. Fernando Mendoza found Elijah Sarratt for game-sealing, fourth-quarter touchdowns in wins over Iowa and Oregon, and then had his “Heisman Moment” when he delivered a knockout punch against Penn State: Omar Cooper’s unforgettable toe-tap touchdown.

Sarratt had another game-winner in a 13-10 defensive battle with the defending champs, as Indiana snapped their 30-game losing streak to Ohio State and notched their first outright Big Ten title since 1945.

In the Rose Bowl quarterfinal, Indiana physically dominated Alabama, dealing the 21st century dynasty a taste of its own medicine. They outrushed the Tide by 200+ yards and won by 35.

The semifinal set up a rematch with Oregon, but on the first pass of the game All American D’Angelo Ponds took back a Pick Six to start the 56-22 rout.

The final test was Miami, a roster packed with top recruits and future pros, on their home turf. Cignetti made two gutsy fourth-down calls, and his players delivered. Mendoza hit Charlie Becker on a back- shoulder fade, and then on another fourth down, Mendoza took a quarterback draw, broke tackles, spun around, and then launched over the goal-line for the iconic title-moment.

“I had to go airborne… I would die for my team,” said Mendoza.

From Big Ten punching bag to a perfect 16-0, Cignetti’s program turnaround will be the new standard that all are compared to going forward. A collection of words I never thought I would write: Indiana won the National Championship.
pick_six_2026.offense:
The dream season was capped off with the school’s first Heisman winner. Mendoza led the nation with 41 passing touchdowns, posted the #1 QB Rating, and made every clutch play required for a 16- 0 perfect season. He was selected first overall in the NFL Draft, but that same night, Indiana was hosting its spring game and breaking in their next signal-caller.

Cignetti focuses on veteran, experienced transfers and followed that strategy at quarterback with TCU’s multi-year starter Josh Hoover who is the active FBS leader in passing yards (9,627) and passing touchdowns (71) and nearly hit the 4,000-yard mark in 2024.

Cignetti says Hoover is at a similar point post-spring that his other two transfer quarterbacks – Kurtis Rourke and Mendoza – were at, however one remaining issue is Hoover’s high number of turnovers. In 31 starts he turned it over 42 times.

Indiana uses a running back duo and last year both Kaelon Black and Roman Hemby went over 1,000 yards but both went pro. Khobie Martin rushed for 505 yards as the third option and is joined by Boston College starter Turbo Richard. Last season Richard fumbled at the goal-line twice which cost BC two winnable games, but it rounded into a solid season and he earned a four-star transfer rank.

Sarratt had go-ahead scores against Iowa, Oregon, and Ohio State, Cooper had the iconic toe-tap to beat Penn State, and both All-Big Ten receivers went pro. Sarratt led the nation with 15 touchdowns and Cooper was second in Power 4 with 13. Title game hero Becker returns and the staff signed one of the top-rated transfers Nick Marsh (Michigan State) who put up 1,300 yards combined over his

first two seasons. Tyler Morris is back from injury and was the spring hero in the slot. The staff also added Shazz Preston who was Tulane’s #1 receiver last year and his 16.8 per-catch average was a Top 5 AAC mark.

The tight end room is the biggest question heading into fall camp after the departure of All-Big Ten Riley Nowakowski. Andrew Barker is a blocking tight end and incoming four-star Brock Schott (Miami) is the receiving threat. Given the uncertainty, coordinator Mike Shanahan may show some new wrinkles or more four-WR sets.

Four starters are back from their Joe Moore Award semifinalist line, including All-American, “Big Ten Lineman of the Year” Carter Smith at left tackle. All-Big Ten center Pat Coogan is the lone departure from their national title line. Bray Lynch shifted in to the center spot, Drew Evans is back at guard, and Adedamola Ajani who surged up the depth chart in the playoffs. The staff signed Wisconsin starter Joe Brunner, who was ranked the #3 interior lineman this cycle.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Indiana allowed just 11.7 points/game (#2) and 266 yards/game (#4) and coordinator Bryant Haines was named the Broyles Award winner. Oregon’s Dan Lanning faced Haines’ defense twice last year and noted several challenges: “they’re really good at post-snap movement, the defensive line plays with relentless effort, and it’s the best zone break defense I’ve seen this year.”

Nine defenders earned All-Big Ten honors, six return for 2026, plus the staff added five more starters off other Power 4 rosters.

The interior tackle duo of Tyrique Tucker and Mario Landino could be one of the nation’s best pairs. Tucker could push for All-America honors, and Landino was a wrecking-ball throughout the season. Three ends are gone, but Daniel Ndukwe played well after the starters were injured, and the staff hit the portal here. Indiana signed both of Kansas State’s starting ends with All-Big 12 Chiddi Obiazor and elite pass rusher Tobi Osunsanmi. Josh Burnham (Notre Dame) and Joe Hjelle (Tulsa) were three-star additions.

The quarterback-of-the-defense Aiden Fisher went pro, but the other two backers return after All-Big Ten seasons: Rolijah Hardy and Isaiah Jones. With a proven pair, they may show more 4-2-5 looks rather than their three-backer 4-3 last year.

Two first-team All-Big Ten defensive backs are gone with lockdown corner D’Angelo Ponds and strong safety Louis Moore both going pro. Jamari Sharpe had the national title-sealing interception and returns at corner, and the other corner spot is a battle between Ryland Gandy and former five-star, Penn State starter AJ Harris. Amare Ferrell returns at free safety and the staff added two more Power 4 starters in Quan Sanks (Cincinnati) and seventh-year Preston Zachman (Wisconsin).

pick_six_projections.notes: Ciancia's 2026 CFP projection: at-large bid, projected to host Ole Miss in first round.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Ole Miss is right back in SEC title contention with Chambliss back and operating in a similar scheme. The receivers may not be as proven as last season, but there is enough firepower – plus an All-American running back – to keep the offense in the top ten.

Golding focused on the defense this transfer cycle and added an amazing eight four-star defenders. Ole Miss is a Playoff at-large pick, and Chambliss already showed he can work magic in January.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Lane Kiffin called himself the Portal King and backed up the title by signing top- rated transfer classes every offseason. He used the transfer portal as an equalizer to catch up to the five-star recruiters atop the SEC, and after a close call in 2024, his sixth Ole Miss team broke through to the Playoff.

For all the four-star transfers and national stars he signed, it was actually a Division II quarterback who was the difference-maker. The staff found Trinidad Chambliss, an under-sized, under-recruited winner whose only other offer was from Temple. When starter Austin Simmons suffered an injury two weeks in, Chambliss stepped up and held the job for good.

Ole Miss survived one-score battles against Arkansas and Washington State, and then Chambliss threw for 315 yards on an elite Oklahoma defense. They sealed their best regular season in school history with a 38-19 Egg Bowl win to get to 11- 1 and clinch the school’s first-ever Playoff spot.

Off the field, a whole different circus was underway, as Kiffin considered taking other head coaching jobs amid the biggest coaching carousel of all-time. No matter your opinion of Kiffin’s actions and decision, this ridiculous schedule forces head coaches to decide between coaching a Playoff team or accepting a

heavily-desired job elsewhere. No other sport has overlapping deadlines like that.

Kiffin ultimately took the LSU job, wanted to coach Ole Miss through the postseason, but the Ole Miss admin rejected that proposal. Instead of a drawn out head coaching search of their own, athletic director Keith Carter knew “we had a guy in our building” already in defensive coordinator Pete Golding.

Golding and the Ole Miss team rallied together and blew out Tulane 41-10, got revenge on Georgia 39- 34, and earned a spot in the national semifinals. The Rebels held a lead in the final seconds but Miami’s Carson Beck scrambled in for the decisive touchdown.

13 wins marked a school record, and Ole Miss finished ranked #3 in the AP for their best finish in over 60 years. The fact they did so despite a tremendous amount of outside noise and distractions speaks volumes.

The next fear was that Kiffin would raid the Ole Miss roster by stealing all the star players, and though he did convince a handful of starters, it was not the wrecking ball some expected. In fact, Ole Miss punched back harder and signed the #2 transfer haul in America.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Chambliss took advantage of his opportunity and thrived into a national star. He quickly drew Kyler Murray comparisons, threw for nearly 4,000 yards, rushed for 527, totaled 30 touchdowns, and finished eighth in the Heisman. Then in the Georgia playoff game his wild scrambles helped convert and extend drives and lead the win.

He won a court case to return for a bonus year of eligibility and enters 2026 as a legit Heisman favorite. Original starter Austin Simmons transferred out to Missouri but the staff landed former five-star, MS legend Deuce Knight (Auburn) as their quarterback of the future.

Kiffin and his coordinator Charlie Weis are gone, but Golding wanted to continue with their successful, productive, up-tempo scheme. He hired John David Baker, who was here at Ole Miss as Weis’ co- coordinator until 2023, then improved East Carolina from #127 scoring to #34 and #24 the past two seasons. Baker says his 2026 scheme is “80% the same” as what has worked here.

Kewan Lacy earned first-team All-SEC, FWAA All-America, and returns after an Ole Miss record-tying 1,567 yard season (Quinshon Judkins 2022). He punched in a Power 4-best 24 touchdowns last year and is now complemented by Michigan State starter Makhi Frazier and former Top200 JT Lindsey (LSU).

Ole Miss was overflowing with talent on the outsides, and five pass-catchers placed in the SEC’s Top 25 of receiving stats. Four of those are gone – Harrison Wallace, De’Zhaun Stribling, Cayden Lee (Missouri) and tight end Dae'Quan Wright – but as always Ole Miss restocked the room. Deuce Alexander is a returning starter and their new #1 weapon, 2025 five-star Caleb Cunningham is ready for a breakout season, and then the staff added another round of five Power 4 receivers. Johntay Cook and Darrell Gill combined for over 1,000 yards as Syracuse starters, Horatio Fields (Auburn) earned a four-star transfer grade, and Traylon Ray (West Virginia) and Isaiah Spencer (Virginia Tech) bring Power 4 experience.

Wright went pro, but a pair of former five-stars form an elite tight end pair for 2026. Luke Hasz is finally back healthy, and Caleb Odom is a receiving matchup nightmare who could also play some receiver.

The offensive line returns its interior with guards Patrick Kutas and Delano Townsend and center Brycen Sanders all back. They did lose two great ones at the tackle spots with All-SEC Diego Pounds and NFL draft pick Jayden Williams both gone. And then their rising star at tackle Devin Harper followed Kiffin to Baton Rouge. Ole Miss stole one back from LSU with their starting tackle Carius Curne who was a Top100 recruit and ranked the #4 transfer lineman this cycle. Terez Davis is projected at the other tackle spot, but three other Power 4 transfers will compete.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Kiffin’s first three defenses averaged #43 of 68 Power 4 in my opponent-adjusted metric. Golding took over in 2023 and his second unit finished ranked #9. Heading into 2025, Kiffin put most resources into the offensive side of the transfer portal, but Golding made sure to load up on defense this cycle.

Ole Miss signed an incredible eight four-star transfer defenders. Yes, they lost a pair of All-SEC stars to Kiffin -- linebacker TJ Dottery and edge Princewill Umanmielen – but Golding has stacked the roster heading into 2026.

First-team All-SEC defensive tackle Will Echoles is back after leading Power 4 tackles with 39 quarterback pressures. Kam Franklin is another returning starter at end, and then Ole Miss signed the top haul of defensive linemen with four four-stars incoming. Blake Purchase (Oregon) and Jordan Renaud (Alabama) look to replace Umanmielen’s production off the edge, while Jehiem Oatis (Colorado) and Michai Boireau (Florida) pack the interior. Boireau even had an athletic, game-winning interception to beat Mississippi State last year. Jonathan Maldonado (Nevada) earned All-Mountain West last year.

Do-it-all Suntarine Perkins returns as a hybrid linebacker, edge rusher and is poised for an All-American run in his final season. Though they lose Golding’s so-called “quarterback of the defense” Dottery, they landed a trio of Power 4 starters. Keaton Thomas (Baylor) was All-Big 12 and hits like a truck, Luke Ferrelli was named ACC Defensive Rookie of the Year after leading all freshmen with 91 tackles, and Tah’j Butler started some games for Georgia Tech. This a top national unit.

The cornerback starters Antonio Kite and Jaylon Braxton are both back, plus they added Auburn starter and four-star transfer Jalyn Crawford. Their safeties are gone but they added three more starters in Edwin Joseph (Florida State), Sharif Denson (Florida), and Joenel Aguero (Georgia).

pick_six_projections.notes: Ciancia's 2026 CFP projection: at-large bid, projected first-round game at Indiana.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
For the first time since the Pete Carroll dynasty, USC signed the nation’s #1 recruiting class. Add in that extra firepower to last year’s #12 Game Grader team (#7 in opponent-adjusted yardage margin), with 14 starters back plus six more Power 4 starters transferring in…

2026 is Playoff or Bust for USC. They are my pick for the final at-large Playoff spot in the 2026 bracket.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
In last year’s preview magazine I wrote that the 2025 season was critical for Lincoln Riley and the USC program overall. They were projected to sign the #1 recruiting class in America, but a losing season could have been enough to fire Riley – and ultimately break apart that top class.

Riley needed to do enough to survive 2025 to get to the other side with a talent-packed roster.

USC dropped a 73-point bomb in the opener and stayed atop the offensive charts for most of the season, finishing 3rd of 68 Power 4 in my opponent- adjusted ranking. The 4-0 start was soured by a shootout loss at Illinois, and then a kickoff return touchdown cost them the Notre Dame game.

Other USC teams over the past decade would have crumbled, but this one found an extra gear. Down two linemen and three running backs, walk- on King Miller overpowered #15 Michigan with 158 rushing yards. Nebraska neutralized their pass game, but Miller again helped lead the win in a “Blackout” game at Memorial Stadium.

USC trailed Iowa 21-7 shortly before halftime but didn’t flinch. Instead, the offense scored on five straight possessions for the comeback win to push to 8-2 overall and a Top 15 AP ranking.

They were unable to break through in a quasi Playoff play-in game against Oregon, losing 42- 27 in Eugene, but they capped a perfect 7-0 home slate by beating UCLA 29-10 in the finale.

They don’t hang banners in the LA Coliseum for nine-win seasons, but it was certainly enough to get Riley through to this program-changing recruiting haul. It was an important nine wins. Riley agrees and said, “we’ll have better teams here in the future than this team, but I don’t know if we’ll have had a more important team.”
pick_six_2026.offense:
Jayden Maiava took a major step forward in his first full season as the starter here. He earned third-team All-Big Ten, placed second in the league with a high 9.2 yards/attempt, and threw 24 touchdowns. Maiava will need to cut down on the 10 picks, but this should remain a Top 10 offense with him at the helm. Five-star Husan Longstreet was projected as the 2027 starter of

the future but he transferred out to LSU.

Waymond Jordan and Eli Sanders were both injured in the Michigan game, forcing the walk-on Miller into the lead role. While healthy, Jordan was averaging 6.6 per carry and posted two 100- yard games in the five before the injury. Miller nearly broke the 1,000-yard milestone (6.2 per carry) and these two return to form a top duo in 2026. They added a pair of Top100 backs in Shahn Alston and Deshonne Redeaux.

Makai Lemon was simply unstoppable. He led Power 4 in receiving yards/game (96), cashed in 11 touchdowns, and earned the Biletnikoff. His co-star Ja’Kobi Lane also graduated, but Tanook Hines impressed as a freshman and leads another crowded room into 2026. Zacharyus Williams was Utah’s #1 receiver and is back from injury. The staff added NC State’s lead receiver Terrell Anderson who was graded a four-star transfer and was fifth in the ACC in yards/catch. Then USC signed some extra firepower with two near-five-stars Ethan Feaster and Kayden Dixon-Wyatt, and another Top200 fresh off a CA state title run in Trent Mosley.

It’s the same deal at tight end. Star veterans Lake McRee and Walker Lyons are gone, but five-star Mark Bowman (Mater Dei, CA) could start right away as a true freshman. The staff added blocking end Tucker Ashcraft (Wisconsin) who was called an “instant impact.” Riley’s tight end usage more than doubled from 2024 to 2025 in targets and yards, but he may shift back to more 11 or 10 personnel if those elite receivers are as-advertised.

The offensive line returns all five original starters, but this group was crushed with injuries and they were forced to start seven different line combinations. Still, the line made it consecutive Top 25 finishes in both OL Run Push and Pass Protection. Elijah Paige is the anchor at left tackle, Justin Tauanuu started all year at right tackle, Alani Noa has 22 career starts, and Tobias Raymond has

shown positional flexibility to play anywhere. Kilian O’Connor is back at center, plus the staff added the nation’s #1 tackle in five-star Keenyi Pepe.

In total, they have eight offensive starters back, plus NC State’s #1 receiver, plus four incoming five- stars.
pick_six_2026.defense:
