After the defensive collapse under Alex Grinch, Riley hired D’Anton Lynn from across town. There was no breakthrough and after two years Lynn left.

A few weeks after playing TCU in the bowl game, Riley hired Mr. TCU himself – former head coach Gary Patterson – to take over the defense. Patterson’s unique match-zone 4-2-5 defense helped build TCU into a mid-major powerhouse and eventually thrive through the transition up to the Big 12.

TCU went just 21-21 overall in his final four years there, but his 20-year sample size of elite defenses is no fluke. He inherits quite the stockpile of blue-chip talent, and at his opening presser he noted “I’ve never had this big of a defensive line.”

Three starting linemen return with Jide Abasiri at tackle and Kameryn Crawford and Braylan Shelby on the ends. Former five-star tackle Jahkeem Stewart earned Freshman All-America honors last year and the room was beefed up by three major signings: Michigan State starter Alex VanSumeren, five-star Jaimeon Winfield, and Top100 Tomuhini Topui.

The staff added two more to the end spots with Penn State starter Zuriah Fisher (rated as a four- star transfer) and five-star Luke Wafle (Princeton, NJ) who was ranked the #1 DE in the 2026 class. USC hasn’t posted a Top 30 run defense since 2014 but this is their best shot.

USC loses do-it-all Eric Gentry whose skillset allowed for creative packages. Desman Stephens led with 89 tackles and is back and will likely start alongside Deven Bryant (Washington) who brings Big Ten starting experience. Incoming Top100 Talanoa Ili could push into the rotation.

Injuries plagued the secondary with two original starters -- Chasen Johnson and Prophet Brown -- lost by mid- September. Then in November both star safeties Kamari Ramsey and All-American Bishop Fitzgerald were injured. Johnson and Brown are back, the safeties are gone, and Patterson has plenty to sort out in the secondary. Marcelles Williams, Alex Graham, and Christian Pierce all started games last year. The staff signed the #1 transfer corner Jontez Williams (Iowa State) who earned All-Big 12 honors and is an instant starter here. And of course, they grabbed another Top100 super-recruit in corner Elbert Hill.

pick_six_projections.notes: Ciancia's 2026 CFP projection: at-large bid, projected first-round game at Notre Dame.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Transition season or not, this is viewed as a Playoff or Bust roster.

Kiffin has a proven track record building elite offenses, and no one has succeeded more with the transfer portal. The nation’s #1 transfer haul instantly moves LSU up from the SEC’s mid-tier to the crowded Playoff tier. LSU is my pick for #5 in the league, but with the added ninth conference game I do not see a repeat of 2025 when the SEC landed five Playoff bids (four of the seven at-large spots).
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
It started with a fake Southern accent and ended four years later with a five-minute, midseason, farewell meeting. Brian Kelly never fit the LSU job.

His first team made the SEC title game and then Jayden Daniels won the Heisman in 2023, but the two sides of the ball couldn’t match up. First, the roster was too young, then the defense collapsed so he hired Blake Baker, then the offense collapsed.

2025 was set to be the big payoff season and after wins over #4 Clemson and Florida, LSU surged to #3 in the AP. The offense broke down and they lost to Ole Miss (-230 yardage margin), then again to Vanderbilt as they settled for four field goals in a seven-point decision. The loss to Texas A&M, with a 35-7 second half blowout, was the final straw.

“Our fan base should be upset, that second half was unacceptable on any level,” said Kelly. He was fired the next day.

The team went 2-3 with interim Frank Wilson but the focus quickly shifted towards the coaching carousel and LSU’s spot in the Lane Kiffin Sweepstakes. In a controversial split, Ole Miss did not allow Kiffin to coach his team through the postseason, but that gave The Portal King more time to start building the foundation here in Baton Rouge.

Kiffin did it again. After several Top 3 transfer hauls at Ole Miss, Kiffin led LSU to the #1 overall transfer class this cycle complete with an insane 17 four/five-stars – the next closest had 12. LSU signed the best from each of the sport’s most important positions: #1 quarterback, #1 offensive tackle, #1 edge rusher.

In total, the transfer class featured 11 starters off Power 4 teams, three more were all- conference at the Non-AQ level, and 10 were former Top200 recruits. Speaking of recruiting, LSU signed another 11 blue-chippers in the 2026 high school class and on a per-player average they ranked #8 nationally.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Kiffin has had sustained success at building elite, explosive, high-scoring offenses. He uses tempo and wide spacing to create personnel mismatches. And every so often they’ll hit a wide-open vertical shot downfield.

All six of his Ole Miss offenses finished in the Top 20 of my opponent-adjusted metric, joining Ohio State, Oregon, and Louisville as the only other programs to go six for six over that span. Charlie Weis took over as the full coordinator in 2024 and his two surged up to #3 and #7.

Kiffin brought Weis with him to LSU and these two offensive masterminds assembled an all-time transfer haul this cycle.

Sam Leavitt was ranked the #1 transfer quarterback after leading Arizona State on their surprise Big 12 title run in 2024. Leavitt used his legs even more in 2025 and willed ASU to some victories before suffering a season-ending foot injury. He ranked fourth in the Big 12 in QB Rating in 2024 with 24 touchdowns and just six picks, but fell to 13th in QB Rating last year. Leavitt also missed spring ball due to injury rehab, though last year Kiffin and Weis got Trinidad Chambliss up to speed without spring.

LSU signed 2025 five-star Husan Longstreet (USC) as a potential quarterback of the future here, or a blue-chip insurance policy if Leavitt’s injury returns.

Caden Durham and Harlem Berry split carries last year and both return. Berry was a five-star and the #1 running back of the 2025 recruiting class and surged to the top spot here in spring. Dilin Jones joins the rotation after splitting carries at Wisconsin last year.

The receiver room is a total roster transfusion: 10 guys out, 10 guys in. As usual, Kiffin added an insane amount of firepower on the outsides. Jayce Brown (Kansas State) was All-Big 12 last year, Eugene Wilson (Florida) is a multi-year SEC starter, and Winston Watkins (Ole Miss) actually took

over the top spot in spring with his scheme familiarity and four-star potential. Two more earned all-league honors at the non-AQ level: Jackson Harris (Hawaii) and Tre’ Brown (Old Dominion). All five guys were rated as four-star transfers making this the top portal unit in the country. It’s also worth noting that Jayce Brown, Harris, and Tre’ Brown all ranked in their league’s top three in yards/catch – a much-needed boost to LSU’s poor pass explosiveness last year (#124). 2026 signee Corey Barber is another near-five star.

Their best pass-catcher is actually at tight end with athletic freak Trey’Dez Green returning after an All-SEC campaign. The 6’7 Green is a mismatch nightmare who will thrive in this offense.

LSU signed the nation’s top transfer lineman in five-star, All-Big 12 Jordan Seaton (Colorado) who is an instant starter at left tackle. Aliou Bah (Maryland) started 24 straight games in the Big Ten and did not allow a single sack last year. The staff convinced center Braelin Moore to delay his NFL bid, Bo Bordelon rose to a starting guard spot this spring, and Top100 Weston Davis held his spot at tackle despite some freshman growing pains last year. Devin Harper (Ole Miss) and Sean Thompkins (Baylor) are both excellent additions who could push in fall camp.
pick_six_2026.defense:
This side of the ball was the team strength -- #13 in opponent-adjusted defense – so Kiffin kept ace coordinator Blake Baker.

LSU returns five starters from the back seven, and then added four starters off other SEC defenses. All-SEC defensive backs AJ Haulcy and Mansoor Delane were drafted in April, but safeties Tamarcus Cooley and Dashawn Spears return along with the corner duo of DJ Pickett and PJ Woodland. Five-star Pickett had a breakout true freshman season and could earn All-SEC hype. The staff added a pair of four-star transfers with first-team All-Mountain West Ty Benefield (Boise State) and 2025 Top50 Faheem Delane (Ohio State).

Do-it-all Harold Perkins went pro, but Whit Weeks and Davhon Keys are back at linebacker. Keys led the team in tackles, Weeks was injured and is looking for a bounce-back season, and then the staff signed TJ Dottery (Ole Miss) who Pete Golding called his “quarterback of the defense” last year. This looks like a three-man rotation for the two spots of the 4-2-5.

Kiffin brought All-SEC edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen from Ole Miss. He led with nine sacks last year and was rated the #1 defender in this portal cycle. Jordan Ross (Tennessee) has less experience but was a five-star in the 2024 class, and then LSU signed the nation’s #1 edge recruit this class Lamar Brown (Erwinville, LA). Yes, that’s a triple five-star edge rush trio.

Five-star Dominick McKinley is back at tackle and now moves into the starting lineup along with Auburn starter Malik Blocton. Stephiylan Green was a four-star transfer, plus they signed the two of the top four 2026 interior linemen: five-star Richard Anderson (Edna Karr HS, LA) and Top100 Deuce Geralds (Suwanee, GA).

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Normally a double coordinator switch, seven linemen lost, and a school-record outbound NFL Draft class would be enough to sink a program. But Texas A&M has been a consistent Top 10 recruiter and landed a Top 10 transfer haul to make this a “reload” instead of the expected “rebuild.”

Last year on their 11-0 start, they faced seven of the bottom nine SEC teams. The schedule heats up in 2026 and they now draw five of the top eight. Texas A&M remains a Playoff contender but are projected a spot or two outside the bracket.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Marcel Reed led a last-minute touchdown drive to finish off a 41-40 shootout win over Notre Dame in South Bend. The statement win launched Texas A&M into the Playoff picture right away.

Fast starts have been common here, but A&M has struggled to get past October hurdles. This time, they had all the answers and found ways to win week after week.

The defense held Auburn to 0/12 on third downs in a 16-10 win. The offense won another shootout 45-42 over Arkansas. Then both sides of the ball flexed with 20+ point wins over LSU and Missouri.

A&M raced to a 10-0 start – their best since 1992 – and rose all the way to #3 in the AP Poll.

Then in the blink of an eye, they trailed South Carolina 30-3 at halftime. Teams were 0-286 when trailing by 27+ points in an SEC game. A&M made it 1-286. Reed led a furious second-half rally with 439 passing yards and a perfect 28-0 score after the break.

At 11-0 the stage was set. A&M hosted Texas in the long-awaited return of the rivalry to Kyle Field, but with a win-and-in scenario for their first SEC title game appearance, they came up short. Reed tossed two picks in the fourth quarter to end his Heisman bid and flip the game back to Texas.

Even with the loss, the resume was strong enough to host their first-ever Playoff game in College Station, but another late interception in the endzone finished off a defensive struggle: Miami 10, Texas A&M 3.

In his second season, Mike Elko got A&M its first Playoff bid, its best start in 30+ years, and now has some lessons learned from their 0-2 finish.

This time, A&M has a double coordinator switch, seven new starters on the lines of scrimmage, and must replace a school-record 10 NFL draft picks.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Ace offensive coordinator Collin Klein took the head coaching job at his alma mater Kansas State, but Elko promoted from within to continue what worked here last season. He picked receivers coach Holmon Wiggins who will be a first-time playcaller but has proven to be an elite receiver coach. Wiggins spent five years on Nick Saban’s Alabama staff and coached five first-rounders and Heisman winner DeVonta Smith. Then here at Texas A&M he was pivotal in signing their two key transfers KC Concepcion and Mario Craver – two moves that undoubtedly changed their season outlook.

These two formed the only Power 4 pair of 900+ yard receivers and their elusiveness in the screen game helped Reed average 10+ yards/pass on throws behind the line of scrimmage. Concepcion was picked in the first round this April, but Craver returns in the slot as an All-SEC headliner. Ashton Bethel-Roman played his best ball down the stretch and averaged 20+ yards/catch over the final seven. The staff added Alabama starter Isaiah Horton who was ranked the #7 transfer receiver this cycle. The 6’4 Horton had eight touchdowns last year and is the solution to A&M’s redzone issue. Terry Bussey is a former five-star, and Top100 Aaron Gregory was noted as the best freshman this spring.

Reed returns after placing in the SEC’s top five in yards/attempt, touchdowns, and the all-encompassing QB Rating. On top of that he added 493 rushing yards and six more scores on the ground. The lasting memory for most will be the redzone interceptions in the two losses, but Reed was a legit Heisman contender into November and is one of the most proven leaders returning in the SEC.

It’s a complete rebuild for the rest of the offense.

Last year A&M returned all five offensive linemen and they were a solid unit ranking in the Top 30 of both my OL Run Push and Pass Protection. But now four starters are gone. All four were drafted and three – Trey Zuhn, Chase Bisontis, and Ar’maj Reed-Adams – were All-SEC picks.

Mark Nabou is the lone returning starter at center, and the staff attacked the transfer portal to round out the 2026 starting five. They signed four starters off other SEC lines with 54 combined starts. Wilkin Formby (Alabama) and Tyree Adams (LSU) both earned four-star transfer grades and were Top200 blue-

chippers before that. Coen Echols (LSU) surged up the depth chart to start eight games as a redshirt freshman, and Trovon Baugh (South Carolina) is a multi-year starter. A&M also has a pair of backup tackles who were highly-touted recruits in Robert Bourdon and 2025 five-star Lamont Rogers.

Le’Veon Moss was the original starting running back but after a midseason injury, Rueben Owens took over and finished with 639 yards (5.4 per carry). Owens is back and four-star Jamarion Morrow will be his number two.

The top three tight ends are gone with Nate Boerkircher and Amari Niblack graduated, and Theo Melin Ohrstrom off to SMU. Fifth-year vet Micah Riley was named a team captain and will be joined by All- AAC Houston Thomas (UTSA).
pick_six_2026.defense:
Elko’s 4-2-5 defense was as aggressive as ever last year. Texas A&M ranked #3 in Negative Play rate which tracks how frequently a defense disrupt plays at or behind the line of scrimmage. They were also #1 nationally on third down conversions (23%). But with that aggressive scheme, they were over-exposed to explosive plays especially long-yardage runs (#130).

It helped having a unanimous All-American coming off the edge. Cashius Howell was the SEC Defender of the Year, was second in the league in sacks with 11.5 and even became the first FBS player in a decade to record three sacks on three straight plays.

Howell, and tackles Albert Regis and Tyler Onyedim were all drafted, and the staff added some key transfers to help the reload. Anto Saka (Northwestern) was All-Big Ten and is drawing some legit first- round buzz as a physical pass rusher. Saka joins returning starting end TJ Searcy and Top200 Marco Jones. On the inside, five-star DJ Hicks moves up into a starting spot, CJ Mims (UNC) had a high 40 tackles last year, and Brandon Davis-Swain (Colorado) was a portal win.

Three-year starter and tackle-machine Taurean York and Scooby Williams both went pro, but Daymion Sanford returns as an excellent run stopper. The staff signed first-team All-AAC Ray Coney (Tulsa) who started the past three years and posted a league-best 128 tackles last year. Top100 Noah Mikhail is the

next backer up in case Sanford’s spring injury lingers.

The secondary is packed with returning talent and proven transfers. All three safeties are back – Dalton Brooks, Marcus Ratcliffe, and Bryce Anderson – with Big 12 honorable mention Tawfiq Byard (Colorado) added to the rotation. Will Lee went pro, but starting corner Dezz Ricks returns. Rickey Gibson (Tennessee) was originally an All-SEC candidate before a season-ending injury.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
It’s all about Underwood’s development, scheme fit, and whether he gets a second-year starter bonus. There are few concerns across the rest of the roster, Whittingham and Beck are coaching upgrades, and they brought several all- conference stars with them from Utah.

Even through the coaching transition, Michigan remains in the Big Ten top five, and could push higher if Underwood lives up to his five-star billing.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
After their 2023 national title, Michigan sent a Top 5 all-time draft class to the pros: 13 selections.

By definition, it was a transition year for new head coach Sherrone Moore in 2024 with a new starting lineup. Their broken offense held them back with a disappointing 6-5 record before shocking #1 Ohio State in the largest upset in “The Game” history.

Heading into 2025, Michigan addressed the need at quarterback by signing the nation’s #1 overall recruit. Bryce Underwood started right away as a true freshman, flashed against the non-AQ teams in September, but ended up struggling through Big Ten play.

The offense doubled down on what was working, and their power rushing attack grinded out enough wins to remain in the Playoff hunt into November. Michigan held on to beat one-win Purdue 21-16, and then overcame three late turnovers to beat Northwestern 24-22 on a walk-off field goal.

Michigan had a “win and in” opportunity in the season finale against Ohio State, but after intercepting Julian Sayin on the second pass of the game, it was all Buckeyes. The loss snapped the four-game win streak in the series, and placed

Michigan outside the Game Grader Top 25 for the second straight year.

A week later, Moore was fired for an affair with a staffer, and then arrested and charged for other crimes. Michigan is also on NCAA probation for recruiting violations with fines that could reach $30 million.

The program needed stability, and they got the perfect definition of it in their next hire. Kyle Whittingham was Utah’s head coach for the past 21 years, took them undefeated back in 2008, helped move up to the Power 5 tier, and eventually built the program into back-to-back Pac-12 champions.

The 67-year-old says “I still have a lot left in the tank” and that he views this blueblood opportunity as a final challenge: “Michigan is a special place with a legitimate opportunity to win a national championship … it can happen here, and has happened here.”
pick_six_2026.offense:
Whittingham described his program style as “physicality, toughness, and grit.” Not only does that sound like Michigan’s 2023 national title formula, Whittingham actually backs up those buzzwords. Just watch a Utah spring game, where they are smashing each other for 60 minutes – no 7-on-7 or non-contact jerseys for the quarterbacks.

He brought offensive coordinator Jason Beck with him. Last year, Beck’s power-spread scheme led the most improved offense from 2024 to 2025. Utah led the nation in yards/carry (6.0), placed second in rushing yards/game (266), and complemented the run game with an efficient pass threat that ranked #31 in QB Rating.

Not to oversimplify the transition season, but Michigan’s 2026 fate depends on Underwood’s development in his second year. His freshman campaign was limited by a conservative gameplan, plenty of drops from the receivers, but also rookie mistakes. Underwood threw nine picks to just 11 touchdowns, was held under 100 yards three times, and placed #12 in the Big Ten in QB Rating.

Beck’s scheme is geared towards dual-threat quarterbacks, and Underwood’s best games last year were the ones when he used his legs.

Justice Haynes and Jordan Marshall both earned All-Big Ten honors and were the engine of the offense. Haynes transferred out to Georgia Tech but it was Marshall that surged with four straight 100-yard games late in the year. Michigan signed five-star super-recruit Savion Hiter who should get carries right away and form a top duo with Marshall.

Utah’s offensive line coach Jim Harding just sent two linemen to the NFL’s first round, and inherits a strong unit here. Injuries caused reshuffling last year but those ahead-of-schedule reps, and returning injured starters, should pay dividends here. Four guys earned All-Big Ten honors, two are gone – Giovanni El-Hadi and Greg Crippen – but tackle Andrew Sprague and center Jake Guarnera are back. As

a freshman, Blake Frazier stepped up and thrived at left tackle. Original starter Evan Link may shift inside to guard after Frazier’s strong play. Andrew Babalola was a five-star 2025 signee who was also battling for a job but was injured last fall camp.

The receiver room was plagued with dropped passes, but halfway through the season true freshman Andrew Marsh emerged as an instant star. Marsh got Big Ten honors after posting 45 catches for 651 yards – all after September. The staff signed the #5 receiver transfer JJ Buchanan who started as a freshman for Utah last year. Marsh and Buchanan are the proven one-two punch, and two additional blue-chippers add to the rotation with Top200 freshman Travis Johnson and Top50 Jaime Ffrench (Texas). This is a young room but has sky-high potential.

Michigan loses their do-it-all Max Bredeson as well as tight end Marlin Klein. Zack Marshall moves up as the full-time starter after 16 catches last year.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Whittingham hired BYU’s Jay Hill to lead the defense. Hill took over a broken BYU defense and after a rebuilding season, his last two ranked #15 and #24 in my opponent-adjusted ranking.

This will look just like Utah’s aggressive 4-2-5 base, as Whittingham notes that Hill “is from my coaching tree and played in our scheme.”

Michigan’s had consistent success on this side of the ball with five straight Top 20 units. They return an elite corner duo but lose their top four linebackers and both All-Big Ten defensive linemen.

The staff brought three impact starters with them from the Utah defense including first-team All- American John Henry Daley who was leading the nation in sacks at the time of his Week 11 injury. He should be back for fall camp and will pick up the pass rush role from the departing Derrick Moore. Utah’s starting tackle Jonah Lea’ea joins Trey Pierce on the interior. Veteran Cameron Brandt was the third end last year, and this room was pumped with four Top100 freshmen: Titan Davis, Alister Vallejo, Nate Marshall (2025) and five-star Carter Meadows.

It’s a complete restart at linebacker as the All-Big Ten trio of Jimmy Rolder, Ernest Hausmann, and Jaishawn Barham are all gone. Even worse, their backer of the future Cole Sullivan transferred out to Oklahoma. Redshirt freshman Nathaniel Owusu-Boateng was a Top200 prospect and could start alongside FCS standout Nathaniel Staehling (North Dakota State).

Whittingham says they will be in nickel 90% of snaps, and they are fully loaded with an all-league corner pair of Zeke Berry and Jyaire Hill joined by Utah’s Smith Snowden at the nickel. Snowden was graded a four-star transfer, was second-team All-Big 12 and the staff even used him on offense with 21 touches for 100 yards. Three-time captain Rod Moore is back at safety but has not had a full healthy season since 2023. The other safety spot is open for either Chris Bracy (Memphis) or a wildcard in near-five-star athlete Salesi Moa who brings 10.7 sprinter speed and was getting receiver reps in the spring game.

pick_six_2026.outlook: Heupel’s got another Top 25 team here, but to move up to the Playoff tier there are two major uncertainties for 2026. Jim Knowles is one of the best defensive minds in the sport, but his complex scheme usually takes a few seasons to start paying dividends. Second, the quarterback battle, where both guys are young and inexperienced – but super-talented – and Heupel has never had an issue getting his signal-callers up to speed.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Tennessee already had plenty of newcomers to their starting lineup heading into 2025. Then their five-star quarterback played contract hardball and left them after spring.

A transition season, plus the top drama/distraction of the entire offseason. That would normally be enough to sink any team but Josh Heupel still churned out another Top 10 offense and an eight-win season. Tennessee beat their unranked opponents, lost to four ranked teams but the 44-41 Georgia overtime loss and 33-27 Oklahoma loss were toss-ups.

Despite missing spring ball as a late transfer, Joey Aguilar picked up the offensive scheme and finished with the third-highest passing season in school history (3,565 yards). He led two late touchdown drives to beat Mississippi State, helped survive an Arkansas upset bid, and delivered Tennessee’s first win in The Swamp since 2003.

One pass shifted the Alabama game and passed the cigars back to Tide fans. Aguillar’s throw at the goal-line just before halftime would have made it a three-point game, but it was picked off and returned 100 yards the other way for a 14-point swing.

The three losses to eventual Playoff teams held them back from a return bid themselves. But then the season-finale blowout loss by Vanderbilt – in Knoxville – shifted the season’s legacy.

Sometimes progress isn’t linear. After stacking years of improvement and punching their first Playoff ticket in 2024, 2025 was a roster transition and step backwards.

Heupel moved quickly and fired longtime defensive coordinator Tim Banks and then hired one of the best in the sport: Jim Knowles.

The youth and inexperience of 2025 pays dividends into 2026 with 14 starters back, plus the #4 recruiting class of 2026, a Top 25 transfer haul, and arguably the top coordinator hire of the entire cycle.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Aguilar exceeded all expectations and finished second in the SEC in QB Rating behind only Heisman runner-up Diego Pavia. He lost an appeal for a bonus year of eligibility, so now the starting quarterback job is up for grabs in fall camp.

6’6 George MacIntyre was a Top200 recruit (#13 QB) in 2025 and despite having the full extra year of practice within the Heupel scheme, he emerged from spring in a virtual tie with true freshman Faizon Brandon. The 6’4 Brandon was a five-star signee, the #3 QB and #10 overall recruit. Per practice reports, Brandon won the scrimmages, MacIntyre won the spring game, but Brandon flashed that five-star upside. After seeing how well Aguilar picked up the offense in just a few months, the inexperience of Brandon is less of a hurdle and I think he’ll eventually win the job.

Eight of the other ten starters are back from an offense that averaged 40 points/game and finished #14 in my per-play, opponent-adjusted stat.

That includes four full-time starting offensive linemen in a total boomerang from last preseason when they had to find four new starters. As a new line, they still ranked in the Top 40 of both my OL Run Push and Pass Protection stats and now they return as veterans. David Sanders was the #1 lineman recruit and rounded into form down the stretch as a true freshman. Sanders has All-SEC potential even as a true sophomore this fall. Wendell Moe graded out well at guard, and center Sam Pendleton and guard Jesse Perry both started all year. The lone departure was Lance Heard who was third-team All-SEC but surprised and left for Kentucky. Tennessee added two Power 4 linemen to compete for that vacancy: former four-star Ory Williams (LSU) and Donovan Haslam (West Virginia).

DeSean Bishop emerged from a crowded rotation to lead with 1,076 yards and 16 scores. The former walk-on was a high school legend at Karns, TN and earned second-team All-SEC. The other two Peyton Lewis and Star Thomas are gone, so Bishop is projected to go over a thousand yards again.

Heupel doesn’t rotate his receivers. The key to his offense is finding three legit receiving weapons, and making the defense “pick its poison” – you can’t cover all three at once. Chris Brazzell, Braylon Staley, and Mike Matthews were the big three last year and they each had breakout games. Brazzell was the leader and went pro, but SEC Freshman of the Year Staley and Matthews are back after combining for

1,650 yards and 10 scores. Heupel has three blue-chippers to choose from for the third spot: Radarious Jackson, Top100 Travis Smith, and five-star TK Keys (Hattiesburg, MS) who was ranked the #1 receiver in the entire 2026 class.

It’s another top duo at tight end with a pair of former Top100’s DaSaahn Brame and returning starter Ethan Davis.

Last offseason Heupel and offensive coordinator Joey Halzle tinkered with their scheme a bit. We saw less of their super-wide, sideline-to-sideline spread formations, and instead it was more bunched and way more throws over the middle of the field. They showed the ability to adapt and still churned out an elite passing attack. Heupel’s got as good a track record as you’ll find.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Tennessee fell from the Top 10 to #50 of 68 Power 4 on defense. They regressed in all 17 of my stat categories but the 45-point, 582-yard collapse against Vanderbilt was the final straw.

Knowles is as proven as anybody and has built dominant defenses at Duke, Oklahoma State, and Ohio State. He’s led six straight Top 40 defenses with three ranking in the Top 10. The 2021 Oklahoma State unit led the nation in sacks, while 2024 Ohio State led in several categories en route to a national title.

He runs a complex, 4-2-5 base scheme with three safeties that take away the quarterback’s ability to make pre-snap reads and adjustments. Normally his scheme needs a full year or two to become elite, though this time around he brought several staffers from his 2025 Penn State defense with him and the install seems ahead-of-schedule. Per co-coordinator Anthony Poindexter: “we’re light years ahead of a year ago.”

It also helps that Knowles brought Penn State starters with him, including his so-called “quarterback of the defense” middle backer Amare Campbell. In total, Tennessee returns six starters, added two Penn State starters, plus three more Power 4 starting defensive backs.

The linebacker room is stacked. All-SEC Arion Carter decided to forgo the early NFL bid and returned for a final season, Edwin Spillman led the team with 81 tackles and earned SEC All-Freshman, and Jeremiah Telander returns as a two-year starter. Throw in Campbell and this is

absolutely packed.

Original starting corners Rickey Gibson and Jermod McCoy were knocked out with injuries but Colton Hood and true freshman Ty Redmond both stepped up to earn All-SEC honors. Redmond is back as a top corner, and the staff added Auburn starter Kayin Lee who earned a four-star transfer grade. Edrees Farooq returns at one safety spot, TJ Metcalf (Michigan) and Qua Moss (Kansas State) are both Power 4 starters, and DeJuan Lane followed the staff from Penn State.

Two starters are back on the line with tackle Daevin Hobbs and end Tyree Weathersby. Then Knowles brought a Penn State starter with him in four-star transfer Xavier Gilliam who was ranked the #7 transfer tackle.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
It feels strange placing Alabama this low in the SEC projection. I launched Pick Six Previews in 2012 amidst the Saban dynasty, and no Alabama team has had this many preseason question-marks: the lines of scrimmage, school-worst run game, and star players transferring out.

Alabama placed #14 in Game Grader (#6 in SEC) last year due to four one-score survival wins, and the 2026 team looks
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
After a shocking loss at Florida State in the opener, Alabama refocused and rattled off eight straight wins to keep their playoff hopes alive.

They did so in historic fashion, too. First, Alabama went Between the Hedges and snapped Georgia’s nation-best 33-game home win streak. Then the defense forced two key Diego Pavia turnovers in the 30-14 win. Alabama then snapped the second-longest home win streak at Missouri thanks to a fourth-and-goal touchdown pass from Ty Simpson to Daniel Hill. Cigar smoke returned to Bryant-Denny Stadium after Zabien Brown took back a 99-yard game-changing Pick Six to beat Tennessee.

Four straight weeks, four ranked opponents, four wins – the first in SEC history to do so.

The team’s motto was “unbreakable” and in so many one-score, tight finishes they lived up to it.

Though they lost by two to Oklahoma, and lost the SEC title rematch with Georgia, Alabama’s run of ranked wins was enough of a resume boost to earn an at-large bid in the Playoff.

They also got a revenge matchup in Norman, and this time Alabama was the one forcing the turnovers and leading a 17-point comeback. Brown struck again, this time with a 50-yard Pick Six, and Tim Keenan blocked a punt to spark the win.

A roller-coaster of a season with severe highs and lows hit the proverbial rock bottom in the Rose Bowl quarterfinal. Not only did Indiana win, but they physically dominated Alabama – a taste of their own medicine that Nick Saban dished out for the past 15 years. It was stunning.

The 38-3 final was Alabama’s worst loss since 1998, and it leaves a confusing legacy for the 2025 team. The expectations for second-year Kalen DeBoer were “Playoff or Bust.” He hit that goal, but the five- touchdown gap in the quarterfinal showed that there is still another tier to build towards.

Once again, Alabama signed an elite recruiting class and the current four classes on the roster were: #1, #2, #3, #3. However there are other key categories in the Talent Acquisition game – transfers and roster retention – and both were below Dynasty-Tier standards this cycle.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Alabama fell to #14 in my overall ranking Game Grader, for their lowest finish since Saban’s transition season back in 2007. It snapped their incredible 17-year streak of Top 10 teams.

The most critical issue was the line of scrimmage. Alabama simply was unable to run the ball. They mustered up just 104 yards/game which ranked #125 in FBS and was actually the lowest output in program history since they began keeping stats in 1946.

And that was with a line that featured two NFL draft picks, three All-SEC nominees, and five-stars packing the two-deep. The line was #118 in OL Run Push, and the per-carry average was even worse at #126.

The three top backs all averaged under four yards/carry and starter Jam Miller is off to the pros. Four Top100 backs will battle for carries with the veterans Daniel Hill and Kevin Riley joined by AK Dear and incoming five-star EJ Crowell (Jackson, AL) who ran for 300 yards in the state title game.

As for the offensive line? Four starters are gone and more reserves transferred out. The only starter returning is Michael Carroll, the nation’s #1 lineman of the 2025 class, who earned SEC All-Freshman last year at guard. Former four-star William Sanders moves up into the other guard spot. The rest of the line will look completely new with transfers and young blue-chippers. At center, Racin Delgatty (Cal Poly) emerged as a starter in spring ball but is making the jump from the FCS to the SEC. Jayvin James (Mississippi State) is an experienced SEC starting tackle and Top100 redshirt freshman Jackson Lloyd was named the top left tackle early in spring. Two more Top100 2025 transfers pack the room: Nick Brooks (Texas) and Ty Haywood (Michigan).

Simpson passed for 3,567 yards, 28 touchdowns and just five picks, led all those close wins, and delivered the program’s first Playoff win since 2021. He waited his time in Tuscaloosa and it paid off with a first- round selection. A quarterback battle between Austin Mack and Keelon Russell will extend into fall camp.

Mack has an additional year in this scheme having played for DeBoer and coordinator Ryan Grubb at Washington, and brings a 6’6 pocket passer frame. Five-star Keelon Russell was Alabama’s highest-rated quarterback commit, has elite athleticism and makes highlight-reel throws off-schedule. With uncertainties along the line in front of them, look for Russell’s elusive, scrambler skillset to eventually win him the job.

Leading receiver Germie Bernard went pro, touchdown-leader Isaiah Horton transferred out to Texas A&M, but Alabama returns a proven one-two punch with Ryan Williams and Lotzeir Brooks. They combined for 81 catches and 1,130 yards last year and were set to be joined by four-star transfer Noah Rogers (NC State) but a knee injury put his season in question. Instead, a pair of Top100 freshmen emerged at A-Day and both have 6’4 frames: Derek Meadows and Cederian Morgan.

Starting tight end Josh Cuevas was drafted and now three guys are rotating. Kaleb Edwards earned SEC All-Freshman last year, Marshall Pritchett is a threat in the pass game, and Josh Ford (Oklahoma State) was a Power 4 starter.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Kane Wommack’s defense ranked #21 in my opponent-adjusted rankings and made game-changing plays to earn the Playoff bid. However, the lasting memory was watching Indiana physically dominate and out- rush them by 200+ yards.

Fixing the run defense is the top priority, though they will have to do so with just one starter back in the front seven. All three defensive line starters are gone after LT Overton and Tim Keenan went pro and James Smith transferred out to Ohio State. Two more in the two-deep departed: Jordan Renaud (Ole Miss) and five-star Keon Keeley (Notre Dame).

The staff hit the portal and brought in USC starter Devan Thompkins and South Carolina’s third end Desmond Umeozulu. At tackle, London Simmons is a rising star who earned SEC All-Freshman last year. Terrance Green (Oregon) earned four-star transfer grades, Edric Hill is a former Top200 prospect, and Jeremiah Beaman is back from injury.

Both starting inside backers Justin Jefferson and Deontae Lawson are gone, and so is their top backup.

Three-star Caleb Woodson (Virginia Tech) was an ACC starter and takes over one spot, while Cayden Jones and incoming five-star Xavier Griffin battle for the other one.

Former five-star Yhonzae Pierre emerged as a top pass rusher last year and returns at the outside backer, edge hybrid role. Qua Russaw left for Ohio State, but Alabama hopes to get back Jah-Marien Latham for a seventh season. Top100 Justin Hill got plenty of snaps here as a true freshman.

The secondary returns almost intact and is the clear strength of the 2026 team. Dijon Lee earned SEC All-Freshman and Mr. Pick Six Zabien Brown returns at the other corner. Both starting safeties are back with All-American Bray Hubbard and Keon Sabb. And then another round of five-stars pack the two-deep with an embarrassment of riches: Jorden Edmonds, Zavier Mincey, and Jireh Edwards.

pick_six_2026.outlook: Following their breakthrough 12-win season, BYU doubled down on roster retention and kept all ten All-Big 12 players that were eligible to return for 2026. No departing star players to the transfer portal. In fact they even added the #1 linebacker transfer to stack the defense even more. BYU’s program culture is rock solid, the lines of scrimmage are stout, and now their big quarterback gets a
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
BYU’s 2025 season outlook was called into question just weeks before kickoff when their returning starting quarterback was suspended and forced out. Instead, the keys to the offense were handed to a true freshman that spent spring ball at Stanford.

The 6’2, 230-pound Bear Bachmeier didn’t look or play like a freshman. The first opposing head coach called him a “centaur” in the postgame after the 69-0 blowout.

The offense scored in a nation-best 27 straight quarters to start the season, and BYU survived one-score tests beating Colorado by three and Arizona by six in double overtime. Bachmeier became a legend in the final minutes of the Holy War as he powered in for the decisive 22-yard touchdown while carrying three Utes with him into the endzone. As ESPN’s Jason Benetti put it, “there’s a bear on the loose in Provo!”

The 2025 team grew into one of the school’s best ever. They went 11-1 in the regular season, lost to Texas Tech in Lubbock and then again in the Big 12 title game, but with the Pop-Tarts Bowl win they got to 12 wins for just the fifth time ever. This time, it was against a Power 4 conference

and it was unquestionably the hardest schedule BYU has ever faced.

Just three years removed from independence, BYU had the breakthrough season in 2024 and now in 2025 they established staying power as a Big 12 contender.

Kalani Sitake’s two-year record of 23-4 is the second-best in program history, only behind their 1984 national title run. He was targeted by Penn State in their head coaching search but Sitake remained loyal to BYU and even got a significant boost to roster funding.

While Texas Tech has been dominating the transfer portal, BYU put their chips on high school recruiting and player retention – and they went two for two. BYU signed a record eight four-star prospects and the class earned a program-high #21 national ranking (#2 in Big 12). Then they successfully retained all available returning starters and did so with a coordinator departing for a blueblood school. 17 starters earned some form of Big 12 honors – 10 returned, 7 graduated, and zero transferred out.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Bachmeier went on to win Big 12 Freshman of the Year with 3,033 passing yards, 527 rushing yards, and 26 total touchdowns. He was the only true freshman in America to post 3,500+ total yards and flipped the program’s biggest preseason uncertainty into a strength. Look for a second-year starter bonus here, especially since he’ll actually get spring ball in Provo this time. In terms of efficiency, Bachmeier placed eighth in the Big 12 in QB Rating but ranked in the top five in completion percentage (65%) and yards/attempt (7.8).

BYU signed near-five star Ryder Lyons, the #5 quarterback of the 2026 class, though he is serving on a mission this year.

BYU has their “Bear” under center but also got back their workhorse at running back. LJ Martin returns after winning Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year and rushing for a league-high 1,305 yards. He did so after suffering a shoulder injury that eventually required offseason surgery, and still averaged 100 yards/game after the injury. He should push for All-America consideration in 2026 and has a shot at catching Jamaal Williams for the school’s career rushing title.

Three pass-catchers earned All-Big 12 honors and all three are gone. Chase Roberts and tight end Carsen Ryan graduated, then Parker Kingston was expelled after a felony charge. Jojo Phillips and Cody Hagen are experienced veterans but the staff leveraged the transfer portal here. They signed three former four-star recruits: 6’6 Kyler Kasper (Oregon) and tight ends Walker Lyons (USC) and Roger Saleapaga (Oregon). Kasper and Saleapaga were stuck in a crowded NFL factory at Oregon, but former Top100 Lyons was a co-starter for USC last year. BYU signed two more Top200 four- stars Ty Goettsche and Brock Harris (out on mission) to complete the reload at tight end.

Offensive line coach TJ Woods did it again. BYU again placed in the Top 40 of both OL Run Push (#38) and Pass Protection (#18) allowing a sack on just 4% of attempts. Sitake and Woods have built an impressive physical force when you combine the line with two bulldozers Bachmeier and Martin in the backfield.

Three starters are gone but BYU returns a pair of all-league linemen. Bruce Mitchell is the headliner after first-team honors at center, Andrew Gentry is back at right tackle, and the staff added in three transfers with starting experience: Paki Finau (Washington), Zak Yamauchi (Stanford), and Jr Sia (Utah State). Finau is a former four-star who coaches named the starting left tackle after spring. Overall the line is veteran with five redshirt seniors in the two-deep.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Longtime Utah head coach Kyle Whittingham took the Michigan job and ended up pulling BYU defensive coordinator Jay Hill with him. Hill’s impact on the defense was one of the best coordinator turnarounds over the past few years and helped BYU find its footing at the Power 4 level.

Sitake promoted Kelly Poppinga from within, and the alum says he’s got influences from Bronco Mendenhall and Hill, noting “I’d be an idiot to change much of what we’re doing.” That’s wise, given BYU’s consecutive Top 25 finishes in my opponent-adjusted defensive rankings.

Usually a departing coordinator is able to pull some starters with him, but not here. Poppinga said he was on the phone non-stop, 12 hours per day, calling every player and keeping the lineup together.

Six All-Big 12 defenders are back – BYU suffered no significant transfer hits – and they even went out and signed the #1 linebacker transfer this cycle in All-ACC Cade Uluave.

Uluave posted 100 tackles, 12 for loss, and is a legit All-America candidate for 2026. Two-year star Jack Kelly graduated and went pro, but do-it-all Isaiah Glasker returns. Uluave and Glasker form a top linebacker duo.

BYU retained their anchor Keanu Tanuvasa, the 6’4 300-pounder who came over from Utah. He earned All-Big 12 honors last year and as Poppinga said, “he elevated everything.” BYU does lose two starting linemen John Taumoepeau and end Logan Lutui but the rest of the two-deep is back. They also get back former Oklahoma State nose tackle Justin Kirkland who redshirted and is another space-eater. Bodie Schoonover and Tausili Akana round out the top rotation.

Tanner Wall earned first-team All-Big 12 in his final season, but BYU returns Faletau Satuala who actually grabbed some All-America praise after leading the team in tackles and taking back a key Pick Six in the Iowa State comeback win. Their top cover corner Evan Johnson is back after tying for the league lead with five picks. Two more starters are back with corner Therrian Alexander and safety Raider Damuni. BYU was in the Top 25 in all three opponent-adjusted categories – overall, passing, and rushing – but the pass defense was the strength at #13.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Washington ranked in the Top 20 on both sides of the ball last year -- #15 overall in Game Grader – and did so with a young lineup. Now they return as a veteran two-deep and join a crowded field of contenders for a Big Ten title spot.

Demond Williams is the X-Factor. He is my third-team All-Big Ten selection, and if he can start to shine against ranked teams, Washington can unlock a higher tier.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Ohio State snapped Washington’s 22-game home win streak in Husky Stadium, and then Maryland jumped out to a 20-0 lead the next week. In danger of an 0-2 league start in Jedd Fisch’s second season, Washington flipped the switch.

Over their final four drives Washington gained 300 yards and scored 24 points, and held Maryland scoreless, to lead the massive fourth-quarter comeback win. The offense exploded by scoring 38+ points in their other four Big Ten wins, and former Purdue head coach Ryan Walters led an improved defense.

It was a strong, balanced season with Washington placing in the Top 20 of both my opponent-adjusted offense and defense rankings – plus a #15 finish in Game Grader. Only five other programs pulled that off in 2025.

The best part? They pulled off the nine-win season with an extremely young two-deep.

Fisch jump-started the transition in 2024 with a heavy transfer class that featured several of his top Arizona players. But in 2025 and 2026 the focus has shifted to the high school ranks and Washington has now landed back-to-back Top 25 recruiting classes. This 2026 class surged all the way up to #13 nationally – a UW record.

The next step in the program build is unlocking another gear against Playoff-tier opponents. Washington got within a score in the fourth quarter each time but failed to finish in crunch time.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Demond Williams’ stat line shows the contrast. In the nine wins, Williams threw 22 touchdowns and just two picks, but in the four losses he threw three touchdowns to six picks – including the 3-INT meltdown against Michigan. Of course, the stats in wins would be expected to look better. But when comparing the Big Ten quarterbacks, Williams ranked #2 in QB Rating in the “wins only” category, and all the way down at #12 in “losses only.”

Still, it was undoubtedly a successful season for his first full year as a starter. In addition to placing fourth in QB Rating, Williams also led Big Ten quarterbacks in rushing with 611 yards. In the Rutgers win, he became just the 16th FBS quarterback to post a 400-yard passing, 100-yard rushing dual-threat game.

After the 2024 bowl game, Fisch called Williams the “face of the program,” and after the 2025 bowl win he signed a contract to remain at UW. Two days later, Williams attempted to enter the transfer portal and it appeared headed to a precedent-setting court case, but then ultimately he returned to UW.

With so much talent and production back for 2026, the surprising loss of their star quarterback would have derailed a promising season.

Instead, Williams gets a second-year starter bonus and assuming he takes some steps forward against ranked teams, he could enter the Heisman discussion.

The offensive line improved by 50 spots in my OL Run Push from 2024 to 2025, and now four starters return up front. Left tackle Carver Willis is the lone loss. John Mills earned the starting left guard spot as a true freshman and fittingly earned Freshman All-America honors. The Hatchett brothers are back at center and guard, and right tackle Drew Azzopardi improved in his second season. The staff signed two top linemen to battle for the open left tackle spot in five-star Kodi Greene (Mater Dei, CA) and four-star transfer Kolt Dieterich (Sam Houston).

Denzel Boston was a pure #1 receiver and was selected in the second round. He will be missed, but this room is packed with young talent. As a freshman, Dezmen Roebuck finished #2 with 42 catches for 560 yards and 7 scores, and there are six four-stars competing for spots in the rotation. Chris Lawson and Justice Williams were 2025 signees, and three more Top200’s are on their way with Mason James, Jordan Clay, and Trez Davis. The staff signed Bodpegn Miller (Ohio State) who was

a Top200 signee in the 2025 class, along with Kennesaw State’s #2 target Christian Moss. And don’t forget Rashid Williams who was originally a starter lost to injury in September.

Jonah Coleman went for 1,100 total yards and 17 touchdowns in his final season. When he was injured in November, Adam Mohammed shined with consecutive 100-yard games but he transferred out to California. Former four-star Jordan Washington has top-notch explosiveness but suffered a severe injury in spring and is doubtful. The staff signed another four-star Jayden Limar (Oregon) and Power 4 vet Trey Cooley.

Fisch called Quentin Moore the best blocking tight end he’s ever coached. That’s a big loss, but top receiving threat Decker DeGraaf returns after placing third on the team with 32 catches and 360 yards. Kade Eldridge missed half the season but returns and should help with the blocking role.
pick_six_2026.defense:
When Steve Belichick left to coach with his dad at UNC, Fisch hired Ryan Walters and the move paid off. Washington improved from 88th to 15th in rushing yards/carry, remained a strong pass defense, and finished 16th of 68 Power 4 in my overall opponent-adjusted ranking.

There shouldn’t be a drop off in 2026 as the back seven remains elite.

The uncertainty lies in the trenches where two starters graduated and another five rotational linemen transferred out to Power 4 programs. Elinneus Davis was the most consistent and he returns as the anchor at nose tackle. The tackle and end spots will be fall camp battles between transfers and incoming blue-chip recruits. Kai McClendon (Mississippi State) played in 12 games as a true freshman but then missed the 2025 season with a knee injury, and Darin Conley was a starter for Ball State. They will compete with a pair of incoming Top200 recruits in Derek Colman- Brusa (Kennedy Catholic, WA) and JD Hill (Mission Viejo, CA).

Zach Durfee graduated but co-sack leader Jacob Lane returns at edge. Two former starters are back from injuries in Isaiah Ward and Russell Davis.

The linebacker room is overflowing with star power and is the strength of the defense. Jacob Manu should push for All-Big Ten, Xe’Ree Alexander surged at the end of the year to finish second with 70 tackles, and Taariq Al-Uqdah was an original starter back from injury. Former Top100 super-recruit Zaydrius Rainey-Sale is a wildcard the staff can use at backer and off the edge on passing downs.

Washington had the tallest corner duo in the nation last year, and even though both Tacario Davis and Ephesians Prysock are out of eligibility, they will remain tall again here with another top duo. Dylan Robinson is a former Top200 who started five games last year as a true freshman, and Emmanuel Karnley (Virginia) was an ACC starter – both are 6’3. Defensive MVP Alex McLaughlin is back at safety after he led the team in tackles and scored on a Pick Six and a fumble return. Rahshawn Clark is back at nickel, and four-star Rylon Dillard-Allen takes over at free safety.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Louisville joined national runner-up Miami as the only ACC teams to place in the Top 25 of both my opponent- adjusted Offense and Defense rankings. They were painfully close to an ACC title breakthrough, but now Brohm has his best roster yet.

The staff excelled in the transfer portal again and now Louisville ranks in the ACC top three in every position unit ranking except quarterback, but few coaches can match Brohm’s track record developing signal-callers. Louisville faces only one of the ACC’s top six, and is my pick to play Miami in the ACC title game.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Jeff Brohm made it three-in-a-row at his alma mater: three transfer quarterbacks, three 9-win seasons.

But this time Louisville did it with defense and a run game.

Ron English’s defense made drastic improvements, especially against the pass, and Louisville finished ranked in the national Top 40 in all 17 of my defensive stat categories. They joined Oregon as the only units to do so.

That pass defense made the difference by picking off Carson Beck four times in Louisville’s 24-21 win over #2 Miami for their second Top 2 win in program history (2016 FSU). The statement win helped push Louisville up as high as #15 in the polls.

Instead of his usual pass-heavy scheme, Brohm doubled down on the run game with his trio of explosive running backs and they finished with the #7 rushing attack in my opponent-adjusted numbers. Even with the roster crushed with injuries, Louisville lined up and powered the ball between the tackles in their 41-0 destruction of rival Kentucky.

It was a nice consolation prize for a season that had several missed opportunities separating Louisville from a potential ACC title spot in such a wide-open league race.

Their first three losses came by a combined seven points. Louisville gave away two defensive touchdowns to Virginia in the 30-27 overtime loss, lost another overtime game to California 29-26, and then held Clemson to 1/13 on third downs but blew it late 20-19 with a run of self- inflicted penalties.

Brohm now has eight one-score losses in his three seasons, but opponent-adjusted Game Grader shows just how close they are to a breakthrough: 2nd in the ACC (2023), 4th (2024), and 3rd (2025).

The staff has excelled in talent acquisition and this 2026 transfer haul has Louisville reloaded for perhaps Brohm’s best roster yet.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Miller Moss posted an average passing season – 10th in the ACC in both yards/attempt and QB Rating – but struggled in crunch time. His sack-turned Pick Six cost them the Virginia loss, and then in the three-game November stretch he threw just one touchdown. Explosiveness was missing from the pass game and Louisville dropped 90 spots year-over-year in long-yardage passing.

Brohm went back to the portal for a fourth-straight transfer quarterback but this is the first one without Power 4 starting experience. Louisville signed Lincoln Kienholz (Ohio State) who spent his freshman seasons backing up Kyle McCord and Will Howard, and then lost the fall camp competition to Julian Sayin in 2025.

Stuck in a crowded NFL quarterback room, he comes to Louisville with minimal game experience but last year in blowouts he showed off a strong arm, good reads in the RPO game, mobility in the pocket, and even some strength in QB power runs. The former Top200 high school recruit brings the most athletic skillset that Brohm has had here.

Louisville lost their top four receivers including the productive All-ACC duo of Chris Bell and Caullin Lacy (1,552 combined receiving yards) but they reloaded with highly-touted transfers for Kienholz to throw to.

They signed a one-two punch with speedster Tre Richardson (Vanderbilt) and Lawayne McCoy (Florida State) who were both graded as four-star transfers. Richardson led Vanderbilt with 806 receiving yards and seven touchdowns and also ranked #7 in the SEC in yards after catch. Both guys should help fix the offense’s lack of explosive pass plays. TreyShun Hurry returns as the third receiver.

Brody Foley (Tulsa) earned first-team All-AAC honors and was ranked the #4 transfer tight end. Another four-star, Foley will be a mismatch nightmare and will pair up well with returning starter Jaleel Skinner.

The running back room was the strength of the offense last year and two of the three return for 2026. Isaac Brown was a 2024 Freshman All-American and was off to an insane pace in 2025 with an 8.6 per-carry average and five 100+ yard games in the first eight. He was injured but then Keyjuan Brown stepped up and averaged a high 7.3 per carry. Both Brown’s are back, and the staff added a Top200 recruit in redshirt freshman Marquise Davis (Missouri).

Three multi-year starting offensive linemen graduated – center Pete Nygra and tackles Rasheed Miller and Trevonte Sylvester – and the staff hit the portal hard. Eryx Daugherty (Boston College) and Cason Henry (South Carolina) are both Power 4 starters with a combined 25 starts while Anwar O’Neal (Delaware) and Johnnie Brown (Georgia Southern) were all-league linemen at the non-AQ level. All-ACC honorable mention guard Lance Robinson is the lone returning starter.
pick_six_2026.defense:
The staff hit home runs in the transfer portal last cycle and it paid off with an elite pass rush, #11 pass defense, and #19 overall defense per my opponent-adjusted numbers. Coordinator Ron English stepped down for family reasons and Brohm hired from within, elevating cornerbacks coach Steve Ellis and defensive line coach Mark Ivey to be co-coordinators. They will continue the 4-2-5 scheme that has worked here.

Their pass rush duo of Clev Lubin and AJ Green combined for 12.5 sacks and 19.5 tackles-for-loss. Both return, and while Wesley Bailey graduated, the staff backfilled with Tyler Thompson (UNC) who placed in the ACC’s top ten in sacks last year. The ends are a clear strength, but they lost three tackles: Rene Konga, Jordan Guerad, and Jerry Lawson (Oklahoma State). They added three Power 4 transfers and Demeco Kennedy (Purdue) got huge spring praise from Brohm.

There are no question marks at linebacker, as they return a top unit for 2026. TJ Quinn graduates

after leading the team in tackles for three straight seasons, but the other three are back including All-ACC Antonio Watts, veteran Stanquan Clark, and TJ Capers who had the game-sealing pick against Miami.

Tayon Holloway had two picks in the Kentucky win and also earned All-ACC honors as a lockdown corner. The other starting spots in the secondary are up for grabs, but again, the staff pumped in highly-touted transfers. Koen Entringer (Iowa) was ranked a Top 10 safety transfer, and Kaleb Beasley (Tennessee) and TJ Banks (Ole Miss) are former Top200 recruits. DJ Waller (Kentucky) is projected to start at the other corner spot and he brings several years of Power 4 experience.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Campbell finally left Iowa State and brought 13 starters with him to Happy Valley. It’s a roster transfusion, as most of the 2025 Penn State star power went pro or transferred out.

They get a schedule boost by avoiding the Playoff trio and instead draw five of the bottom seven. The talent level is
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
James Franklin was fired despite a 104-45 (.698) overall record at Penn State. By my count, only nine other coaches in college football history were fired with .700+ win percentages at their school.

From the Penn State mindset, 2025 was the year. This was “National Title or Bust.”

The school-record 2022 signing class were experienced seniors, they were fresh off a Playoff semifinal appearance, the vast majority of the starting lineup returned, and they added in two of the top coordinators in the sport.

Franklin helped rebuild the program post-sanctions, won a Big Ten title, earned three New Year’s Six bowl invites, and made it one throw away from a national title appearance. Still two hurdles blocked his program from reaching the “elite” tier: Top 10 opponents (4-21) and Ohio State (1-10).

So this was it, 2025 was the year to break through. It had to be.

After a 3-0 start, Penn State lost an overtime battle against #6 Oregon in front of a 111,000+ White Out. While it was a gut punch, all team goals were still intact heading into October. But then Penn State lost to a winless, coach-less UCLA team, and then got out-muscled by Northwestern. Per Chris Fallica, they became the first

team ever to lose consecutive games as 20+ point favorites.

The 0-3 start to Big Ten play – in this, the Title or Bust season – was enough for athletic director Pat Kraft to pull the plug and fire Franklin there in October.

His legacy remains positive, after helping return the program to the national stage, bring in an elevated level of recruits, and help secure the $700 million facilities upgrade. But it was clear that his program plateaued, albeit at an “almost elite” level that most other schools would be ecstatic about.

After a 50+ day coaching search, Penn State surprised with one of the most sought-after coaches in college football: Iowa State’s Matt Campbell. He inherited a broken program in Ames but built them into winners. The 2024 team was Iowa State’s first-ever double-digit win season, he won Big 12 Coach of the Year three times, and walks away as the school’s winningest coach.

Campbell became a popular target in the annual coaching carousel, but he declined the offers one by one over the years. Penn State must have been on his short list. He calls Penn State “one of the blue bloods of college football, and the program’s history and tradition are unmatched.”
pick_six_2026.offense:
With a budget that Campbell said was “a fourth” of the top Big 12 spenders, he made up ground with top- notch player development and innovative schemes. Over his whole tenure at Iowa State, they signed just eight four-star commits, but he and his staff were able to develop 16, twice as many, into NFL draft picks.

Campbell brought his offensive coordinator Taylor Mouser with him, along with 13 starters off his 2025 Iowa State team that went 8-4. Mouser gets to run it back with his starting quarterback, workhorse running back, top two receivers, and top two tight ends from last year.

With Drew Allar off to the pros, and Ethan Grunkemeyer following Franklin to Virginia Tech, it’s a new quarterback room. Rocco Becht transferred in from Iowa State where he started for three years, showed off elusiveness in the pocket, and had a penchant for late fourth-quarter winning drives. His playing style will remind Penn State fans of Trace McSorley.

Becht enters 2026 as one of the most experienced quarterbacks in Power 4 – second in career yardage and third in passing touchdowns – and brings those years of scheme knowledge. His deep ball is excellent, but he’ll need to hit the shorter lay-ups with more consistency. The skillset is a perfect fit for Mouser’s offense which establishes a power run game but then takes vertical passing shots more frequently than most.

The record-breaking duo at running back graduated but they left their mark. Kaytron Allen broke the all- time rushing yardage record (4,180) and earned All-American honors while Nicholas Singleton set the all-time touchdown mark (45). The staff brought their two-year starter Carson Hansen, who averaged 100+ yards per game last year and earned All-Big 12 second-team. Hansen is a between-the-tackles workhorse, while bowl game star Quinton Martin and Top100 James Peoples (Ohio State) have home- run explosiveness.

Iowa State’s top two receivers also joined. Four-star transfer Chase Sowell has stacked three straight 500- yard seasons and was named Big 12 Newcomer last year, and Brett Eskildsen got league honors after leading Iowa State with 526 yards and five scores. Koby Howard is a former four-star in the third receiver role. This position has held back the Penn State offense for several years and it’s another restart after last year’s top four all departed.

Another position, another pair of Cyclones. Ben Brahmer was rated a four-star transfer as the #2 tight end this cycle after placing as a Mackey semifinalist, Gabe Burkle is a two-year starter, and together they are both 6’6 plus receiving threats up the seam. Penn State also returns former Top100 Andrew Rappleyea.

The offensive line was a disappointment after returning the starting five off a 2024 Top 10 line. Now four starters are gone – including first-round pick Vega Ioane – with Anthony Donkoh as the only returner. Donkoh is moving from guard to tackle, Cooper Cousins started the bowl game at guard, and a trio of former Top100 recruits are battling at tackle: Malachi Goodman, Garrett Sexton, and Owen Aliciene. The staff signed Brock Riker (Texas State) at center, and then four of their Iowa State linemen. All four had three-star transfer grades, but Trevor Buhr is a lock at guard after an All-Big 12 campaign last year.
pick_six_2026.defense:
The Jim Knowles experiment backfired last year. The top-rated defensive coordinator actually led a steep decline in his transition season, as Penn State fell from #1 in my opponent-adjusted defense rankings all the way to #31. They declined in all 17 of my stat categories and are restarting again for 2026.

Campbell’s Iowa State program was known for its unique defensive scheme, Jon Heacock’s 3-3-3 “Dime Stack” that confused Big 12 offenses for years. Heacock chose to retire, so Campbell pivoted to USC coordinator and Penn State alum D’Anton Lynn and his 4-3 base scheme.

Six defenders earned All-Big Ten honors and all six are gone. Instead, the staff signed seven starters off the Iowa State defense. The top five defensive tackles are gone, but the staff brought in plenty of 300- pound run-stuffers like the UCLA pair of Siale Taupaki and Keanu Williams. At end, Dani Dennis-Sutton went pro, two more transferred out with high grades, but four-star Max Granville returns and the staff

moved Lavar Arrington to the edge.

Tony Rojas is back after his season-ending injury in the Oregon loss, and the captain is joined by the three Iowa State starting backers. Kooper Ebel was a two-year starter at middle backer for ISU, Caleb Bacon was rated a four-star transfer at outside backer, and Cael Brezina packs the two-deep.

Penn State retained their interim head coach Terry Smith, and the move allowed them to keep cornerback Audavion Collins, nickel Zion Tracy, and Daryus Dixson who surged up the depth chart as a true freshman causing two veterans to transfer out. Their top three safeties left, and again, the staff brought three safeties from Ames: Marcus Neal, Jeremiah Cooper and Jamison Patton. Neal is the headliner as a four-star transfer with Big 12 honorable mention, but they are all in new roles due to the scheme change.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Lashlee is leveling up the roster talent from the high school ranks, and each year of development it will pay off more and more. SMU is on an upward trajectory but in the short-term, there are some obstacles in 2026: a double coordinator change, and the loss of nine of their 12 All-ACC stars.

Jennings is a Heisman darkhorse, he’s got plenty of weapons to throw to and a stout line blocking for him. SMU is a legit ACC title contender but the talent drain on defense, as well as the loss of ace coordinator Symons, keeps them in the #3 spot.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
In 2024 SMU moved back up to the Power 4 level, ending a decades-long rebuild from their crippling NCAA sanctions. They became the first program ever to move up and post an 8-0 regular season in their new league, and then came a field goal short from winning the ACC title game.

Far from a one-hit wonder, the 2025 team showed the program has staying power. SMU went into Clemson’s Death Valley and avenged the ACC title loss, gave their home fans a field-stormer by beating #10 Miami in overtime, and went into the final day of the season with a win-and-in scenario to another ACC title game.

SMU rallied from a 17-point deficit to take a late lead on California, but the Bears drove right down the field to steal back the win, leaving SMU on the bad end of a five-team title tiebreaker.

It was a missed opportunity, and along with the Baylor, TCU, and Wake Forest games, SMU held fourth-quarter leads in all their eventual losses.

Even though it ended without a return trip to Charlotte or another Playoff appearance, head coach Rhett Lashlee found plenty of positives – and rightfully so: “this senior class is special, they put SMU back on the national stage, and we’re just getting started.”

The seniors set a program record with 31 wins over three years and added SMU’s first ranked bowl win since the 1984 Aloha Bowl over Notre Dame. Along with the 2024 accolades, Lashlee’s comments are certainly backed up.

The on-field success is paying off in other areas too. Gerald Ford Stadium had the nation’s highest year-over-year boost in attendance from 2023 to 2024-25. Then they signed consecutive #32 ranked recruiting classes – 12 four-stars -- to set a program record in the modern recruiting era.
pick_six_2026.offense:
SMU retained their most important star in quarterback Kevin Jennings. The dual-threat gunslinger enters his third and final season as the starter. Simply put, he is a highlight reel and with him under center SMU can score on any given snap.

Jennings posted back-to-back 3,000+ yard seasons and placed in the ACC’s top five in QB Rating both times. In 2025, he cut down on his turnover-collapse games and did so despite suffering a leg injury that limited his mobility. When he gets back to 100% this fall, his elusiveness and speed add another element to his game, and he should contend for All-ACC honors.

He loses his top two targets with Jordan Hudson and Romello Brinson both graduating. Yamir Knight caught 54 balls for 637 yards last year and emerged over the second half of the season. Knight steps up as the featured receiver this fall and is joined by two impact transfers in four-star Yannick Smith (East Carolina) and Jalen Hale (Alabama) who was a former five-star recruit. Top200 Jalen Cooper impressed as a freshman last season, true freshman Aljour Miles got huge praise from Lashlee this spring, and SMU stocked the room with another round of young blue-chippers.

The staff has also stacked recruiting wins in the trenches, with four four-star linemen in the past two recruiting cycles. While the freshmen spend 2026 as a developmental growth year, SMU has a veteran starting five again.

First-team All-ACC guard Logan Parr leaves as a program legend, but the right side of the line is back. Right tackle PJ Williams is the star this season, center Joshua Bates also received ACC honors, and Addison Nichols returns at right guard. Alex Woods and Andrew Chamblee are projected starters on the left side, though Top100 Dramodd Odoms could push at left tackle as a redshirt freshman. They need some improvement in Offensive Line Run Push (#98) but landed another Top 25 rank in Pass Protection, even with a less-mobile Jennings in November.

SMU loses their one-two punch in the backfield with the physical TJ Harden graduating and the explosive Chris Johnson transferring out to Clemson. The staff signed California starter Kendrick

Raphael who grinded out a 900-yard season and ACC honorable mention despite getting no help from the #135 offensive line at Cal. Dramekco Green got experience in the bowl game, and versatile pass-threat Derrick McFall returns and may even get some reps in the slot.

All three tight ends depart, including All-ACC Matthew Hibner. The staff signed three Power 4 tight ends from the portal: Florida State starter Randy Pittman, four-star Theo Melin Ohrstrom (Texas A&M), and Trey Jackson (Texas Tech).

Offensive coordinator Casey Woods took the head coach job at Missouri State, and Lashlee promoted receivers coach Rob Likens. Lashlee is still the playcaller though, so there won’t be changes to the high-tempo spread offense. This should be a Top 15 offense again.
pick_six_2026.defense:
The coordinator change on this side is more uncertain. Over the past three-year average, SMU ranks #10 in my opponent-adjusted defense rankings and they lose mastermind Scott Symons to the NFL. Lashlee promoted internally here too – linebackers coach Maurice Crum and cornerbacks coach Rickey Hunley – but the loss of Symons is an uncertainty.

It doesn’t help losing six All-ACC stars. The entire starting defensive line is gone along with four starting defensive backs.

The linebacker trio returns as one of ACC’s best groups. Alex Kilgore is a proven star, Brandon Booker is ready for a breakout season, and former walk-on Brandon Miyazono continues to impress. The trio combined for 174 tackles, 11 for loss, and 3 picks.

Outside of the linebacker room it is a complete rebuild.

SMU allowed 283 pass yards/game, second-worst nationally, but from a per-play, efficiency perspective they checked in at #56 in QB Rating, and #34 of 68 Power 4 in my opponent-adjusted passing number. All-ACC stars Ahmaad Moses, Isaiah Nwokobia, and Deuce Harmon are all gone, and corner Marcellus Barnes is the only returning starter in the secondary. Jarvis Lee (USF) and All-AAC Jimmy Wyrick (UTSA) are three-star transfers projected as starters at nickel and safety.

There’s even more attrition up front with all four defensive linemen gone: Isaiah Smith, Jeffrey M’ba, Terry Webb, and Cam Robertson. SMU does get two original starters back from injury recoveries with former Liberty transfer Aakil Washington at edge, and Jonathan Jefferson finally back at tackle. Former Missouri transfer Jahkai Lang started four games at end here last year, and a pair of three-star transfers battle at tackle: Malcolm Alcorn-Crowder (Kansas State) and All-MAC Marques White (UMass).

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Normally the loss of all nine starting linemen would be enough to sink the season. But thanks to years of elite player development, Utah has a pipeline of linemen and they never lose their physicality edge. Even though Whittingham moved on, Scalley’s promotion means one thing: Utah is still Utah.

They also have the ultimate ace card at quarterback – the elusive Devon Dampier – and an upgraded receiver room. Despite all the changes, Utah remains in Big 12 title contention.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
After consecutive seasons were derailed by quarterback injuries and broken offenses, head coach Kyle Whittingham made a change and brought in the coordinator and quarterback duo from New Mexico’s top five offense.

Jason Beck led one of the biggest offensive turnarounds from 2024 to 2025, quarterback Devon Dampier thrived in the step up from non-AQ to Power 4, and Utah powered through the Big 12. They won five league games by 27+ points. Utah routed defending champs Arizona State 42-10, suffocated Cincinnati’s pass offense holding Brendan Sorsby to a 33% completion rate, and rolled up a 43-0 halftime lead on Colorado.

Though they came up short in the fourth quarters of their losses to Texas Tech and BYU, this was one of Whittingham’s strongest Utah teams, especially along the lines of scrimmage where seven of nine linemen earned All-Big 12 honors.

After 21 seasons leading the program, Whittingham stepped down after the season.

“I’m very grateful for the relationships forged with all the players that have proudly worn the drum and feather during our time here,” he said in his final presser. Whittingham led their BCS Buster undefeated team in 2008, beat Nick Saban’s Alabama team in the Sugar Bowl, and then led Utah through their promotion up to the Pac-12. Through consistent player development and a physical brand of football, he eventually led Utah to back-to- back Pac-12 title wins in 2021 and 2022.

His Utah program has been a mark of consistency, especially through the modern era of constant change: 18 winning seasons and eight 10+ win years.

Utah had planned for this eventual transition by naming long-time defensive coordinator Morgan Scalley as their “head coach in waiting” back in 2023. Scalley was an All-American safety on the 2004 undefeated BCS team and has coached here ever since.

Whittingham fully endorsed his successor: “Scalley is an exceptional football coach, a proven commodity, and he’s invested in this program as much as anybody ever has been.”
pick_six_2026.offense:
A few days after the announcement, Whittingham took the head coaching job at Michigan. The dominoes started falling as he brought key players and starters with him to Ann Arbor.

He also brought Beck, the mastermind of Utah’s overnight offensive fix. Utah ranked #63 and then #66 of 68 Power 4 in my opponent-adjusted metrics in 2023 and 2024. They surged to #8 last year with Beck at the helm.

It also helped having what Whittingham called his “best offensive line ever.” Far from just coach-speak, this line was absolutely dominant, and paved the way for school rushing records in yards and touchdowns. Utah ranked #2 in my OL Run Push and #13 in Pass Protection. Spencer Fano and Caleb Lomu were both drafted as first-rounders, and all five starters earned All-Big 12 honors.

All five linemen are gone. So is ace line coach Jim Harding and his O-Block.

Their sixth and seventh linemen who were used in some jumbo packages are both back as experienced veteran guards: Solatoa Moea’i and Keith Olson. Alex Harrison got a bonus eligibility season and should start at center. Then the staff added FCS national champion Cedric Jefferson (Montana State) at right tackle, and signed five-star left tackle Kelvin Obot (Fruitland, UT) who could start right away.

Scalley hired Utah State coordinator Kevin McGiven, who will install a scheme similar to what worked here last year – though Scalley wants some of the aggressive mindset of his defense reflected on this side of the ball.
