Minnesota does return its top two blockers in left tackle Nathan Roy and left guard Greg Johnson, plus starting center Ashton Beers. Tony Nelson started the final two games at right guard and moves up into the full-time role, and the staff signed Bennett Warren (Tennessee) who was a Top100 recruit in the 2024 class. The line is more athletic but smaller than the usual giant Minnesota offensive lines of the Fleck era.

The top three tight ends are gone, and they turn to a fifth-year Kaden Helms (Oklahoma) who has minimal game experience but was a four-star recruit stuck in a deep room.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Fleck has an acronym or slogan for everything. First-time defensive coordinator Danny Collins certainly backed up their H.A.V.O.C. motto by disrupting opposing offenses at a top five clip. Minnesota ranked #4 in my Negative Play Rate which tracks how often the defense makes a sack or tackle behind the line of scrimmage.

The unit had big performances like the sack-fests against Nebraska and Michigan State, but collapsed in the 38-35 Northwestern loss, not to mention the Playoff-team blowouts.

Three of their four All-Big Ten stars are back for 2026, but the headliner Perich’s departure stings. The silver lining may have been more resources to boost the incoming transfer class, and they added some firepower to an already strong pass rush.

TJ Bush transferred in and was Cal’s best pass rusher last year. First-team All-Big Ten Anthony Smith is back and his 12.5-sack season was the school’s first double-digit sack year since Willie VanDeSteeg in 2009. If Smith stacks another 10+ sack season he would break the Minnesota career record. Karter Menz (6.5 sacks) also returns, making this defensive end trio one of the best in the Big Ten.

It’s a total rebuild in the middle, with the top four defensive tackles departing. The staff hit the portal with 320-pound space-eater Naquan Crowder (Marshall) and Xion Chapman (FIU).

Maverick Baranowski earned All-Big Ten honors after posting the school’s first 100-tackle season since Blake Cashman in 2018. His fellow starter Devon Williams is gone, but Matt Kingsbury and Emmanuel Karmo moved up the depth chart.

Perich will be missed in the secondary, but John Nestor played well at corner and Fleck called him “the ultimate competitor.” Aydan West (Michigan State) got nearly 400 snaps last year as a true freshman and could be the starter opposite of Nestor. The safety room returns an All-Big Ten headliner in Kerry Brown, plus Zack Harden who transitioned to the position midseason and impressed. The staff signed a wildcard in All-Patriot League Mekhai Smith (Lehigh) from the FCS level.

pick_six_2026.outlook: Stein’s no-excuses attitude is refreshing and Kentucky’s #11 transfer haul is an instant boost to the rebuilding project -- especially in the trenches with a beefed up offensive line. It’s a solid start but their overall roster talent
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Coming off a 4-8 season, Kentucky was alive for bowl eligibility with two shots to get their sixth win. They lost both by a combined 86-17 score: a 484-yard passing day by Diego Pavia and then a 41-0 demolition by Louisville.

It was enough to end Mark Stoops’ 13-year tenure in Lexington. Stoops is the winningest coach in Kentucky history and built physical, competitive teams but a few catalysts caused the downfall.

2022 had the look of a potential dream season, but their ace offensive coordinator left for the NFL and Kentucky couldn’t get past the 4-0 start. Stoops almost took the Texas A&M job after the 2023 season, and then throughout the 2024 season he often complained about NIL funding, telling fans to “Pony Up.” His right-hand man Vince Marrow left for rival Louisville.

All the while, the NIL/Portal system was a bad match for what worked best for Stoops. He and his staff were excellent at finding under- recruited gems in the Midwest and developing them over four or five years. That model was flipped on its head with the transfer portal, and

Kentucky lost its strategic edge.

Less than 24 hours later, Kentucky announced Will Stein as their new head coach. Stein quarterbacked Trinity High School (Louisville) to three KY state titles before walking on at Louisville. But Stein and his family were UK diehards: “growing up in Kentucky and sitting in the stands at UK games as a kid … this is truly a dream come true.”

Stein rose to the top of the coaching carousel after posting four straight Top 15 offenses at UTSA and Oregon, with four different quarterbacks, with a simple motto: “Feed The Studs.”

Stein’s offense can do it all – creative play-calling, fast tempo, RPO, pro-style concepts – but he gears the scheme towards his personnel and forces the ball to his best playmakers.

The 36-year-old didn’t want to hear any excuses regarding budgets or funding. Stein went out and signed the #11 transfer class, #4 in the SEC, and stacked the roster with former blue-chip recruits. Of the 11 “must-keep” players, Kentucky retained seven of them.
pick_six_2026.offense:
The offense really struggled the past two years under Bush Hamdan with #47 and #59 (of 68 Power 4) finishes in my opponent-adjusted metric. Stein’s three Oregon offenses: #3, #5, and #5.

Yes, Oregon is a consistent top five recruiter but Kentucky signed an impact class of transfers to jump-start the rebuild.

Seventh-year quarterback Zach Calzada struggled and was injured, then freshman Cutter Boley stepped up to post the #6 QB Rating among Power 4 freshmen with an SEC All-Freshman honor. Boley left for Arizona State, but Stein pulled off a transfer flip by stealing Kenny Minchey (Notre Dame) away from his Nebraska commitment. Minchey was a four-star recruit and then earned a four-star transfer grade after nearly beating out CJ Carr for the Notre Dame starting job. Minchey has a dual-threat skillset with explosive runs and off-platform throws, and was a significant win for the new Stein staff.

The thunder-and-lightning pair of Dante Dowdell and Seth McGowan have moved on, but the staff signed two former super-recruits in CJ Baxter (Texas) and Jovantae Barnes (Oklahoma). Baxter starred in 2023, Barnes posted 500+ yard seasons in 2022 and 2024, but both are looking to bounce back from injury-filled careers.

Kentucky retained two of their most promising receivers in Hardley Gilmore and DJ Miller who flashed breakout potential last year. Nic Anderson (LSU) transferred in and looks to bounce back to 2023 form when he posted 798 yards, 10 touchdowns, and a top-five 21 yards/catch at Oklahoma. Shane Carr (Southern Utah) was a productive FCS receiver, and Top200 Kenny Darby was a signing day flip from LSU.

Kentucky hasn’t had a tight end eclipse the 400-yard mark since Jacob Tamme in 2007, but Stein loves getting his tight ends involved, especially when they are the so-called Studs. He’s got two good ones here with potential All-SEC Willie Rodriguez and former Top200 Mikkel Skinner. Look for that 20-year drought to be snapped.

At the peak of the Stoops era, Kentucky was defined by their physical offensive line. After consecutive years of poor line play, Stein hit the portal and may have just rebuilt their Big Blue Wall. This is one of the best OL transfer hauls in America with three four-star transfers that were multi-year Power 4 starters.

Lance Heard (Tennessee) earned All-SEC last year and the former five-star tackle is looking to bolster his NFL draft resume. Coleton Price (Baylor) is a three-year starting center, and Tegra Tshabola (Ohio State) was a starter on two Playoff teams. Mark Robinson (UTEP) earned All-CUSA honors, and two more were high school blue-chippers with limited college experience: Max Anderson (Tennessee) and Olaus Alinen (Alabama). Malachi Wood took over the right tackle spot in spring.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Brad White built consistently above-average defenses here with three Top 25 units in seven years, and just one ranked outside the Top 40. He landed at Florida after the coaching change.

Stein’s aggressive playcalling on offense carries over to what he wants from his defense: “I’m not a bend-don’t-break guy.” It’s a contrast from White’s main focus on limiting explosive plays, even if it meant allowing consistent short gains underneath.

He hired Jay Bateman who led Texas A&M to #22 and #28 finishes in my opponent-adjusted rankings. Mike Elko was calling the plays at A&M so Bateman takes on that new role here after some mixed results back during his UNC tenure.

From the defensive line two-deep, two graduated, two more transferred out, but the staff was able to retain two potential breakout candidates in ends Tavion Gadson and Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace.

Last year Humphrey-Grace posted 31 tackles, 7 for loss, and 3.5 sacks and has star potential. Jamarrion Harkless (Purdue) is an instant starter at nose tackle.

Linebackers Daveren Rayner and Alex Afari combined for 130 tackles and both graduated. Grant Godfrey earned some starts down the stretch and returns as the lead inside backer. The staff signed two former blue-chippers Tavion Wallace (Arkansas) and Top100 Elijah Barnes who got a four-star transfer rating and is projected to start alongside Godfrey.

The secondary lost two starters – Cam Dooley (Florida) and Quay’sheed Scott (South Carolina) – to other SEC rosters but they pulled in two of their own. Jordan Castell (Florida) started 35 games and his teammate Aaron Gates came to Lexington with him. Castell will start at safety, Gates is at nickel, and the staff retained their best player in All-SEC safety Ty Bryant who led the league in interceptions last year. The cornerbacks were crushed with injuries last year but Terhyon Nichols is back healthy and Bateman called him the MVP of spring ball. Hasaan Sykes (Western Carolina) was a top FCS corner who picked Kentucky over Illinois.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Longwell coined the term “misfits” to describe Vanderbilt’s collection of under-recruited, chip-on-the-shoulder roster. They even had t-shirts made. Along with Indiana’s dream season, Vanderbilt was America’s underdog team of 2025.

The defense ranked third-worst in the SEC last year, and the offense now has to move on without do-it-all Pavia. Five- star Curtis will have a bright future but this is a tough act to follow, especially for a true freshman. With the league’s lowest talent profile, Post-Pavia, Vanderbilt is set for a rebuilding season.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
When Clark Lea returned to Nashville to take over his alma mater, a program suffering through a seven-year losing season streak, he set out a "ten-year plan” to get Vanderbilt competitive.

Lea has achieved unthinkable heights in just half the time.

After his third team collapsed with a 2-10 (0-8 SEC) season, he took a chance on an under-recruited bunch from New Mexico State. He brought their offensive coaches, their 5’9 JUCO quarterback, and the tight end.

Then Vanderbilt finally secured the long overdue financial commitment, modernized their stadium, and got a signature win in 2024 by upsetting Alabama. The goalposts were carried out by celebrating fans and tossed in the Cumberland River.

But that New Mexico State core led an offensive explosion here in 2025 and finished as the #1 ranked unit in my opponent-adjusted metrics. Eli Stowers won the Mackey Award and Diego Pavia placed second in the Heisman race.

Vanderbilt started 5-0 thanks to the offense scoring 30+ points in the first five games – a school-best in 110 years. Pavia and the offense grinded out last-minute wins against LSU (first since 1990), Missouri, and an overtime shootout at Auburn.

Then Pavia exploded in November to become the first SEC player ever with four consecutive 400- yard games. He kept striking the Heisman pose, but kept backing it up game after game, drive after drive. In the season finale Vanderbilt cashed in on their shot at the first-ever 10-win season in school history by blowing out rival Tennessee 45-24 – in Knoxville – behind Pavia’s 433 yards.

“He’s the best player in the country, the best competitor and teammate I’ve ever met in my life,” said Lea.

While they came up a few spots short of a Playoff berth, and Pavia placed second behind eventual national champion Fernando Mendoza, this was an all-time season for Vanderbilt football. The Ten- Year Plan turned out a Ten-Win season, shifted the culture and expectations, brought a national spotlight to Vanderbilt, and laid the groundwork for the future.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Just days later, Vanderbilt signed the #1 overall recruit in the nation. Yes, Vanderbilt flipped a five-star quarterback from his commitment to Dynasty-Tier Georgia. How’s that for a succession plan post-Pavia?

Jared Curtis (Nashville Christian) said the 2025 breakout season changed his opinion and that he wanted to be part of the growth of his local program. This is Vanderbilt’s first-ever five-star commit, much less the #1 overall national recruit.

The 6’4 Curtis brings a big frame, pocket mobility, and he showed off his arm with a spring game toss that went 65+ yards in the air. Curtis enrolled early to practice in bowl season, was the clear #1 in spring, and will be a true freshman starter this fall.

Tim Beck’s offense ranked in the national top 10 in 13 of my 17 stat categories, none more impressive than the #1 rank in my opponent-adjusted number. How much of that was the Pavia Effect?

Pavia put up 3,593 passing yards, 9.4 per attempt, with 29 touchdowns. He was the leading rusher with 862 yards and eight scores, and had more carries than the top two running backs combined. He was also invincible in the pocket, scrambling away from countless would-be sacks.

The absence of Pavia – even with a super-recruit taking over – and the loss of four starting linemen are major uncertainties for 2026.

Cade McConnell is the only returning starting lineman, but the staff brought in three impact transfers and all are projected starters. Beau Johnson (North Dakota State) was an FCS All-American last year at tackle, Lyndon Cooper (Pittsburgh) is a multi-year starting center, and Micah DeBose (Alabama) was a Top200 recruit in the 2025 cycle. Orion Irving and Clinton Azubuike battle at the other tackle spot.

Stowers was far and away the most productive SEC tight end and was selected in the second round in April. Cole Spence returns as a starter in Vanderbilt’s 12-personnel, and the staff signed four-star transfer Jayvontay Conner (East Carolina) who will be another receiving threat.

Vanderbilt had a pair of 800-yard receivers with Tre Richardson and Junior Sherrill, but their vertical deep-threat Richardson transferred out to Louisville. A pair of transfers will join Sherrill in the new starting rotation. Four-star transfer Ja’Cory Thomas (Old Dominion) put up 719 yards with an explosive 17.5 yard/catch average last year, and Cole Adams (Alabama) was a former blue-chipper stuck in a crowded room. Tristen Brown also returns to compete with Adams in the slot.

Sedrick Alexander and Makhilyn Young both return at running back and they will get a bigger workload without Pavia taking 10-15 carries per game. Together they combined for 981 yards and 17 scores with Young posting a high 9.0 per-carry average. They also signed Kentucky’s Gatorade Player of the Year four-star Evan Hampton.
pick_six_2026.defense:
The defense was strong against the run but overall checked in at #51 of 68 Power 4 in my opponent- adjusted ranking. They do benefit from more roster continuity on this side of the ball, and added in three starters off other Power 4 defenses for an instant boost.

Vanderbilt returns three defensive line starters and also gets back a legit NFL prospect in defensive tackle Yilanan Ouattara who only played in one game before an injury. Khordae Sydnor will be missed but Miles Capers returns at the other edge spot. The staff added five transfer linemen, most notably Power 4 starter Edwin Kolenge (Boston College) and Brian Allen (Iowa) who drew a four-star transfer grade. CJ Jackson (LSU) was a four-star in the 2024 class.

Langston Patterson’s eligibility appeal was declined, but Bryan Longwell returns for a third year as the starting inside backer. Bryce Cowan and Nick Rinaldi move up the depth chart.

The starting corner pair returns and they showed some improvement late in the season. Jordan Matthews surged up the depth chart and now looks like the #1 cover corner and a possible star. Martel Hight became

Vanderbilt’s first two-way player in the modern era – he grabbed four interceptions along with seven receptions on offense.

The safety room is absolutely loaded. CJ Heard was very involved in the run game and led the team in tackles. The staff landed the school’s first-ever all-conference transfer in Ricardo Jones (Clemson) who led the ACC with six interceptions last year. Dontae Carter was Lea’s highest-ranked signee before landing Curtis this cycle, plus a pair of incoming four-stars could play right away: Davin Chandler and Carson Lawrence.

pick_six_2026.outlook: Gundy’s best Oklahoma State teams featured explosive passing attacks and that is exactly what Morris brought with him. As he said, “I was born in the Big 12.” Morris imported the core of his #1 ranked North Texas offense – including first-round NFL quarterback prospect Mestemaker – and this will be the most improved offense of 2026. The defense is a total rebuilding project, but still Oklahoma State is a darkhorse team and moves up from dead last to the middle of a crowded Big 12 field.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Mike Gundy’s 18-year streak of winning seasons was snapped in 2024. He attempted a complete rebuild for 2025 by hiring 11 new coaches and adding 40 players from the transfer portal.

In their first FBS game Oklahoma State lost to Oregon 69-3, for their worst defeat since 1907. Oregon outgained them by 430 yards, scored at will, and took back Pick Sixes on consecutive plays. At times, Oklahoma State looked like an unprepared high school team.

Then Tulsa came into Stillwater and won there for the first time since 1951. The Cowboy fans were chanting "Fire Gundy” throughout the game.

Oklahoma State did just that, four days after the Tulsa embarrassment – OSU’s 11th straight FBS loss -- and ended Gundy’s 21-year tenure. The collapse was caused by his resistance to get the fundraising/NIL program up to speed, young/unproven coordinator hires, and below average high school recruiting.

It was time for a change, but Gundy will still be remembered as an Oklahoma State legend, the winningest coach in school history, and the figurehead that elevated them to heights unthinkable a generation ago. As Pistols Firing podcast put it: “Mike Gundy is as Oklahoma State as Pistol Pete himself.”

The season only got worse after the September firing. Oklahoma State went 0-9 in Big 12 play with the first six by double-digits and the final three in one-score heartbreakers. At 1-11 overall, and the lone win against their FCS opponent, Oklahoma State finished dead last 68th of 68 in my opponent-adjusted Game Grader.

For the first time since the 1960s, Oklahoma State hired an active head coach from another FBS program. They picked Eric Morris who led North Texas to a 12-2 dream season that had them in the AAC title game and in the mix for a Playoff spot. The hire signals their desire to return to the brand of football from Gundy’s peak years: an explosive Air Raid offensive system.

Morris has been a head coach or offensive coordinator for 13 years at Texas Tech, Incarnate Word, Washington State, and North Texas. Over those 13 years, 9 were Top 5 passing attacks, 10 were Top 10 total offense, and 10 were Top 25 in scoring.
pick_six_2026.offense:
His 2025 North Texas unit was his best yet, ranked #1 nationally in both scoring (45 points/game) and total offense (512 yards/game). Morris brought his offensive coordinator Sean Brophy and was able to land six of his offensive starters too.

It is a complete roster overhaul here as Oklahoma State signed 62 transfers, 26 from Power 4 rosters, and 18 from North Texas. Most importantly, the staff brought their top passer, rusher, and receiver, with the All-AAC trio each earning four-star transfer grades.

Drew Mestemaker was the nation’s passing champ with 4,379 yards, placed second with 34 touchdowns, and finished #4 in QB Rating. The 6’4 pocket passer was ranked the #3 transfer quarterback of the entire cycle and will be Oklahoma State’s first NFL-caliber quarterback since Mason Rudolph in 2018. On top of the physical skills, Morris loves Mestemaker’s fast post-snap processing.

Oklahoma State’s lead rusher and top playmaker Rodney Fields transferred out to Kansas State, the three starting receivers are gone, so the skill positions are total roster resets.

The staff brought their star running back Caleb Hawkins who led the AAC with 1,434 rushing yards. He led the entire country with his 25 rushing touchdowns and also kept a high 6.2 per-carry average. Tre Page is the #2 back after leading FCS Tarleton with 839 yards as a freshman.

Slot receiver Wyatt Young led the AAC with 1,264 yards and ranked second with an explosive 18.1 yards/catch average. Young headlines one of the top transfer receiver hauls this cycle along with four-star speedster Chris Barnes (Wake Forest) and the 6’5 red zone threat Justin Bowick (Illinois).

Miles Coleman and Terrence Lewis combined for 734 yards last year for North Texas and should add to the rotation here. Donovan Green (LSU) emerged as the starting tight end in spring as a blocker and pass threat.

Another position, another complete rebuild. The offensive line struggled the past two seasons and last year ranked in the bottom ten in OL Run Push and yards/carry. Six offensive linemen transferred out to Power 4 programs, and their only Big 12 honoree Bob Schick graduated. It will be an all-transfer starting five, with the addition of three North Texas starters and three more from Power 4 programs. All were rated as three-star transfers: center Tyler Mercer (Kansas), guards Jacob Sexton (Oklahoma) and Johnny Dickson (North Texas), and tackles Braydon Nelson (North Texas) and Ashton Lepo (Michigan State). Dickson and Nelson earned All-AAC honors and are familiar with the scheme, while the other three have 31 combined starts at the Power 4 level.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Last offseason, Morris hired 30-year-old defensive coordinator Skyler Cassity away from Sam Houston State where he led a Top 25 defense. Cassity then led one of the biggest one-year statistical turnarounds last year, improving North Texas from their bottom ten marks (34 points and 460 yards per game) up to middle-of-the-pack (25 points and 370 yards per game).

More importantly, when paired with a high-powered offense, the goal of the defense is to create turnovers and steal extra possessions back. His Sam Houston State defense grabbed 27 takeaways, North Texas had 26 last year, and both were Top 10 ranks.

Cassity brought his star linebacker Ethan Wesloski with him and he’ll lead another transfer-heavy unit with as many as seven new starters from the portal. Wesloski earned All-AAC honors, Isaiah Chisom (UCLA) and Tate Romney (Arizona State) bring Power 4 starting experience, and Jack Puckett (Central Oklahoma) was a DII All-American.

Oklahoma State lost their best pass rusher as Wendell Gregory transferred out to South Carolina with a four-star transfer grade. But the staff landed some Power 4 vets of their own with tackles Jerry Lawson (Louisville) and Braylon Rigsby (Texas Tech), and pass rush specialist James Williams (Florida State). Keviyan Huddleston (North Texas) followed his coordinator, and they were able to retain some partial starters in Jaleel Johnson and Malik Charles.

The secondary was torched last year with bottom-five national marks in Opponent QB Rating, Yards/Attempt, and Explosive Passing. The staff retained cornerback LaDainian Fields and brought their top corner from the North Texas secondary in Kollin Lewis. Mo Horn (Texas Tech) will compete at corner, and Christian Bodnar (Liberty) got huge spring praise from Morris. Cameron Epps is back from injury and hopes to return to his 2023 form, plus another round of transfers will compete for the other safety spot: Vincent Holmes (Washington), Quinton Hammonds (North Texas), and Mose Phillips (Missouri).

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Grinch’s defense held up well in my opponent-adjusted metric with a #5 Big 12 finish. And there is still room to improve since a main feature of his defenses are takeaways and UCF only had 14 last year (#91 nationally).

UCF is due for a second-year coach bonus with excellent player retention coupled with a proven game-changer at quarterback. Bowl season is likely as they move up to the mid-tier of the Big 12 and draw the bottom three (Kansas, Colorado, Iowa State).
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Scott Frost led UCF to an undefeated season in 2017, left to attempt to rebuild his alma mater Nebraska, and then returned here to Orlando last offseason.

2025 had the clear look of a transition season with 70 new players, 19 new starters, and new schemes on both sides of the ball.

After a 3-0 start that featured a 34-9 beatdown of Bill Belichick’s UNC team, this started to look more like Frost’s Nebraska teams. They were able to move the ball just fine with high yardage totals and frequent explosive plays, but they weren’t able to convert into points.

Penalties, turnovers, and red zone failures led to close losses to Kansas by 7, Cincinnati by 9, and Houston by 3… this is textbook “Frost Effect.” The 5-7 finish marked their first consecutive seasons without a bowl game since 2003-04.

However, some credit is due for grinding out five wins in a complete transition season. UCF did so with an unsettled quarterback room that was crushed with injuries. Younger players flashed later in the season and emerged as stars to build around. And Frost’s most controversial move, the hiring of beleaguered defensive coordinator Alex Grinch, turned out to be a success so far.

Andrew Cherico of Knights247 listed out the seven “must-retain” players for UCF to keep in Orlando, away from the transfer portal. To Frost’s credit, they retained all seven.

Retention of star players, second-year coach and scheme bonuses, and a total upgrade at quarterback have UCF well-positioned to return to bowl season and join a crowded Big 12 field in 2026.
pick_six_2026.offense:
The three-man fall camp battle at quarterback ended up extending into the regular season due to a run of injuries. Tayven Jackson played the majority but struggled with the 14th ranked QB Rating in the Big 12 and threw almost as many picks (8) as touchdowns (10). He lacked the mobility to fit Frost’s scheme, Jacurri Brown had the athleticism but not the passing, and all

three guys ended up transferring out.

UCF found a winner to build the 2026 team around. Alonza Barnett led James Madison to the College Football Playoff last year and is 21-6 overall as a starter. Barnett earned Sun Belt Player of the Year after throwing for 23 touchdowns and 2,806 yards, while adding 589 yards and 15 scores on the ground – the sixth-most among quarterbacks.

Barnett’s dual-threat skillset is a perfect match for Frost’s offense. On the recruiting trail, UCF signed their highest-rated quarterback commit of all-time in Top300 four-star Rocco Marriott (Platte County, MO). And for the backup role, they signed FIU’s three-year starter Keyone Jenkins.

The running back duo of Myles Montgomery and Jaden Nixon was a bright spot last year. Montgomery led with 705 yards as the between-the-tackles workhorse while Nixon had 554 and a penchant for explosive long-runs. With both off to the pros, the staff is attempting to reload the same dynamic from the portal with Landen Chambers (Central Arkansas) and Duke Watson (Louisville). Chambers rushed for 1,273 yards – a Top 10 FCS mark – while Watson led the entire nation with an explosive 8.9 yards/carry back in 2024 before his injuries last year.

DJ Black and Marcus Burke were the original starters but Duane “Speedy” Thomas and freshman Waden Charles emerged as star receivers to build around. Thomas led with 528 yards and was used all over the field – outside, the slot, the backfield, and in the return game. The 6’2 Charles showed off his big catch radius and flashed highlight reel plays later in the season. Ric’Darious Farmer is back from a season-ending injury and the staff signed first-team FCS All-American Josh Derry (Monmouth) who put up 1,101 yards and 13 touchdowns last year.

UCF also retained their breakout star tight end Dylan Wade who earned All-Big 12 honorable mention as a coverage mismatch in the pass game. Wade’s 43 catches, 523 yards, and five touchdowns were all UCF records.

There is uncertainty in the trenches with four starters gone from a line that struggled. They missed assignments and were heavily penalized, often killing drives and keeping them out of the endzone. UCF ranked #29 in yards/carry and #32 in long-yardage explosive rushing, but did so with minimal help from the offensive line which ranked #95 in my OL Run Push stat. Those rushing totals were a testament to what the running backs achieved in spite of the line.

Preston Cushman is the lone returning starter and the new line will be transfer-heavy. The staff signed four from the portal and all were rated as three-star transfers. Cooper Terpstra (Michigan State) was a Big Ten backup and is projected to start at center. Henry Tabansi (Buffalo) earned other Power 4 offers, and Brady Wayburn (Connecticut) and Tyler Gibson (Charlotte) were starters from the non-AQ level.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Grinch was considered a controversial pick at defensive coordinator, after struggling at prior stops, but Frost said the two of them both wanted fresh starts and a chance to prove it.

UCF’s defense improved in scoring and made major jumps in passing stats. They finished fifth in the Big 12 in my opponent-adjusted defense metric – #5 vs. the pass and #8 vs. the run.

Seven defenders earned All-Big 12 honors, and while they lose their game-changing defensive end pair of Malachi Lawrence and Nyjalik Kelly to the pros, there are still stars returning at each level.

RJ Jackson is back at defensive tackle and is rejoined by original starter Horace Lockett who was playing well before his injury in week four. UCF did an excellent job with player retention this cycle, but the best one to get away was hometown four-star John Walker (Ohio State). The staff signed All-MAC Bruno Dall (Akron) and 2025 Top200 four-star Jessie Harrold (Florida State) to compete

with Sincere Edwards and four-star Isaiah Nixon.

UCF retained their star middle backer and tackle leader Lewis Carter who should push for all-league honors again. Cole Kozlowski graduated but the staff signed Old Dominion starter Jahleel Culbreath and former four- star Tackett Curtis (Wisconsin).

Four starters are back in the secondary with safety Phillip Dunnam the lone loss. All-Big 12 Jayden Bellamy emerged as the top corner, Braeden Marshall started at nickel, and both were key retentions for 2026. Demari Henderson was active in run support with 61 tackles, and the staff signed Ty Bartrum (Harvard) fresh off an FCS All-America season last year.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
UCLA hired a proven winner in Chesney. He brought both of his James Madison coordinators, ten of their players, and multiple all-conference stars to jump start the transition.

The staff was also able to retain five-star Iamaleava and upgrade all the position rooms around him. UCLA will
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Back in 2011, UCLA suffered a 50-0 loss to USC, an embarrassment so severe it caused the administration to change coaches and recommit to recruiting. It led to the Jim Mora era that started with a 29-11 run and pair of Top 15 seasons.

After a 5-7 debut season, DeShaun Foster’s second team suffered a 43- 10 loss to Utah, a loss to UNLV, and then a 35-10 meltdown against New Mexico. An 0-3 start, with a blowout loss to a coach-transition, Mountain West program – that was Foster’s 50-0 moment.

UCLA fired Foster two days later and opened up a season-long coaching search that allowed for a much more thorough process than the February 2024 scramble after Chip Kelly left for Ohio State.

In the meantime, the interim staff sparked a three-game win streak capped by the 42-37 win over then #7 Penn State. Tight ends coach Jerry Neuheisel took over the playcalling and outdueled PSU’s Jim Knowles to become the first 0-4 team to beat a Top 10 opponent in 40 years.

“You’d think it was Mardi Gras,” said interim head coach Tim Skipper regarding the postgame locker room celebration.

They notched wins over Michigan State and Maryland but lost the final five games. That makes it seven losing seasons in the past ten, and Rose Bowl attendance dwindled to a 37,000 per- game average.

The three-month coaching search ended with a major win as they hired James Madison’s Bob Chesney, one of the top prizes in the biggest coaching carousel in college football history. Chesney took over JMU in 2024 after Curt Cignetti took his staff and 20 players with him to Indiana. In two years he went 21-6, won the Sun Belt, and earned a spot in the Playoff – quite the achievement for a school just five years removed from the FCS level.

Before that at Holy Cross he won the Patriot League five times in six seasons, and had similar success at DII Assumption and DIII Salve Regina. He brought both JMU coordinators and 10 of his players with him to Westwood to help spark the program rebuild.
pick_six_2026.offense:
UCLA ranked in the national bottom ten in both scoring offense and scoring defense. James Madison was in the top ten in both with coordinators and schemes that clearly work.

Nico Iamaleava returns as the face of the franchise. The former five-star finished just 14th in the Big Ten in QB Rating, but he showed off his big arm and his athleticism in the Penn State win with five touchdowns. His toughness cannot be questioned, as he shouldered the team-high in carries and rushing yards, battled through hits and a November concussion, and rallied the locker room after the Foster firing.

His skillset fits better with this scheme, as James Madison used a lot of quarterback designed-runs.

The biggest concern is in the trenches, where last year’s transfer portal gamble backfired and produced a below average unit. This cycle, they flipped the strategy and signed guys with proven starting experience. UCLA only returns one starter, but it’s their best one in left guard Eugene Brooks. From there, it is Pick Your Transfer at the other four spots.

Three JMU linemen transferred in with tackle JD Rayner and the All-Sun Belt duo of Riley Robell and Carter Sweazie. Hall Schmidt was a starter on Boise State’s 2024 Playoff team, Jordan Davis (South Alabama) is a three-year starter, and Derek Osman (Harvard) was All-Ivy.

Iamaleava was the lead rusher, and the trio of running backs shared carries with Jalen Berger, Anthony Woods, and Jaivian Thomas all getting 60+ attempts. Berger graduated, and the staff

signed their star running back Wayne Knight who rushed for 1,300 yards for them at JMU last year. Knight is a speedy 5’7 and put up 100+ yards in the Playoff loss to Oregon. Look for another three- man committee here.

Three of the top four receivers are gone, but with a boost from the portal it is an upgraded unit. The lack of explosiveness in the pass game (#134 nationally) was an issue but it’s a fresh start for 2026. Aidan Mizell (Florida) is a former Top100 recruit and earned a four-star transfer grade and brings track speed to the room. Another speedster Brian Rowe (South Carolina) was a 2025 four-star and he’ll battle veteran Mikey Matthews for reps in the slot.

They signed some proven production too. 6’4 Leland Smith (San Jose State) and Landon Ellis (James Madison) were both all-league performers at the non-AQ level, and combined for 77 catches and 1,312 yards last year. The staff also brought their blocking tight end Josh Phifer with them from JMU.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Chesney brought defensive coordinator Colin Hitschler with him after building a dominant unit at JMU last year that placed in the national top ten in total defense, rushing defense, opponent QB Rating, and third downs among other categories.

10 of his 11 starters earned All-Sun Belt honors and three of them came to UCLA: corner DJ Barksdale and defensive ends Sahir West and Aiden Gobaira.

West is the headliner after a 7 sack, 14 tackle-for-loss season earned him Sun Belt Freshman of the Year. West and Gobaira, along with California’s best edge rusher Ryan McCulloch, directly addresses their weakness in pass rush last year. UCLA was the least disruptive defense in America per my Negative Play Rate.

The interior tackles struggled too. Both starters Gary Smith and Keanu Williams are gone, and UCLA turns to Darold DeNgohe who was a projected starter for Rutgers before a preseason injury. DeNgohe was actually at JMU before that with the staff in 2024 and posted a productive season.

Former Top100 Tyson Ford (California) emerged as the other tackle starter.

Jalen Woods is the lone returning starter at linebacker after JonJon Vaughns graduated and Isaiah Chisom transferred out to Oklahoma State. The staff reloaded from the portal with four-star transfer Sammy Omosigho (Oklahoma) who posted 89 tackles, and 9.5 for loss, in two years in the rotation. Anthony Sacca (Notre Dame) was a 2025 four-star, and Drew Spinogatti came over from JMU.

Corner Rodrick Pleasant was arguably their top defender last year and he returns with all-league potential. Three more transfers are projected starters in Dante Lovett (Virginia Tech) at the other corner, Utah starter Tao Johnson at safety, and DJ Barksdale (JMU) at nickel. Key Lawrence graduated but Cole Martin is back at strong safety.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Cal signed the #3 transfer class in the ACC and boosted the receiver room and secondary with instant impact starters. JKS should get a second-year boost and he earned my third-team All-ACC preseason spot.

The lines of scrimmage hold them back from a higher projection, but if Lupoi can develop them quicker than expected, Cal has a good shot at a bowl bid. They need to win two of the four swing games: UCLA, Pittsburgh, @ UNLV, and @ NC State.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
The Justin Wilcox era at California resulted in little change year-to-year and his nine teams followed the same general script. His program was defense-first, led by a secondary that continued to churn out NFL draft picks. The lines of scrimmage were consistently below average, pass protection and pass rush struggled, but a handful of skill players picked up the slack.

Even through five offensive coordinator changes, the pattern remained the same. And they always finished right near the .500 mark.

It got to the point where even Cal football analyst Nick Kranz admitted “it became increasingly difficult to find anything interesting to say about Wilcox’s teams – they were always the same.”

The sharp highs and lows of the 2025 season flipped the script.

Last spring, the program’s top boosters threatened to pull their donations unless Ron Rivera was given full control. Top players transferred out, but four-star freshman Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele flipped his commitment from Oregon to Cal, and provided a spark heading into the season.

JKS became the first true freshman to start an opener here since Jared Goff and he tossed six touchdowns over their 3-0 start. Then they were shutout 34-0 by San Diego State, lost to Duke by 24, and threw a decisive Pick Six in the Virginia loss.

Wilcox’s defense helped secure two more wins at the goal-line with Luke Ferrelli’s endzone interception to beat Boston College and Brent Austin’s forced fumble and recovery in the endzone to fend off UNC. JKS then put in his two best games as Cal snapped a five-year losing streak against ranked opponents beating both #15 Louisville and #21 SMU – eliminating them both from the ACC race.

But even with such highs, the low point against Stanford was enough to finally end the Wilcox era. Cal gave up two fumble touchdowns and committed a Wilcox era high 13 penalties in the 31-10 embarrassment.

Rivera moved quick and Cal hired alum Tosh Lupoi. After playing here in the early 2000s, Lupoi was a co-defensive coordinator on Alabama’s title teams in 2015 and 2017, and has led Oregon’s defense the past four years with consecutive Broyles Award semifinalist nominations.

Lupoi also has a strong recruiting profile. He earned the 2010 Rivals Recruiter of the Year by helping Cal sign a Top 15 class, then led several Top 5 classes at Alabama and Oregon. He backed up the reputation right away by flying out to Hawaii the day after the press conference to meet JKS and secure his commitment.
pick_six_2026.offense:
The 6’3 lefty JKS was an instant program-changer. He threw 18 touchdowns, nine picks, and placed third nationally among true freshmen in QB Rating. For the first time in years, downfield explosive passing returned to the offense and he heads into 2026 riding a 178-pass streak without an interception – seven shy of Goff’s school record. Lupoi loves his pocket presence and how he “does the most difficult things the best.”

His freshman season, paired with Lupoi’s recruiting chops, attracted a top-rated group of pass-catchers to transfer in. Cal’s transfer class ranked #14 nationally and #3 in the ACC.

Ian Strong (Rutgers) earned All-Big Ten honors and thrived in one-on-one balls, Chase Hendricks (Ohio) was ranked as the #15 transfer receiver and led the MAC with 1,037 yards, and Cooper Perry (Oregon) was a Top200 recruit last cycle. Tight end Dorian Thomas (New Mexico) earned first-team All-Mountain West.

That’s three four-star transfers and another recent Top200 four-star recruit.

All-ACC Jacob De Jesus departs after a 1,000-yard season, Trond Grizzell is also gone, but that transfer haul provides more than enough firepower for the pass game.

Lupoi’s coordinator hires followed a pattern: young 30-year-olds from NFL staffs with West Coast college roots. On offense, Jordan Somerville spent the last three seasons on the Tampa Bay Bucs staff and helped lead Baker Mayfield to two top ten passing seasons.

In addition to his first role as play-caller, Somerville is tasked with rebuilding an offensive line that struggled the past few seasons. The run game was completely broken in 2025 and the line has consecutive bottom ten finishes in my OL Run Push metric.

Four partial starters return with a combined 2,300 career snaps: Bastian Swinney, Frederick Williams, Tyson Ruffins, and Sioape Vatikani. The staff added another round of transfer additions with limited experience and mid-three star rankings. Jimothy Lewis (Mississippi State) emerged in spring as the likely fifth starter.

Two of the three backs were battling injuries so Kendrick Raphael stepped up to take 70% of the carries and earned All-ACC recognition. The explosiveness was lacking but he gained tough yards with minimal room from the line. Raphael transferred to SMU but Cal feels they upgraded with Adam Mohammed (Washington) who was the #6 ranked transfer running back.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Lupoi and Dan Lanning came from the Nick Saban and Kirby Smart trees and together they put their own spin on the defense. They kept the same level of aggressiveness but tweaked the base formation to stress the RPO game. Lupoi uses a four-man front, two outside backers, and three safeties with the middle one almost at linebacker depth.

Cal will shift from their 3-3-5 to a 4-2-5 and they need to find a whole new defensive line. They struggled to create disruption last year with a #109 rank in Negative Play Rate and #100 in sacks. Both interior starters graduated and two ends transferred out – Ryan McCulloch (UCLA) and TJ Bush (Minnesota) – but the staff signed five defensive line transfers. Three of them were former four-star recruits from high school: Jericho Johnson (Oregon), Solomon Williams (Texas A&M) and Emmanuel Okoye (Tennessee). Nate Burrell and Derek Wilkins are both fifth-year veterans at end.

Both All-ACC backers Cade Uluave (BYU) and Luke Ferrelli (Ole Miss) transferred out and Lupoi is gambling on former Top200 prospects that lack collegiate experience: Tristan Jernigan (Texas A&M) and Kamar Mothudi (Oregon).

As usual for the Wilcox era, they had an elite coverage corner duo but both Hezekiah Masses and Brent Austin are both gone. Incoming corner Ricky Fletcher (Ole Miss) is their top All-ACC candidate on defense and Daniel Harris (Georgia) was a rotational corner last year. Isaiah Crosby was the original starting safety before an injury, Aiden Manutai filled in and helped seal the SMU win, and both are back for 2026. Both nickelbacks Cam Sidney and Jasiah Wagoner are also back, plus the staff added high four-star Kingston Lopa (Oregon).

pick_six_2026.outlook:
This is not the usual “second-year coach bonus” in fact with 85 new players this is basically a second transition season. Rodriguez upgraded the roster with the nation’s rushing champ, improved lines of scrimmage, and a Top 25 high school signing class to build the foundation for future seasons.

West Virginia will move up a few spots on the Big 12 ladder but next year 2027 looks like a better shot for a program revival season.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Rich Rodriguez left West Virginia in 2007 just days after Backyard Brawl rival Pittsburgh ruined their shot at a BCS national title appearance.

18 years later Rodriguez returned and was able to avenge that loss with a comeback win over Pitt. Nicco Marchiol came off the bench and sparked the 10-point comeback in the final five minutes to force overtime. Then Tye Edwards cashed in the game-winning score to push West Virginia to 2-1 entering Big 12 play.

The season highlights end there. As Rodriguez said after the 41-10 loss to Kansas the following week: “nothing was good, coaching? not good, playing? not good.”

It was already set up to be a typical transition season with 70 new players and a scheme change to Rodriguez’s rushing attack. But the transition season was made worse by a run of injuries in September at the offensive skill positions. Before the end of the month they were already down preseason All-Big 12 running back Jahiem White, his backup Edwards, Marchiol, top receiver Jaden Bray, and then the offensive line got hit a few games later.

West Virginia trudged through a 4-8 season with six losses by double-digits. They closed with a 49-0 beat down from eventual Big 12 champs Texas Tech, but even worse was the 45-13 loss to UCF, a fellow coaching transition program.

Normally I would be writing about all the returning starters and stat gains that are expected from a second-year coach bonus. But this has the look of another full transition season. The senior-heavy 2025 roster graduated, West Virginia added 83 new players – 49 recruits and 34 transfers – and they will have as many as 19 new starters.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Rodriguez cycled through five different quarterbacks and eventually found a spark from true freshman Scotty Fox. In his second start, West Virginia almost knocked off TCU (23-17) with a 301-yard passing day from Fox who even drew compliments from the opposing head coach Sonny Dykes. Fox led two Big 12 wins, a 45-35 shootout over #22 Houston and a 29-22 win over Colorado, and he shouldered 27 carries for 123 rushing yards and two scores in the wins.

All other quarterbacks transferred out, so it will be Fox battling incoming transfer Michael Hawkins (Oklahoma) who also brings the dual-threat skillset needed for this scheme. Hawkins started a few games for Oklahoma back in 2024 as a true freshman but he struggled in a tough spot.

The top four running backs are gone, and the staff signed the nation’s rushing champ Cam Cook (Jacksonville State). Cook ran for 1,659 yards and 16 touchdowns with a high 5.6 per-carry average and will be the workhorse here in 2026. Four-star signee Amari Latimer will be the second back as a true freshman.

The top three receivers are gone – Cam Vaughn, Jeff Weimer, and Rodney Gallagher – though that doesn’t account for their original top target Jaden Bray who returns after the early season-ending injury. Bray is their clear #1 receiver to build around, and a trio of transfers fill out the new rotation. TaRon Francis (LSU) was a Top200 recruit in the 2025 class, Prince Strachan (USC) had success at Boise State but was stuck behind All-Big Ten stars and the Biletnikoff winner at USC, and DJ Epps (Troy) will start in the slot.

Rodriguez mentioned using more 12 personnel this year but their top two tight ends graduated. Ryan Ward got plenty of snaps last year and assumes the starting role, while 6’7 Cam Ball (Mississippi State) and Josh Sapp (Clemson) were Power 4 backups last year.

The offensive line was hit with injuries and the unit never gelled together. Last year West Virginia placed in the bottom 15 nationally in both my OL Run Push (#121) and Pass Protection (#120) by allowing a sack on 9% of pass attempts. Two starters return in center Landen Livingston and

honorable mention All-Big 12 Nick Krahe. Rodriguez hired back a coaching legend in Rick Trickett, who enters his 53rd season as an offensive line coach. Together these two led top-ranked rushing attacks at West Virginia (2001-2006) and more recently at Jacksonville State. His final three JSU rushing offenses all ranked in the national top five.

West Virginia added Devin Vass who started the final seven games for Kansas State last year, Amare Grayson (Jacksonville State) who earned first-team All-CUSA, and signed Top100 Kevin Brown who looks like an instant starter at right tackle. They also retained their top two backups Malik Agbo and Josh Aisosa to add experienced depth and potentially win starting spots.
pick_six_2026.defense:
There is even more change on this side of the ball as West Virginia will feature a completely new starting lineup – 11 new starters.

Change may be welcomed after allowing 31 points per game (#114) with a pass defense ranked in the bottom ten of most stat categories including third-worst – #66 of 68 Power 4 – in my opponent- adjusted passing stat.

The star of the defense, All-Big 12 lineman Edward Vesterinen, graduated and West Virginia lost their top six in the trenches. Nate Gabriel got 300 snaps and is the new projected nose tackle, and from there it’s a mix of transfers. Tackle KJ Henson was a JUCO All-American last year, ends Zeke Campbell (Coastal Carolina) and Harper Holloman (Western Kentucky) both earned all-league honors at the non-AQ level, and Tobi Haastrup (Oregon) was a Top250 recruit in the 2025 cycle. This is an upgraded room from 2025 despite the loss of Vesterinen.

The two starting backers and two more potential rising stars are all gone. Ben Cutter rises to a starting spot, and FAU starter Tyler Stolsky will battle Illinois backup Malachi Hood for the other spot.

Every safety on the roster departed along with their top three cornerbacks after a rough 2025 statistical performance. Nickelback Fred Perry led the team in tackles and he also left.

Another position, another transfer reload and the new secondary will feature two non-AQ starters at the safety spots -- Kamari Wilson (Memphis) and Andrew Powdrell (UNLV) – and two backup corners moving up to the starting lineup in Nick Taylor and Keyshawn Robinson. At nickel, the staff signed Wisconsin’s starter Geimere Latimer, and they found a wildcard in Top100 recruit Matt Sieg who can play safety and may even be used as an offensive weapon.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Aranda upgraded his defense, hired a proven coordinator Joe Klanderman, and shifted more of the roster budget over to the defense. The other side is a complete rebuild as they lose 10 starters from their elite passing offense.

Baylor is basically .500 (36-37) during the Aranda era, and this year will be similar. Baylor remains in the mid-tier of
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
Baylor closed the 2024 season on a six-game Big 12 win streak, placed in the Top 25 of Game Grader, and carried that momentum forward into 2025 with a Top 10 mark in returning production. 18 starters were back and both coordinators returned.

The fundamentals clearly pointed up. This was the year to cash in with a veteran roster and return to the Big 12 title game for the first time since 2021.

It turns out that the pass game was the only thing that was as-advertised. The defensive flaws were apparent right away, as Auburn rushed for 300+ yards in the opening loss. Arizona State won a coinflip game in the Big 12 opener, but still Baylor got to 4-2 with a pair of miracle comeback wins.

Sawyer Robertson threw for 440 yards to outlast SMU 48-45 and was the first Big 12 quarterback since Patrick Mahomes to post three straight 400+ yard games. Robertson led another comeback against Kansas State with help from Jacob Redding’s Pick Six and Cooper Lanz’s blocked field goal as time expired.

Baylor was 4-2 with all goals still on the table but then crashed, losing five of the final six. The defense allowed nearly 200 rushing yards/game

(bottom ten nationally) and the high-powered passing attack couldn’t keep playing from behind.

The 5-7 season brought Dave Aranda’s record back below .500 at 36-37 and perhaps the timing of a November athletic director change saved his job. Thanks to extra bowl openings, Baylor actually earned a bowl invitation but rather than use the 15 bonus practices as a chance to shift the momentum back in the positive direction, Aranda shockingly rejected the bid.

2026 is certainly a make-or-break season, and their veteran roster now flips to a new-look, transfer- heavy starting lineup.
pick_six_2026.offense:
Offensive coordinator Jake Spavital put it simply: “we’re a brand-new team.”

That is not an overstatement, at least offensively, as 10 starters are gone from their pass-heavy attack that finished #20 in my opponent-adjusted rankings.

Robertson graduated after a high-volume final season. He threw for 3,681 yards and 31 touchdowns – both top five national marks – and his 14-game streak of multiple touchdown passes was the longest in the Big 12 since Baker Mayfield.

Baylor went all-in on their new quarterback and he instantly became the new face of the program. DJ Lagway was the #1 ranked quarterback of the 2024 recruiting cycle, and the five-star started 16 games for Florida. Lagway’s father was a running back here at Baylor, and he was drawn to Spavital’s scheme which he notes "reminds me of my high school offense.”

That should be music to Baylor fans’ ears – Lagway compiled 5,500+ yards of offense and 75 touchdowns as a senior in that offense for nearby Willis. At 6’5, 240 pounds, Lagway adds a quarterback-run dynamic and can be a bowling ball in short-yardage spots. He ranked second in the SEC in QB Rating in 2024, but fell to second-worst last season.

All four receivers are gone – first-team All-Big 12 Josh Cameron, Ashtyn Hawkins, Kobe Prentice, and Kole Wilson – plus the pass-game mismatch and human highlight reel Michael Trigg at tight end. It’s a full rebuild here, but the staff pulled in other Power 4 starters Dre’Lon Miller (Colorado) and Gavin Freeman (Oklahoma State). Miller is the most dynamic addition after earning starts as a freshman in 2024 and then moving to running back in 2025. Jadon Porter and Louis Brown are the only returners but they only combined for 15 catches last year. Former four-star tight end Tony Livingston (Florida) followed Lagway to Waco, and blocker Matthew Klopfenstein is back.

It’s another complete rebuild in the trenches as four of the starting five are gone. All-Big 12 Omar Aigbedion graduated, and two more starters landed at SEC programs: center Coleton Price (Kentucky) and Sean Thompkins (LSU). Right tackle Kaden Sieracki is the only full returning starter, though his brother Koltin started a few at right guard. The other three spots are up for grabs and three incoming transfers are projected to win the jobs with Yakiri Walker (Memphis) at center, Nate Kibble (Texas) at left guard, and Logan Moore (UAB) at left tackle. The starting five were all three-star recruits or transfers.

The run game was supposed to feature a top duo of Dawson Pendergrass and Bryson Washington, but before the season Pendergrass was knocked out with an injury. Washington hit a fumble problem, and the yards/carry fell from Top 40 to below average. Washington transferred out to Auburn, but Pendergrass returned healthy as the lead back for 2026. Caden Knighten is also back after 104 carries and 469 yards as a true freshman.

While the run/pass split will certainly balance out from last year’s heavy-pass selection, Spavital will still feature his choice routes in the pass game and operate with fast tempo, which he calls “our biggest weapon.”
pick_six_2026.defense:
Defense is Aranda’s area of expertise but so far Baylor has landed just one Top 25 defense in six years per my opponent-adjusted rankings. The last three under coordinator Matt Powledge had a bottom ten average rank. The pass rush was historically ineffective last year, and their 13 sacks were the fewest by a Big 12 defense in a decade.

Aranda made a coordinator change here with Kansas State’s Joe Klanderman and also made the decision to give up play-calling duties and return to a CEO-type role. Klanderman has a track record of effective defenses and his focus on creating havoc directly addresses the pass rush problem. His scheme is aggressive, attacking, and ranked in the Top 25 of turnovers in three of the past four seasons.

This year Aranda shifted their roster budget to this side of the ball: “this is the most money we’ve spent on defense since I’ve been here.”

Four starters return, but they also get back two more original starters from injury, two starters off other Power 4 teams, and two JUCO All-Americans.

Devonte Tezino is back at defensive tackle and is joined by national champion and four-star transfer Hosea Wheeler (Indiana) who is appealing for a bonus eligibility season. Jamaal Whyce (Marshall) and Jordan Mack (Coastal Carolina) add depth to the interior, while end Zavion Hardy (South Carolina) was

the overall #1 JUCO prospect of 2025. Kyler Jordan returns at end after starting the final two games.

Keaton Thomas was the leader of the defense but he transferred to Ole Miss. Baylor does get back original starter Travion Barnes, the former C-USA Player of the Year, as well as starter Kyland Reed and rising four-star Kaleb Burns.

Two starters return to the secondary and both had All-Big 12 honors: safety Jacob Redding and corner LeVar Thornton. Devin Turner was a former All-Big Ten star at Northwestern and he is back healthy to start at safety – Klanderman calls him a “difference-maker.” The other corner spot is a battle between Reggie Bush, Devon Jordan (Oklahoma), and wildcard JUCO All-America Stilton McKelvey. Klanderman also brought two Kansas State defenders with him: Jayden Rowe and Colby McCalister.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
Can lightning strike twice in Winston-Salem?

Dickert will have to do so with just six returning starters – nine All-ACC performers are gone. With bottom-five
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
A year ago, longtime Wake Forest head coach Dave Clawson retired citing college football’s structural changes and the disappearance of the four-year student-athlete. His final team finished 4-8 and top talent was poached from the program via the transfer portal.

Clawson’s concerns about the game are still valid, and his Wake Forest legacy will be remembered well, but new head coach Jake Dickert pulled off an instant transition and his nine-win debut was nothing short of shocking.

Dickert flipped the roster with 32 transfers plus a full recruiting class, and after some September growing pains, Wake Forest finished the season winning seven of their last nine. They knocked off a pair of ranked teams including the program’s first Top 15 win since 1979 when they beat ACC runner-up Virginia.

They did it with defense, Dickert’s area of expertise, by improving in every single stat category and turning a 2024 weakness into a 2025 strength. Wake Forest finished ranked #9 nationally in my opponent- adjusted metric and they held those ranked opponents Virginia and SMU to just 9 and 12 points.

The surprise debut season ended with a five-gallon mayonnaise shower – the infamous reward for winning the Duke’s Mayo Bowl – to cap off the school’s fourth nine-win season ever.

Player movement may still be at an all-time high, but Dickert was clearly proud of his team’s academic performance, posting a combined 3.3 GPA which he called a school record.

They were hit with a high-profile case of potential roster tampering when starting offensive tackle Melvin Siani took a multi-million deal with Texas in the final hours despite being under contract. The program lost a trio of star players who earned four-star transfer grades, but did not sign any four-stars of their own.
pick_six_2026.offense:
No four-star transfers, but they did pull in one Power 4 starter via the portal.

Gio Lopez was Bill Belichick’s hand-picked quarterback for his college debut season, but the sophomore struggled without much help around him. Lopez finished 14th of the 17 ACC starting quarterbacks in QB Rating with a low 6.7 yards/attempt and just 10 touchdowns.

Dickert is more intrigued with what he saw from Lopez the year prior when he was at South Alabama and paired up with current Wake offensive coordinator Rob Ezell. In 2024, Lopez earned All-Sun Belt honors with 18 touchdowns, just 5 picks, a 66% completion, and a high 8.2 yards/attempt. That offense averaged 34 points/game to place in the Top 20 of scoring.

Ezell’s impact was felt immediately here as he helped fix the offensive line, and re-instill confidence in a sixth-year journeyman at quarterback in Robby Ashford. The veteran shouldered a heavy workload, especially when star running back Demond Claiborne was sidelined with injuries, and helped grind out win after win.

Ashford is gone, along with backup Deshawn Purdie, meaning they are all in on Lopez at quarterback.

It’s a total transition season all over the offense. The quarterbacks are gone, Claiborne went pro, five of the six receivers are gone, three offensive linemen graduated and a fourth transferred out in the final hours.

With 2,599 yards, Claiborne leaves as the fourth all-time rusher in school history and earned All- ACC twice. Ty Clark shined in his bowl game start with 164 total yards and a score. The staff added KD Daniels (Florida) who was a former Top200 recruit and got backup carries last season.

Leading receiver Carlos Hernandez is back but otherwise it is a complete rebuilding project behind him. Sawyer Racanelli graduated, then the next three left with high transfer grades: Sterling Berkhalter (Texas), Chris Barnes (Oklahoma State), and Micah Mays (Florida).

The staff signed four transfers, headlined by C-USA All-Freshman Wondame Davis (UTEP) whose explosive 23.5 yards/catch ranked #2 nationally. The other three come from Power 4 programs but were either backups or in the rotation last year: Chase Tyler (Duke), Ny Carr (Miami), and Kam Shanks (Arkansas). Despite all the change, Dickert says “we’ve gotten faster” at receiver.

Starting tight end Eni Falayi departs, Kamrean Johnson returns, and the staff added a sixth-year vet in Landon Morris (California).

Another position group, another complete rebuild. Ezell improved the offensive line 100 spots in Pass Protection, up to #22 (4% Sack Rate) from the 2024 line at #122 (10% Sack Rate). Now four of those starters depart including three All-ACC performers: Fa’alili Fa’amoe, George Sell, and Devin Kylany. They were planning to build the new line around their anchor at left tackle Melvin Siani but he left for Texas in the final hours and was rated the #3 transfer linemen this cycle.

Clinton Richard and George Steih return as partial-year starters, and the staff signed a trio of FCS transfers Tolu Olajide (New Hampshire), John Ohnegian (Bucknell), and Will Way (Weber State), along with Ryan Berger (Oregon State).
pick_six_2026.defense:
Dickert led the third-largest defensive turnaround as Wake Forest cut off 10 points/game and 100 yards/game from their 2024 averages. They saved their best for the ranked opponents as they kept Virginia out of the endzone and then held SMU 2.6 yards/play below their average which was the #14 defensive performance of the entire 2025 season.

Unlike the offense, this side of the ball does return some key stars to build around. Both defensive ends are back with Gabe Kirschke and All-ACC Langston Hardy combining for 12 sacks and 26

tackles-for-loss. Starting tackles Jayden Loving and Nuer Gatkuoth are gone but they were able to retain their next pair of Zach Lohavichan and Dallas Afalava.

Aiden Hall returns at one linebacker spot though they lose All-ACC honorable mention backer Dylan Hazen. Frank Cusano got experience as a freshman and now moves up into the starting lineup. The staff signed Buom Jock (California) who redshirted last season but in 2024 earned All-Mountain West with 100 tackles at Colorado State.

One all-league star returns in Davaughn Patterson but two more graduated. Both corners Karon Prunty and Lardarius Webb are gone and the biggest loss of the defense is former walk-on turned program legend Nick Andersen, the first-team All-ACC safety. Braylon Johnson is a returning starter at free safety and the staff signed a pair of non-AQ starting corners in All-CUSA Deuce Blades (FIU) and Bernard Causey (Georgia State).

pick_six_2026.outlook:
2025 was a dream season and the school’s winningest Senior class (35 wins over four seasons) capped it off with an ACC title.

All pointers indicate a fall down the standings in 2026. Game Grader had them 10th in the league last year, they benefitted from nation-best turnover luck, and none of their regular season wins were over teams with ACC winning records. Then their star quarterback and 1,000-yard receiver both went to South Beach and they did
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
In baseball they call it a “seeing-eye single” when a soft ground ball somehow slowly finds its way into the outfield. It appears harmless off the bat, but eventually finds its way.

That was the Duke football season. Duke committed five turnovers in the Illinois loss, botched three field goal attempts in the Tulane loss, lost to UConn, and then dropped two league games. They were 5-5 heading into their in-state rivalry games.

Three weeks later they were hoisting the ACC Championship trophy in Charlotte.

At several points throughout the season, this would have seemed impossible. Even aside from the five losses, there were moments within the wins where Duke survived by a thread. Down double-digits against NC State, Tre Freeman took a goal-line pick back 70 yards for an eventual 14-point swing. At Clemson, Duke went 5/5 on fourth downs and then Manny Diaz called for the game-winning two-point attempt in the final seconds to clinch Duke’s first win in Death Valley since 1980. Trailing UNC, Diaz called a gutsy fake field goal that made them 5/6 on fourth downs and set up the game-winning

touchdown. Another fake punt led to a score in the Wake Forest win.

And then by way of a wild five-way tiebreaker, Duke punched a ticket to the title game and earned a rematch with Virginia. They controlled time of possession, nailed yet another fake punt, and scored the game-winner on a fourth down in overtime.

Now that’s a seeing-eye Conference Title.

Diaz now has consecutive 9+ win seasons to start his Duke tenure, and clinched their first outright ACC title since 1962. They again swept UNC, Wake Forest, and NC State to mark back-to-back state titles.

The five losses were enough to keep Duke below two non-AQ conference champs so they did not earn an automatic bid the Playoff. But after a decade of Clemson’s Dabo Dynasty and the recent resurgence of Miami, an outright ACC title – no matter how they pulled it off -- makes this an all-time season for Duke.
pick_six_2026.offense:
It started last offseason when Duke made the financial commitment to sign a top quarterback from the transfer market. Tulane’s Darian Mensah came to Durham and proceeded to shatter the school’s single- season passing records for yards (3,973) and touchdowns (34). On fourth down in overtime, he sat patiently in the pocket before scrambling left to find Jeremiah Hasley for the ACC-clinching touchdown. Money well spent.

Duke was one of just five Power 4 offenses to feature a 3,000-yard passer, 1,000-yard rusher, and 1,000- yard receiver. And from that list they joined Ohio State as the only programs set to return their trio.

Instead, the same transfer portal that brought Mensah to Duke, took him away. The contract breach was battled in the courtrooms but eventually Mensah left for Miami and took his 1,000-yard receiver Cooper Barkate with him.

In total, Duke now has to replace their record-setting quarterback, top four receivers, and three starting offensive linemen including an All-American tackle.

The staff signed San Jose State starter Walker Eget who passed for 5,551 yards, 30 touchdowns, and 19 picks over his two seasons. In QB Rating, Eget placed 7th in the Mountain West both years. He’ll be challenged by redshirt freshman Dan Mahan who was a three-star recruit in the 2025 class.

Barkate and Que’Sean Brown (Virginia Tech) transferred out, four-year starter Sahmir Hagans graduated, and Andrel Anthony went pro. That’s nearly 3,000 receiving yards and 23 receiving touchdowns – and Hagan’s return abilities – all gone. It’s a complete rebuilt at receiver and the staff signed a pair of high three-star transfers in FCS All-American Jared Richardson (Penn) and All-AAC Javen Nicholas (Charlotte).

Three starting offensive linemen are gone including Brian Parker who started 33 games and left as an All- American. Left guard Jordan Larsen and center Matt Craycraft are returning starters, Bradley Smith started the bowl game at guard, and the open tackle spots will likely be the two transfers Braden Miller

(California) and Nick Del Grande (Coastal Carolina). The line ranked #50 in pass protection, #90 in OL Run Push, and it’s hard to project improvement after the talent drain this cycle.

Nate Sheppard posted Duke’s sixth-ever 1,000-yard rushing season and broke the freshman rushing records. He shared carries with Anderson Castle and they both rushed for 10+ touchdowns. Castle graduated, so Sheppard should get an increased workload and post another 1,000-yard season.

Jeremiah Hasley is the leading returning tight end in the ACC after catching 40 balls last year. Landen King graduated but the staff signed veteran Nate Kurisky (Louisville) who has caught seven touchdowns over three years.
pick_six_2026.defense:
As always, Diaz’s defense shows up on the stat sheet with a Top 25 ranking in my Negative Play rate which tracks how frequently they disrupt behind the line of scrimmage. Duke was #3 in 2024 and #19 last year.

The defense ranked below average in every other stat category including a bottom five -- #64 of 68 Power 4 – in my opponent-adjusted overall stat, and bottom ten marks in most passing categories.

How did a statistically poor defense win the ACC? Turnovers. Duke may have allowed a ton of yards but they grabbed 20 takeaways in league play. Together with the offense, Duke’s +17 turnover margin in league games was #1 nationally. The offense gave away almost all their turnovers in non-conference games that ultimately didn’t impact their path to Charlotte.

Like the offense, there’s plenty of roster turnover here and Duke must replace 9 of its top 14 tacklers, and all four All-ACC stars.

Their elite defensive ends Wesley Williams and Vincent Anthony head to the pros, and starting tackles Josiah Green and All-ACC Aaron Hall are both gone too.

End Tyshon Reed and tackle Preston Watson are the next men up, and the staff added a tackle pair from the transfer portal: Owen Wafle (Penn State) and Dakota Quinonez (Dartmouth).

Linebackers Jaiden Francois and Tre Freeman graduated, but Duke brings back their top playmaker Luke Mergott who had four takeaways in the final three games – two fumbles vs. Wake, and late interceptions to seal the ACC title and Sun Bowl wins. Former top recruit Bradley Gompers moves up in the rotation, and they get back Nick Morris, a 2023 starter who has had the past two seasons cut short with injuries.

The secondary loses All-ACC corner Chandler Rivers, and three safeties in 2025 starter Caleb Weaver, 2024 All- American Terry Moore (Ohio State) and Ma’Khi Jones (Florida State). Starting safety DaShawn Stone and corner Landan Callahan return, and two transfers join the starting lineup with Patrick Smith-Young (North Texas) and Che Ojarikre (Stanford) who had six starts last year.

pick_six_2026.outlook:
2026 marks a new chapter for Northwestern with the opening of the almost-billion-dollar Ryan Field. This latest financial boost upgraded the facilities and the coaching staff but hasn’t been reflected in roster talent acquisition yet.

Northwestern has to replace eight linemen – four offensive linemen and the full defensive line – and their future first-rounder was poached by Texas A&M. They signed zero four-star linemen and the trenches will hold them back in 2026.
pick_six_2026.recap_2025:
David Braun’s third season resembled parts of his first two. The streaky 2025 team had some surprising highs like his 2023 debut, but also some 2024-style offensive breakdowns and low-points.

It started with a four-interception game from new quarterback Preston Stone in the 20-point opening loss to Tulane. With a 1-2 record and star running back Cam Porter sidelined for the season, Braun worked his magic and Northwestern rattled off four straight wins with the old formula: run game and defense.

Their biggest moment was a 22-21 win at preseason favorite Penn State. Northwestern played perfect, mistake-free football, Caleb Komolafe punched in the game-winning score, and then the defense forced a final turnover on downs. This shocker was Northwestern’s biggest upset win since 1995 and was the final knockout punch for Penn State’s James Franklin.

A 19-0 shutout of Purdue got Northwestern to 5-2 overall – their best start since 2020 – and Braun praised his big offensive line and running back stable: “we know who we are… it starts with the running game and it’s built around that.”

The run game wasn’t enough against three of the league’s top recruiting programs and they lost to Nebraska, USC, and Michigan. Stone saved his best for November, and threw for 305 yards while rallying from a two-touchdown deficit to beat Minnesota and secure bowl eligibility.

A 7-6 season doesn’t pop off the page, but in the context of where Northwestern was, it was just enough of a positive finish to spark the transition to their new era.

Insurance mogul Pat Ryan continued his philanthropy to his alma mater, and this round was the biggest yet. This October, Northwestern is set to open the new Ryan Field, a state-of-the- art $865 million project that became the most expensive stadium in college football history. Paired with their iconic lakefront practice fieldhouse, Northwestern’s facility combo is tough to top.

Then they made an offensive coordinator to match. Northwestern hired Chip Kelly, one of the best offensive minds in football, in a move that Braun called “reflective of Northwestern’s long-

term commitment to the pursuit of championships – a program-defining change.”
pick_six_2026.offense:
Kelly built Oregon into a powerhouse with his hyper-tempo spread scheme, dual-threat quarterbacks, and pure speed at the skill positions. He then stacked three winning seasons at UCLA with consistent rushing attacks, and led the Ohio State offense to the 2024 national title.

This was a shocking win for a program that has been plagued by slow, unproductive offenses. The 2024 unit was one of the worst offenses in America, and while last year they made statistical gains in every category, the offense still remained below average – 57th of 68 Power 4 – in my opponent- adjusted metric.

Kelly added quarterbacks coach Jerry Neuheisel who led a three-game spark at UCLA as the interim playcaller last year. They will pick between a pair of experienced Power 4 starters in Aidan Chiles (Michigan State) and Nicco Marchiol (West Virginia). Chiles was a near-five star recruit back in 2023, started 20 games, but was eventually benched late last season.

Chiles has flashed a high ceiling, improved his decision-making with a 10-3 touchdown-to-pick ratio, and regardless of what happened with the benching, he still graded as a Top 15 transfer quarterback this cycle.

Both Chiles and Marchiol bring dual-threat skillsets that match Kelly’s scheme.

Komolafe stepped up after Porter was sidelined with another injury, and ended up with 941 yards, 11 touchdowns, and All-Big Ten honors. Backup Joseph Himon also returns, and the staff signed veteran Gavin Sawchuk who has rushed for 1,600 yards while starting at Oklahoma and Florida

State. Kelly’s most recent college offense featured a duo – TreVeyon Henderson and Quinshon Judkins – and he may share carries here too.

Griffin Wilde returns as the #1 receiver after posting the school’s best season in a decade (Austin Carr, 2016). His 71 catches, 880 yards, and 8 touchdowns earned third-team All-Big Ten honors. Hayden Eligon surged at the end of the season, with more than half of his season production coming in the final three games, and is a vertical threat to complement Wilde. Veterans Frank Covey and Ricky Ahumaraeze are joined by Top150 four-star Jaden McDuffie on the two-deep.

Hunter Welcing also earned all-league honors but went to Ohio State as a four-star transfer tight end. Northwestern signed in-line blocker 6’7 270-pounder Alex Honig (UConn) and a wildcard in Division II All-American Luke Dehnicke (Minnesota-Duluth).

Northwestern made stat gains in both my Offensive Line Push (from #133 to #71) and Pass Protection (from #60 to #27) and this was one of their best lines in recent memory. Four starters, including two of the three all-league performers, are gone and it is a full rebuild for Kelly disciple Tim Drevno. Ezomo Oratokhai is the lone returner and he can play both guard or center. They signed a proven starter in Grant Seagren (Oklahoma State) and a pair of unknowns in Arkel Anugwom (Alabama) and David Anchondo (DII Saginaw Valley). This is an uncertainty, though Kelly has never failed to produce an effective, productive run game.
pick_six_2026.defense:
Northwestern finished in the Top 25 in scoring defense, but due to their slow-tempo offense, that is a bit misleading from a per-play perspective. They allowed 5.7 yards/play (#80), 4.3 per carry (#73), and ranked #66 in Opponent QB Rating.

This side of the ball featured eight defenders with some form of All-Big Ten honors. Four return with three stars back in the secondary headlined by do-it-all safety Robert Fitzgerald. Top corner Josh Fussell is back along with Braden Turner. On returning production alone, this should be an above average Big Ten secondary.

But like the offensive line, it’s a full rebuild here in the trenches. Aidan Hubbard graduated after placing fifth on the school’s all-time career sacks leaderboard (20.5). The other star edge rusher Anto Saka transferred out to Texas A&M, and both starting defensive tackles Carmine Bastone and Najee Story are gone.
